title: Target protein arrives as a powder and goes on hold until QC
story:
Given an order of 2 vials of Target X (100 µg each, lyophilized, supplier lot A2210, catalog TX-H52H3).
When the box is opened at the bench, both vials are scanned or labeled, and the delivery is recorded with the CoA attached.
Then there are 2 containers of lot A2210, 200 µg in total, status "on hold, waiting for QC". They count as existing stock but not usable stock.
real_life_noise: the person receiving types 100 µL instead of 100 µg because every other field on the form is in µL
the CoA PDF is in the box but nobody scans it, so it lives in an email inbox
the vials are put in the -80 freezer before they are registered, and registration happens the next morning
the lot number on the vial is printed in 4 pt and gets typed as A221O (letter O instead of zero)
system_should: Create one lot record per supplier lot and one container per vial. New lots start on hold and are excluded from "usable" until a QC result releases them. Keep both the time the box arrived and the time it was recorded. Refuse a mass-only material entered with a volume unit, or at least warn.
question_it_answers: How much Target X do we have, and how much can we use right now?
cost_reason: Using an unchecked lot can waste a whole binding run; hiding it makes people reorder
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, error wrong_unit (µL for µg) p≈0.04, typo_lot_number p≈0.03, register_late (6 to 30 h after arrival) p≈0.25

title: Antigen goes through reconstitution, buffer exchange and QC and becomes a stock tube
story:
Given a vial of Target X, lot A2210, 100 µg powder, on hold.
When a scientist adds 200 µL of water as the CoA says (0.5 mg/mL), runs it through a 0.5 mL desalting spin column into the assay buffer, measures it at 0.41 mg/mL in 190 µL, and fills one stock tube.
Then the stock tube holds about 78 µg of lot A2210 in assay buffer. The 22 µg difference is recorded as process loss, not as missing material. The stock tube is linked to the vial it came from and to the buffer lot used.
real_life_noise: the scientist records the CoA concentration (0.5 mg/mL) instead of the measured one, so the tube shows 95 µg that don't exist
the vial is reconstituted in PBS instead of water because the CoA for a different product said so
buffer exchange is done but the buffer lot is not recorded
the stock tube gets the vial's original label, so two barcodes point to related but different material
the empty vial is thrown away but never marked as empty, so it still shows 100 µg of powder
system_should: Treat reconstitution plus buffer exchange as one task with an input (vial) and an output (stock tube). Keep the lot the same, record the measured concentration on the output, and store the gap between input and output as an explicit loss. Mark the input vial as used up. Link the buffer lot as a second input so a bad buffer can be traced later.
question_it_answers: How much target is really in that stock tube, and what buffer is it in?
cost_reason: Overstated target concentration goes straight into BLI plate prep and skews binding numbers
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action reconstitute_and_exchange, loss drawn from 10 to 30 percent of mass, error record_coa_value_not_measured p≈0.15, forget_buffer_lot p≈0.10, forget_empty_parent p≈0.20

title: QC passes and the lot becomes usable, QC fails and it is blocked but kept
story:
Given lot A2210 of Target X on hold, with one stock tube and one unopened vial.
When QC (concentration by A280 and a purity gel) passes, the lot is released. In a parallel case, lot B0918 of Target Y fails QC because the gel shows a second band at half the size.
Then every container of A2210 becomes usable at once, including the unopened vial. B0918 stays in the records with status "failed QC", its containers stay where they are until someone disposes of them, and it never counts as usable.
real_life_noise: QC is passed on the stock tube but the person forgets the unopened vial belongs to the same lot
someone deletes the failed lot to keep the list clean, and the supplier later asks for evidence for a refund
the failed vials are thrown out without recording it
system_should: Put QC status on the lot, not on each container, so one decision covers every vial and tube of that lot. Never delete a failed lot. Keep the QC result as a record with who, when, method and values.
question_it_answers: Which lots of Target Y can we use?
cost_reason: A failed lot used in a run spoils a customer result
sim_hook: Actor qc_scientist, action record_qc, outcome fail p≈0.08 per target lot, error delete_failed_lot p≈0.02, dispose_without_record p≈0.15

title: QC retest after a borderline first result
story:
Given lot C0412 of Target Z, measured at 0.31 mg/mL when the CoA says 0.50 mg/mL.
When the scientist suspects a blank error on the spectrophotometer, re-blanks, and measures again at 0.47 mg/mL, then passes the lot.
Then the lot has two QC results, the first marked as superseded by a retest, and the status is "passed" based on the second.
real_life_noise: the first result is edited in place to 0.47, so nobody can see there was ever a doubt
the retest is done on a different tube than the first test
three retests are run and only the best one is recorded
system_should: Keep every QC attempt as its own row. Let a later attempt explicitly supersede an earlier one, with a reason. The current status comes from the latest decision, but the history stays visible.
question_it_answers: Why was this lot released, and was there any doubt about it?
cost_reason: Hidden retests make it hard to explain an odd binding curve later
sim_hook: Actor qc_scientist, action record_qc, first_result_borderline p≈0.10, error overwrite_instead_of_retest p≈0.30, cherry_pick_retest p≈0.05

title: Measured concentration disagrees with the certificate
story:
Given lot A2210 whose CoA says 0.50 mg/mL after reconstitution and >95 percent purity.
When our own A280 reads 0.38 mg/mL (24 percent lower) on two separate measurements.
Then the lot keeps both numbers: the supplier's claim and our measurement. Planning uses ours. The lot is flagged so someone decides whether 24 percent is inside tolerance (Assumption: the lab has a tolerance, we guess ±20 percent).
real_life_noise: the extinction coefficient used for A280 is the default 1.0 instead of the protein's real value, so our number is the one that is wrong
the CoA reports concentration by BCA, we measure by A280, so the two methods differ by design
the scientist overwrites the CoA value with ours and the supplier's claim is lost
system_should: Store supplier claims and our measurements as separate facts, each with the method used. Never overwrite one with the other. Compute usable mass from our measurement when we have one, and say which number was used.
question_it_answers: How much target do we really have, and does it match what we paid for?
cost_reason: Wrong concentration silently shifts every BLI result that used this target
sim_hook: Actor qc_scientist, action measure_concentration, true_vs_coa ratio drawn from N(0.9, 0.12), error wrong_extinction_coefficient p≈0.05, overwrite_coa_value p≈0.20

title: Twist DNA plate arrives dried, with a plate map file
story:
Given an order of 96 gene fragments from Twist for customer project P-031.
When a 96-well plate arrives at room temperature with DNA dried in each well (Twist says 100 ng to 1 µg per fragment) and the plate map CSV is downloaded from the Twist portal.
Then the plate is one container with 96 wells, each well holding its own DNA material linked to its design name and sequence from the map, with yield in ng. The plate is on hold until reconstituted.
real_life_noise: the CSV is uploaded but its plate barcode column doesn't match the physical plate's barcode because Twist sent two plates in the box
Excel turns construct names like MARCH1 or SEPT9 into dates when someone opens and re-saves the map
names in the map have trailing spaces, so they don't match the designs in our records
the plate is put in the -20 freezer before anyone imports the map, and sits there "unknown" for a week
system_should: Import the plate map as data, matched to the plate barcode, and reject or flag rows whose barcode or well doesn't match. Create one lot per well (each well is a different DNA). Keep the original file attached. Treat a plate with no imported map as a known container with unknown contents, not as nothing.
question_it_answers: Which DNA is in well C7 of this plate, and where did it come from?
cost_reason: A swapped map means every expressed protein is labeled with the wrong sequence
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action import_plate_map, error wrong_map_for_plate p≈0.03, excel_date_mangling p≈0.02 per plate, delay_import (1 to 7 days) p≈0.15

title: 384-well Twist plate with some wells missing
story:
Given an order of 380 fragments.
When a 384-well plate arrives and the map shows 372 wells filled, 4 wells empty by design and 8 constructs marked as failed synthesis, to follow later.
Then 372 wells hold DNA lots. The 8 failed constructs are still open on the order, not in stock. The 4 empty wells are empty, not "zero ng of something".
real_life_noise: someone creates 384 well records from a template, so 12 wells show DNA that isn't there
the 8 late constructs arrive 3 weeks later in tubes, not in the plate, and get registered as a new plate
a well with 40 ng (below what the expression step needs) is treated the same as one with 900 ng
system_should: Only create well contents for wells that the map says have DNA. Let an order line stay open after delivery. Record per-well yield so low-yield wells can be flagged before expression.
question_it_answers: Which constructs for project P-031 do we actually have?
cost_reason: Phantom wells get expressed and give empty results that look like non-binders
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action import_plate_map, synth_failure p≈0.02 per construct, error template_fill_all_wells p≈0.05, low_yield (<100 ng) p≈0.03 per well

title: Plate map applied rotated 180 degrees
story:
Given a dried Twist plate registered with its map.
When the reconstitution robot loads the plate the other way round (A1 where H12 should be) and nobody notices until expression shows GFP signal in the wrong pattern.
Then the system cannot know the physical truth by itself, but the lab can record a correction that remaps every well, and everything made from the plate is updated through lineage.
real_life_noise: only some downstream plates get corrected
the correction is done by editing well contents in place, so the earlier wrong record disappears
system_should: Allow a correction event on a plate that remaps wells, kept as a new entry, not an edit. Make it easy to find every plate made from the corrected one so they can be corrected or flagged too.
question_it_answers: What did the record say before the correction, and which results used the wrong map?
cost_reason: Every sample on the plate is attributed to the wrong sequence
sim_hook: Actor robot, action load_plate, error rotated_180 p≈0.002 per load, detected_downstream p≈0.7

title: Dried DNA plate is reconstituted by a liquid handler
story:
Given a dried 96-well Twist plate with per-well yields from the map.
When the robot adds 20 µL of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 to every well (Twist advises TE or Tris, not water).
Then each well now has 20 µL, with concentration computed from its yield (for example 500 ng in 20 µL is 25 ng/µL). The plate becomes the "reconstituted Twist plate" of the workflow and its storage rules change from dried to liquid.
real_life_noise: the robot run aborts after column 8, so columns 9 to 12 are still dry but the whole plate is logged as reconstituted
the plate is not spun down first and some DNA pellet sits on the seal
a scientist uses water because the TE bottle is empty
the robot log says 20 µL but the tip for row H was clogged
system_should: Record reconstitution per well, ideally from the robot's own log file, not as one plate-level action. A well's state (dry or liquid) is part of what it is. Flag wells where the robot reported an error.
question_it_answers: Which wells on this plate are ready to use?
cost_reason: Dry wells give no expression and get re-ordered at Twist prices
sim_hook: Actor robot, action reconstitute_plate, error partial_run_abort p≈0.01, clogged_channel p≈0.005 per channel per run, wrong_diluent p≈0.02

title: Partial delivery of a target order
story:
Given an order of 5 vials of Target X.
When 3 vials of lot A2210 arrive this week and 2 vials of a different lot, A2301, arrive 12 days later.
Then the order shows 3 of 5 received, then 5 of 5. There are two lots, each needing its own QC.
real_life_noise: the receiver marks the order complete on the first box
the second box is assumed to be the same lot and is added to A2210 without checking the label
the packing slip for the second box lists all 5 vials, so it gets registered as 5
system_should: Track received quantity per order line, separate from the lot. Make a new lot whenever the lot number differs. Warn when received quantity would exceed ordered quantity.
question_it_answers: Is the target order complete, and which lots are waiting for QC?
cost_reason: An unchecked second lot gets used under the first lot's QC pass
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, partial_shipment p≈0.10 per order, error merge_into_existing_lot p≈0.10, register_packing_slip_qty p≈0.05

title: Same delivery registered twice
story:
Given a box with 4 vials of Target Y, lot B1102.
When one person registers it at the door from the packing slip, and a second person registers it again when unpacking at the freezer, scanning each vial.
Then the system should end up with 4 containers, not 8, and the double entry should be visible as a correction.
real_life_noise: the first registration has no vial barcodes, only "4 × 50 µg", so the duplicates don't collide on barcode
the second person sees the first entry, thinks it is wrong, and edits it instead of cancelling
nobody notices for 3 weeks, and by then someone has consumed from one of the ghost containers
system_should: Warn when a new receipt has the same supplier, catalog number, lot and order line as a recent one. Let a receipt be cancelled with a reason, which reverses its containers. If a ghost container has already been "used", keep that usage visible and move it onto the real container.
question_it_answers: How much Target Y do we really have?
cost_reason: Phantom stock delays a reorder until a run fails for lack of target
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, error duplicate_receipt p≈0.03 per delivery, detected_within_1_day p≈0.6

title: Wrong item shipped
story:
Given an order of human Target X with a C-terminal His tag, biotinylated.
When the vial label says the right catalog number but the CoA says "mouse", or the vial is the non-biotinylated version.
Then the lot is registered as what actually arrived (if known) and put on hold with reason "wrong item", linked to the order line, which stays open.
real_life_noise: the receiver checks only the catalog number on the box, not the vial
it is spotted only after reconstitution and two aliquots have been made
the supplier ships the replacement and asks to keep the wrong vial, so it stays in the freezer as an orphan
system_should: Record what arrived, not what was ordered. Keep the order line separate from the lot. A hold reason should be specific. Holding a lot should hold everything made from it.
question_it_answers: Why is the Target X order still open when we have a Target X vial?
cost_reason: A non-biotinylated target gives no signal on streptavidin sensors, and the run looks like all non-binders
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action ship, error wrong_variant p≈0.01 per order, detected_at_receipt p≈0.5, detected_after_aliquoting p≈0.4

title: Lot on hold because the certificate is missing
story:
Given a delivery of HEPES powder, 500 g, lot SLCD1234.
When the box has no CoA and the supplier website hasn't posted it yet.
Then the lot is registered and on hold with reason "no CoA". When the PDF is attached 2 days later, the hold is lifted (Assumption: the lab requires a CoA for buffer components; it may not).
real_life_noise: the CoA attached is for lot SLCD1243
someone lifts the hold without attaching anything because they need the buffer today
system_should: Let a lot carry documents, each with the lot number read from it. Warn when a document's lot doesn't match. Lifting a hold is an event with a person and a reason.
question_it_answers: Why can't I use this HEPES?
cost_reason: Mostly paperwork, but matters when a recall comes
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action attach_coa, missing_at_arrival p≈0.15, error coa_for_other_lot p≈0.03, lift_hold_without_doc p≈0.10

title: Cold chain broken on arrival
story:
Given an order of Target Y shipped as a frozen liquid on dry ice.
When the box arrives on a Monday after sitting at the courier since Friday, there is no dry ice left, and the data logger shows above -20 °C for about 30 hours.
Then the lot is registered, with the shipping condition recorded, and put on hold with reason "cold chain". The scientist decides: use after extra QC, or reject and claim a replacement.
real_life_noise: the vials are moved straight into the -80 so it "looks" fine, and nobody writes down that the ice was gone
there is no logger, only "box felt cold"
the lyophilized vials in the same box are fine but get rejected with the liquid ones
system_should: Record arrival condition per receipt (temperature, ice present, logger reading) as a fact. A hold for cold chain applies to the containers in that shipment, not to every container of the lot ever received.
question_it_answers: Can we trust the Target Y that arrived on Monday?
cost_reason: Thawed target can aggregate and give false binding
sim_hook: Actor courier, action deliver, delay_over_weekend p≈0.05, ice_depleted given delay p≈0.5, error not_recorded p≈0.4

title: Supplier recalls a lot
story:
Given lot P7781 of 10x PBS, used to make 6 batches of assay buffer over 2 months, which went into 14 BLI plates.
When the supplier emails that P7781 has an endotoxin or pH problem and asks customers to stop using it.
Then the lot goes on hold with reason "supplier recall", and the system lists every buffer batch, plate and run that used it, and every container that still holds some of it.
real_life_noise: two bottles of P7781 were registered under a typo, P7718, and are missed by the search
one buffer batch was made without recording which PBS bottle was used
the recall email arrives months later, after most containers are thrown away
system_should: Hold a lot with one action and pass the hold to everything made from it that still exists. Answer "where did it go" through the lineage, including disposed containers. Show buffer batches with an unknown component lot as a gap, not as clean.
question_it_answers: Which experiments touched the recalled PBS lot?
cost_reason: Customer results may need to be re-run or flagged
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action recall_lot, p≈0.002 per lot per month, error component_lot_unrecorded p≈0.05 per buffer batch

title: The same supplier lot number appears again years later
story:
Given a lot "1234" of a buffer component received in 2023 and used up.
When in 2026 the same supplier sends the same catalog number with lot "1234" again (some suppliers reuse short lot codes or restart counters).
Then the system must not merge the 2026 delivery into the 2023 lot. They have different expiry dates and different CoAs.
real_life_noise: the receiver picks "1234" from a dropdown of existing lots and it attaches to the old, expired lot
the old lot's QC pass is carried over silently
system_should: Do not use supplier, catalog and lot number as a unique key on its own. Every receipt makes or links to a lot by explicit choice, and a match to a lot with a very different expiry or a receipt date years apart triggers a warning.
question_it_answers: Is this lot 1234 the one that passed QC?
cost_reason: Inherits the wrong expiry and QC status
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action assign_lot_number, reuse_old_code p≈0.005 per lot, error pick_existing_lot_from_dropdown p≈0.5 given reuse

title: Two suppliers, same lot string
story:
Given lot "220315" of NaCl from supplier A and lot "220315" of a target protein from supplier B (both date-style codes).
When someone searches for lot 220315.
Then both come up, clearly from different suppliers. A recall of one never touches the other.
real_life_noise: the receiver leaves the supplier field empty because the box came via a distributor
the distributor's own lot number is typed instead of the manufacturer's
system_should: A lot belongs to a supplier and a catalog item. Record the manufacturer and the distributor separately when they differ. Lot number alone is just a label.
question_it_answers: Which lot 220315 is this?
cost_reason: A recall or QC fail lands on the wrong material
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, error missing_supplier p≈0.03, distributor_lot_instead_of_manufacturer p≈0.05

title: Same material from two suppliers
story:
Given Target X bought from supplier A (lot A2210) and the same human protein from supplier B (lot S-88), each with a different tag and buffer.
When a scientist asks how much Target X we have.
Then the answer can be given per supplier and in total, but the two are not silently treated as interchangeable. For PBS from two suppliers, they usually are.
real_life_noise: supplier B's product is registered as a new material "Target X (B)", so the total never shows up
an experiment uses half lot A and half lot B in one plate and records only one
system_should: Keep one material ("human Target X") with lots from several suppliers, plus product-level facts (tag, construct, biotinylated or not). Let the material type decide whether lots can be mixed (buffers yes, targets only with a note). Record every lot a plate actually used.
question_it_answers: How much Target X do we have, from whom, and can we swap one for the other?
cost_reason: Hidden duplicates cause needless reorders; mixing hides a source of variance
sim_hook: Actor purchaser, action order_from_alternate_supplier p≈0.15 per target order, error new_material_instead_of_new_lot p≈0.3

title: Supplier vial has no barcode we can use
story:
Given 3 vials of Target Z with printed labels but no barcode, or a barcode format our scanners don't read.
When the receiver prints 3 lab barcode labels and sticks one on each vial.
Then each vial is a container with our barcode, and the supplier's label text (catalog, lot) is recorded as data on the lot.
real_life_noise: two identical vials are on the bench and labels A and B get swapped. Harmless here (same lot), harmful when two different lots sit together
labels are printed but one falls off in the -80 and is found loose in the box
the receiver prints 4 labels for 3 vials and the 4th is stuck on the box, which then gets registered as a container
system_should: Let containers get barcodes at registration time, and let a barcode be printed before it is assigned. A barcode that was printed but never assigned should show up as unused, not as a container.
question_it_answers: Which vial is this?
cost_reason: Swapped labels between lots break traceability
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action label_container, error swap_labels_same_bench p≈0.01 per pair, label_falls_off_in_freezer p≈0.005 per month, extra_label_registered p≈0.02

title: Relabeling a container whose barcode can't be read
story:
Given a stock tube with barcode T-004112 whose label is frosted over and won't scan.
When a scientist sticks a new label T-009877 on it.
Then the container stays the same container, now known by T-009877. Scanning T-004112 (on an old printout) points to the same tube with a note that it was relabeled.
real_life_noise: the scientist registers the tube as a new container with the new barcode and the old record stays with full volume
the new label is put on over the old one, so a scanner sometimes reads the old one through it
system_should: Treat barcodes as names a container has over time, not as the container itself. Relabeling is an event. Never create a new container by relabeling.
question_it_answers: Is T-009877 the same tube as T-004112?
cost_reason: Ghost duplicates double-count expensive target
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action relabel_container, trigger label_unreadable p≈0.02 per container per year in -80, error register_as_new p≈0.3

title: Twist plate barcode can't be read by the robot
story:
Given a Twist plate with its own side barcode.
When the plate reader on the liquid handler misreads one digit, so the robot logs work against an unknown plate.
Then the robot's log should not create a new plate. The run is flagged as "unknown input plate" until someone matches it.
real_life_noise: the tech scans it by hand and types the barcode, adding a digit
our own barcode label is stuck over the Twist barcode on the wrong side, so the robot reads the Twist one and the person reads ours
system_should: Allow one container to have several barcodes (supplier's and ours). Robot logs that reference an unknown barcode are parked, not turned into new containers.
question_it_answers: Which plate did the robot actually use?
cost_reason: Lineage breaks between DNA and the protein made from it
sim_hook: Actor robot, action scan_plate, error misread p≈0.003 per scan, two_barcodes_conflict p≈0.01

title: DNA made in-house instead of ordered
story:
Given a construct that is also on order from Twist, but needed in 2 days instead of 5 to 10.
When the lab makes the DNA in-house (Assumption: by PCR or similar from a template, details not in the brief) into a 96-well plate.
Then the wells hold DNA lots whose source is "made", linked to the inputs (template, reagents), with the same design names as the Twist order. When the Twist plate arrives later, both exist and the system can tell them apart.
real_life_noise: in-house DNA is registered as if it were the Twist plate, so the Twist plate later arrives and has nowhere to go
the Twist order is not cancelled, so we pay for both
in-house wells have no measured concentration
system_should: The same material (a DNA design) can have lots from a supplier or from an in-house task. The lot's source is always clear. Show both sources when someone asks "do we have DNA for design D-118?".
question_it_answers: Do we already have this DNA, from anywhere?
cost_reason: Duplicate orders at Twist prices
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_dna_in_house p≈0.3 of urgent projects, error register_as_supplier_lot p≈0.05, forget_cancel_order p≈0.2

title: Target expressed in-house instead of bought
story:
Given a target that is hard to buy.
When the lab expresses and purifies it in-house, ending with 1.2 mL at 0.8 mg/mL.
Then a new target lot exists with source "made", linked to its DNA, and it goes through the same hold and QC as a bought lot.
real_life_noise: in-house lots skip QC because "we made it ourselves"
the lot gets a name like "TgtX_prep2" that collides with a supplier lot naming style
system_should: Apply the same hold-until-QC rule to made targets. Give made lots our own IDs so they never collide with supplier lot numbers.
question_it_answers: Has this in-house target been checked?
cost_reason: Unchecked targets corrupt binding data
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action purify_target, error skip_qc p≈0.2

title: Buffer component arrives
story:
Given an order of 1 L of 10x PBS and 500 mL of Tween-20.
When the bottles arrive with expiry dates 2028-03 and 2027-11.
Then each bottle is a container of its lot. Usable amount is the full bottle. Expiry comes from the label (Assumption: some components get a shorter expiry once opened, which the lab sets per material).
real_life_noise: the receiver enters the expiry as 03/2028 and it is read as 3 February
the bottle is opened and the open date is never recorded
4 identical bottles are registered as one container of 4 L
system_should: Store expiry as a date with the supplier's precision (month only is common). Allow an "opened" event that can start a shorter clock. Prefer one container per bottle so each can be tracked and thrown away.
question_it_answers: Do we have PBS that's in date?
cost_reason: Cheap, but buffers made from expired components carry the problem forward
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, error date_format_swap p≈0.03, bulk_as_one_container p≈0.2, forget_open_date p≈0.5

title: Consumables arrive in boxes and cases
story:
Given an order of 1 case of 96-well plates (50 plates) and 10 racks of 200 µL tips.
When they arrive.
Then the system records counts (50 plates, 10 racks) at the level the lab cares about, not each tip. There is no QC hold and no expiry.
real_life_noise: half a case is taken to the robot room and nobody records the move
the same plate model is ordered from 2 suppliers and registered as two items
plates are counted as 1 (the case) instead of 50
system_should: Let a material type say whether it needs QC, has expiry, and how it is counted. Consumables are counted in units, not volume.
question_it_answers: Do we have enough 384-well plates for next week?
cost_reason: Running out stops the robot for a day
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_consumables, error count_case_as_one p≈0.1

title: BLI biosensors arrive, a consumable that does expire
story:
Given an order of streptavidin biosensors (for example a tray of 96 tips for an Octet-style instrument).
When they arrive with a lot number and an expiry date 11 months out.
Then they are registered with lot and expiry even though the brief lists consumables as "no expiry".
real_life_noise: sensors from an older lot are used first and a data review later finds a shift between lots
expiry is not entered because consumables "don't expire"
system_should: Expiry and lot tracking are per material type, not per category. Some consumables need both, and it should be cheap to switch on.
question_it_answers: Which sensor lot did this BLI run use?
cost_reason: Expired or odd sensor lots give poor data that has to be re-run
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_consumables, error skip_expiry_for_consumable p≈0.4

title: Customer sends their own material
story:
Given a customer who ships their own target protein or their own DNA (Assumption: the brief says samples are sometimes bought as finished protein, and we assume customers can also send material).
When a tube arrives with a handwritten label and no CoA.
Then the lot's source is the customer, it is owned by that customer's project, and it is on hold until we QC it.
real_life_noise: concentration is only in the customer's email, not on the tube
the tube is used for another project because it sits next to our own Target X
system_should: Let a lot have an owner or restriction (only for project P-031). Warn when restricted material is used elsewhere.
question_it_answers: Whose material is this, and may we use it?
cost_reason: Using a customer's material for someone else is a trust problem
sim_hook: Actor customer, action ship_material, error no_concentration p≈0.3, used_for_other_project p≈0.01

title: Finished sample proteins bought in a plate
story:
Given a project where samples are bought as finished protein (the brief says this happens sometimes).
When a 96-well plate of 80 purified proteins arrives frozen with a spreadsheet of names and concentrations.
Then the plate is registered with 80 well-level sample lots, linked to the project, skipping the DNA and expression path.
real_life_noise: the spreadsheet has 82 rows, two of them duplicates
the plate thaws on the bench for 2 hours waiting for the spreadsheet
system_should: Sample lots can start from a supplier, not only from expression. The same plate-map import as for DNA plates applies.
question_it_answers: Which samples on this plate came from where?
cost_reason: Lost lineage on a customer's paid samples
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action import_plate_map, error duplicate_rows p≈0.05

title: Packing slip, label and CoA disagree on amount
story:
Given a vial whose packing slip says 100 µg, whose label says 50 µg and whose CoA says 50 µg.
When the receiver registers it.
Then the amount comes from the vial or the CoA, not from the packing slip, and the mismatch is noted for the purchaser.
real_life_noise: the receiver uses the slip because it's on top
a "2 × 50 µg" pack is entered as one vial of 100 µg
system_should: Record the source of every quantity. A pack of several vials is several containers.
question_it_answers: How much did we actually get?
cost_reason: Overstated stock means a run runs short
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, slip_mismatch p≈0.03, error pack_as_single_container p≈0.1

title: Lot arrives close to or past its expiry
story:
Given an order of Target Y.
When the lot arrives with an expiry 3 weeks away, or a powder whose "use by" passed last month.
Then the lot is registered with its real expiry and the short or past date is flagged on arrival, not on the day it's needed.
real_life_noise: expiry left blank because the vial label only has a manufacturing date
after reconstitution the expiry of the liquid is shorter than the powder's, but the powder's is kept
system_should: Warn at receipt when expiry is less than some lab-set margin away. When the material changes form (powder to liquid), its expiry is recomputed from the new form's rule.
question_it_answers: What expires soon?
cost_reason: Short-dated targets get used up or wasted without notice
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action ship, short_dated p≈0.03, error keep_powder_expiry_after_reconstitution p≈0.3

title: Supplier extends a lot's expiry with a new certificate
story:
Given lot A2210 with expiry 2026-12-31.
When the supplier sends an updated CoA after stability testing, with expiry 2027-12-31.
Then the lot gets a new expiry, recorded as a change with the document as the reason, and the old expiry remains in history.
real_life_noise: only the containers in one freezer get updated
the new CoA is for a different product lot
system_should: Expiry from the supplier is a lot fact that can change over time with a source. Container expiry is computed from the lot plus storage rules, not typed per tube.
question_it_answers: Why did this tube's expiry change?
cost_reason: Good material thrown out, or a change with no paper trail
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action reissue_coa, p≈0.01 per lot per year

title: Material used before QC
story:
Given lot A2301 of Target X on hold, and a run due tomorrow.
When a scientist makes a BLI target plate from it anyway, then QC fails two days later.
Then the plate and the run are recorded as they happened, and the run is flagged "used material that later failed QC".
real_life_noise: the scientist records the plate as made from the released lot A2210 to avoid a warning
QC passes later and the warning is never cleared
system_should: Never block recording what physically happened. Warn at the time, and keep a link so a later QC result can flag or clear the affected runs.
question_it_answers: Which runs used a target lot before it was checked?
cost_reason: Bad data reaches a customer
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_target_plate, use_on_hold_lot p≈0.05 under time pressure, error record_wrong_lot_to_avoid_warning p≈0.2 given use

title: Failed lot replaced by the supplier
story:
Given lot B0918 that failed QC.
When the supplier sends replacement lot B1002 free of charge and asks that B0918 be destroyed.
Then B1002 is a new receipt on the same order line marked "replacement", and B0918 containers are disposed of with reason "destroyed per supplier".
real_life_noise: the replacement is registered as a new order, so spend numbers double
B0918 vials stay in the freezer because nobody wants to throw out expensive protein
system_should: A receipt can be a replacement for a failed lot. Disposal is an event that keeps the record.
question_it_answers: Did we get a replacement for the failed target?
cost_reason: Failed vials come back into use by mistake
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action ship_replacement p≈0.7 given qc_fail, error keep_failed_vials p≈0.3

title: More vials of an already-checked lot arrive months later
story:
Given lot A2210, QC passed in March.
When in September 2 more vials of A2210 arrive.
Then the vials join the existing lot and inherit its QC status, but they get their own shipment record with its own arrival condition. (Assumption: the lab accepts a past QC for the same supplier lot. A stricter lab would re-check.)
real_life_noise: the new vials arrived warm but are released because the lot passed QC
the receiver creates a new lot A2210 because the old one is "used up"
system_should: Separate lot (made by the supplier, QC'd once) from receipt (shipped to us, checked for transit damage). A receipt hold can block containers from one receipt while the lot stays released.
question_it_answers: Can I use the new A2210 vials?
cost_reason: Damaged vials pass under an old QC result
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, same_lot_repeat p≈0.15 per target order, error duplicate_lot_record p≈0.2

title: Twist plate arrives with a lifted seal
story:
Given a dried 96-well Twist plate.
When the foil seal is partly lifted over wells A1 to A4.
Then the plate is registered and those four wells are put on hold for possible cross-contamination, while the other 92 wells are fine.
real_life_noise: the whole plate is rejected and re-ordered
the note "seal lifted" goes in a chat message, not on the plate
system_should: Allow holds per well, not only per container or per lot.
question_it_answers: Which wells on this plate can I trust?
cost_reason: Cross-contaminated DNA gives a mixed protein
sim_hook: Actor courier, action deliver, seal_damage p≈0.01 per plate

title: Registered late, used before registered
story:
Given a box of Target Z that arrived Tuesday and was put in the freezer unregistered.
When on Wednesday a scientist splits one vial into 5 aliquots, and on Thursday the receiver registers the box.
Then the system ends up with the correct state. The split happened Wednesday, the arrival Tuesday, and the records were entered Thursday. Late entries are allowed with their real times.
real_life_noise: the Wednesday split is entered against a placeholder container "unknown target"
the arrival is entered with Thursday's date, so the split appears to happen before the material arrived
system_should: Every event has a time it happened and a time it was recorded. Allow back-dated events and check that the order still makes sense.
question_it_answers: When did this arrive, and when did we know?
cost_reason: Audit history looks impossible and erodes trust
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action receive_lot, register_late p≈0.25, consumed_before_registered p≈0.05

title: Antigen aliquoted after QC into single-use tubes
story:
Given a released stock tube of Target X, 190 µL at 0.41 mg/mL.
When it is split into 9 tubes of 20 µL for -80 storage (the supplier advises single-use aliquots and warns against aliquots below the minimum size on the CoA).
Then 9 tubes of lot A2210, each 8.2 µg, all released, and 10 µL left or lost.
real_life_noise: aliquots of 5 µL are made, below the CoA minimum, and lose activity
two tubes are not scanned
system_should: Children inherit lot and QC status. Let a material carry a minimum aliquot size and warn when it is broken.
question_it_answers: How many usable aliquots of Target X are left?
cost_reason: Too-small aliquots waste expensive target
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action split_tube, error below_min_aliquot p≈0.05, forget_scan p≈0.03 per child

title: The supplier's lot is ours after all
story:
Given a lot from a supplier who is also the in-house team (a buffer made by the lab next door, or a colleague's target).
When it is handed over with a hand-written label.
Then the lot is registered with source "internal", which is neither "bought" nor "made by us here".
real_life_noise: no lot number at all, so the receiver invents "TgtX_from_Anna"
system_should: Keep the source a reference to who supplied it. Allow lots without a supplier lot number but give them our own ID.
question_it_answers: Where did this tube come from?
cost_reason: Hard to trace later
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action hand_over_material p≈0.02 per week

title: Receiving form filled in from memory at the end of the day
story:
Given 6 deliveries in one day.
When the receiver registers all of them at 18:00 from memory and packing slips.
Then quantities and lots may be right, but storage locations are guesses. The system records what was entered with the time, and later scans in freezers correct the locations.
real_life_noise: two boxes' freezer locations are swapped
one delivery is missed and only found weeks later in a freezer scan
system_should: Treat location as something that later scans can correct, with the correction kept in history. A container found in a freezer with an unknown barcode should be a finding, not an error.
question_it_answers: Where is the Target Y that arrived this morning?
cost_reason: Lost tubes get reordered
sim_hook: Actor lab_tech, action batch_register, p≈0.3 of days, error swap_locations p≈0.05, miss_delivery p≈0.02

title: Supplier changes the product without changing the catalog number
story:
Given Target X bought for two years from the same catalog number.
When the new lot's CoA shows a different formulation (buffer with trehalose instead of without, or a different tag position).
Then the lot records the formulation and product facts from its own CoA, and a comparison with earlier lots shows the change.
real_life_noise: nobody reads the new CoA because "it's the same product"
system_should: Keep product facts that can vary per lot on the lot, not only on the catalog item.
question_it_answers: Did anything change between lots of Target X?
cost_reason: Explains a shift in binding data across months
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action change_formulation p≈0.01 per lot

title: Scientist splits a target stock tube into single-use aliquots
story:
Given a 400 µL tube of Target X at 1.0 mg/mL (lot T-0412, QC passed) in freezer F2.
When a scientist thaws it, splits it into 15 tubes of 25 µL, scans each new barcode, and puts the box back in F2.
Then there are 15 tubes of lot T-0412 with 375 µL in total, the parent shows 25 µL left (or is marked empty and thrown away), and the parent counts one freeze-thaw.
real_life_noise: scans 14 of the 15 new tubes, the 15th sits in the box with a barcode the system has never seen
types 30 µL per tube because that was the plan, so children add up to 450 µL from a 400 µL parent
pipette set to 25 µL but real delivery is 24 to 26 µL, so the last tube gets 18 µL
writes the split on paper and enters it two days later, after one aliquot is already used
throws the parent away with 25 µL in it and never records the disposal
system_should: Keep the lot the same on every child and copy the freeze-thaw count and QC status down. Refuse or flag a split where children plus leftover exceed what the parent had. Keep the time of the split separate from the time it was typed. A barcode that shows up later should be attachable to the split as a late child, not created as a new lot.
question_it_answers: How many single-use tubes of Target X do we have, and how many times has each been thawed?
cost_reason: Target is expensive and shared; a lost aliquot leads to a needless reorder
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action split_tube(n=10..24, vol=20..50 µL). Errors: forget_scan per child p≈0.03, record_planned_not_actual volume p≈0.10, late_entry (1 to 72 h) p≈0.15, unrecorded_parent_disposal p≈0.05.

title: Scientist pipettes by hand from a tube into a few wells of a plate
story:
Given a 50 mL bottle of HBS-EP buffer lot B-221 and an empty 96-well plate P-77.
When a scientist pipettes 50 µL into wells A1 to A12 by hand.
Then A1 to A12 each hold 50 µL of B-221 and the bottle goes down by 600 µL.
real_life_noise: records the transfer against the tube that was scanned first, not the one actually used
uses a reservoir trough poured from a 50 mL bottle and never records the trough at all
pipettes into row B instead of row A
records the whole row as one transfer, the system needs twelve wells
system_should: Let a person record one action that covers a set of wells ("A1 to A12, 50 µL each") and expand it into well-level entries. Reject or flag a transfer that would push the source below zero, and show which source was likely meant. Allow an intermediate trough as a short-lived container, or allow the bottle to be the source directly.
question_it_answers: Where did the buffer in this well come from?
cost_reason: Buffer is cheap, but a wrong source breaks lineage when a buffer lot goes bad
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action manual_transfer(src, dest_wells, vol). Errors: wrong_source_scan p≈0.02, wrong_row_offset p≈0.01, skip_intermediate_container p≈0.30.

title: Pipetting more than the source holds
story:
Given a tube of Target X that the system thinks holds 25 µL.
When a task records taking 30 µL from it.
Then the transfer is saved but flagged, because either the earlier record was wrong or this one is.
real_life_noise: the tube really had 32 µL because an earlier split over-recorded loss
the scientist typed 30 instead of 3.0
two people took from the same tube in parallel and both recorded against 25 µL
system_should: Never silently clamp to zero and never block the bench (the liquid already moved). Save the fact as it was reported, mark the container's balance as negative or uncertain, and put it on a list for someone to reconcile with a recount entry.
question_it_answers: Which containers have balances we cannot trust?
cost_reason: Planning reads these numbers; a hidden negative balance means an experiment is planned on air
sim_hook: Actor scientist or robot, action any_transfer. Error over_draw where vol > recorded balance, p≈0.02 per manual transfer; decimal_slip (×10) p≈0.005.

title: Last few microlitres can't be pipetted out (dead volume)
story:
Given a 1.5 mL tube with 6 µL of Target X left.
When a scientist tries to take 10 µL and can only get 4 µL.
Then the tube shows 2 µL, which counts as existing but not usable, and the 4 µL is recorded as moved.
real_life_noise: records 10 µL anyway because that was the plan
writes off the tube as empty and throws it away while the system still shows 6 µL
the "dead volume" is different per container type (about 2 µL in a PCR tube, 5 to 10 µL in a 1.5 mL tube, 10 to 20 µL per well in an Echo source plate)
system_should: Store dead volume on the container type, and report usable volume as total minus dead volume. Accept a "tube is empty" event that writes off whatever is left as a loss, with a reason.
question_it_answers: How much of what we hold can actually be used?
cost_reason: Overstated usable stock means a planned run fails at the bench
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action transfer with request > usable. Behaviour: record_requested_not_actual p≈0.25; mark_empty_discard p≈0.6 when balance < 2× dead volume.

title: Transfer recorded against the wrong source plate
story:
Given two DNA plates on the bench, D-1001 and D-1002, same layout, different customers.
When the robot actually aspirates from D-1002 but the scientist scanned D-1001 into the run.
Then the record says D-1001 lost material and the expression plate came from D-1001, both wrong.
real_life_noise: found out a week later when the BLI results for customer A look like customer B's
the scientist corrects it by editing the source on the run, so the original claim disappears
only half the wells came from the wrong plate because the plates were swapped mid-run
system_should: Let someone correct a run's source by adding a correction that reverses the old entries and adds new ones, keeping both visible. After correction, lineage from the expression plate must point at D-1002 and both DNA plates' balances must be right.
question_it_answers: Which DNA plate did this protein really come from, and what did the record say before the fix?
cost_reason: Wrong customer data delivered, and the audit trail is the only way to prove what happened
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action start_robot_run. Error wrong_source_scan p≈0.005 per run when two same-layout plates are on deck; detection delay 1 to 10 days; correction_by_overwrite p≈0.3 (to test that the system refuses it).

title: Plate loaded rotated 180 degrees
story:
Given a 96-well source plate loaded on the robot deck turned around, so A1 sits where H12 should be.
When the robot runs a worklist from A1 to H12.
Then well A1 of the destination actually holds material from source H12, and so on for every well.
real_life_noise: nobody notices; the plate barcode is on the short side and was scanned fine
it's caught at Split GFP because the empty wells (column 12) show signal and column 1 doesn't
only the destination was rotated, not the source
system_should: Support a single correction that remaps every well of a run by a known rule (rotate 180) instead of 96 manual fixes. Keep the original run as recorded and the corrected mapping as a later fact.
question_it_answers: For destination well A1, which source well did the material really come from?
cost_reason: Every result on the plate is assigned to the wrong design
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action load_plate. Error rotate_180 p≈0.002 per plate load; detected by empty-well pattern p≈0.7.

title: Liquid handler copies a plate well by well from a worklist
story:
Given DNA plate D-1001 (96 wells, 40 µL each) and an empty destination plate.
When a Hamilton-style liquid handler runs a worklist moving 5 µL from each source well to the same well in the destination.
Then 96 transfers are recorded, each source well shows 35 µL, each destination well holds 5 µL of the same DNA lot as its source.
real_life_noise: the worklist is a CSV with columns that differ by robot (SourcePlate, SourceWell, DestWell, Volume)
well names come as "A1", "A01" or as numbers 1 to 96 counted down columns
the robot log is uploaded hours after the run, or never
system_should: Import one run from a worklist or robot log, normalise well names, and create one transfer per well under a single run. Keep the lot of each destination well equal to its source well because nothing changed chemically.
question_it_answers: Where did each well of this plate come from?
cost_reason: Plate copies are the backbone of lineage for every sample
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist(n_wells=96 or 384). Errors: log_upload_missing p≈0.03, log_upload_delay 0.5 to 24 h, well_name_format random.

title: Robot run fails halfway
story:
Given a worklist with 96 transfers.
When the robot stops after 52 transfers with a tip pickup error and the scientist aborts.
Then only 52 transfers are recorded, the destination plate is marked as partly filled, and the run is marked aborted.
real_life_noise: the scientist records the whole worklist because that is what the template does
she restarts the run from the beginning, so wells 1 to 52 get a second 5 µL
she finishes the last 44 wells by hand with a multichannel and records nothing
the robot log says 53 because the 53rd aspirated but never dispensed, so the tip went to waste with 5 µL in it
system_should: Record transfers from what the robot says it did, not from what was planned. Allow a run to be aborted and resumed or completed by a second manual run. Flag wells that received twice. Treat an aspirated but not dispensed volume as lost.
question_it_answers: Which wells on this plate are really filled, and with how much?
cost_reason: Half-filled plates look complete and produce empty-well data
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist. Error abort_at step ~ Uniform(1, n) with p≈0.03 per run; then scientist chooses restart_full p≈0.2, resume p≈0.5, finish_by_hand_unrecorded p≈0.3.

title: Worklist says one thing, robot log says another
story:
Given a worklist asking for 2.5 µL per well and a robot log that reports 2.5 µL for 94 wells, 0 µL for B7 (clot detected) and 2.5 µL for G3 that was flagged as a short aspirate.
When the run is imported.
Then 94 wells get 2.5 µL, B7 gets nothing, G3 is recorded with an uncertain volume.
real_life_noise: someone imports the worklist instead of the log
the log is in the robot's own format and the columns are renamed in the latest software update
the scientist re-does B7 by hand and forgets to record it
system_should: Prefer the instrument log over the plan when both exist, and keep the plan attached for comparison. Mark per-well status (done, skipped, error). Allow a volume to be flagged as uncertain rather than forcing a number.
question_it_answers: Did this well get what the plan said?
cost_reason: One bad well per plate is normal; not knowing which is the problem
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist. Error per-well clot_or_bubble p≈0.005, short_aspirate p≈0.003; import_plan_instead_of_log p≈0.05.

title: A well is skipped and nobody notices
story:
Given a 384-well run where D14 was skipped by the robot because its source well was empty.
When the destination plate is used downstream.
Then D14 has no material and the inventory knows it, so the empty well is not reported as a failed protein.
real_life_noise: the source well was empty because the DNA supplier failed that design (Twist marks it in the plate map)
the robot doesn't log skips at all, only successes
system_should: Treat a well with no recorded transfer as empty, not as "unknown". Carry known-empty wells from the supplier plate map so they never look like failures.
question_it_answers: Is this well empty because nothing went in, or because the experiment failed?
cost_reason: Customers get "no expression" for a design that was never made
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist. Error skip_well p≈0.002 per well; supplier_failed_well p≈0.01 per DNA well.

title: Echo acoustic dispenser moves nanolitres from a 384 source plate
story:
Given an Echo-qualified 384-well source plate with 40 µL per well of DNA at 50 ng/µL.
When an Echo run moves 500 nL from 120 source wells into a 384-well expression plate, in 2.5 nL droplets.
Then each source well shows 39.5 µL, each destination well gets 25 ng of DNA, and the source plate's usable volume accounts for a dead volume of about 15 µL per well.
real_life_noise: the Echo survey reads 37 µL in a well the system says has 39.5 µL (evaporation or earlier miscount)
volumes are logged in nL and someone imports them as µL
the Echo refuses wells below its minimum working volume and logs them as exceptions
system_should: Store quantities with units and convert, so 500 nL and 0.5 µL are the same number. Let an instrument survey reading become a recount fact for each well. Treat the instrument's exception list as skipped wells.
question_it_answers: How much DNA is left in each source well, and is it above what the Echo can still use?
cost_reason: Unit slips of 1000× wreck balances quietly
sim_hook: Actor robot (Echo), action acoustic_transfer(vol_nL). Errors: unit_slip_nL_as_uL p≈0.01 per import; survey_drift ±0 to 3 µL per well per day open; below_min_exception when balance < dead volume.

title: Cherry-picking a few wells into a new plate
story:
Given three expression plates, E-31, E-32 and E-33.
When a robot picks 23 wells that passed Split GFP (for example E-31:C4, E-32:H11) into a new 96-well plate for a re-run.
Then the new plate holds 23 wells, each traced to its own source well and its own protein lot.
real_life_noise: the pick list was made from yesterday's Split GFP data and two of the wells have since been used up
the scientist reorders the pick list by hand and the mapping gets shifted by one
picks are recorded with the destination well only, no source
system_should: Keep lineage per well across many source plates. A destination plate can have wells from several sources and several customers. Refuse a transfer record that has no source well.
question_it_answers: For this re-run plate, which original wells and DNA does each well come from?
cost_reason: Re-runs are where mapping slips cost a second time
sim_hook: Actor robot, action cherry_pick(n=5..60 from 2..5 plates). Errors: off_by_one_mapping p≈0.01 per pick list, stale_pick (source empty) p≈0.03 per pick.

title: Pooling several wells into one
story:
Given four wells of the same protein expressed in parallel, 40 µL each.
When a scientist pools them into one tube to get enough for a BLI repeat.
Then the tube holds 160 µL, and its material has four parents, which may be four different protein lots.
real_life_noise: pools wells from two different DNA designs by mistake
records only the first well as the source
concentration of the pool is entered as the average, but the wells had very different expression
system_should: Support a container whose content has several parent lots. Decide one rule: pooling the same design makes a new lot whose parents are the pooled lots. Flag pools that mix different designs.
question_it_answers: If one of the pooled wells was bad, which results did it touch?
cost_reason: Mixed lineage hides the root cause of bad data
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action pool(src_wells=2..8). Errors: mixed_design p≈0.02, record_single_parent p≈0.10.

title: Reconstituting dried DNA turns a mass into a volume and a concentration
story:
Given a Twist plate where each well holds about 1 µg of dried DNA (amount varies per well, stated on the plate map).
When a scientist adds 40 µL of water to every well.
Then each well holds 40 µL at about 25 ng/µL, same DNA lot, and the water lot is recorded as an ingredient.
real_life_noise: the plate map says 1000 ng but the real yield per well ranges from 600 to 1400 ng
adds 20 µL to half the plate because the multichannel ran out
records "water" without a lot, because nobody tracks water
measures concentration later on a NanoDrop and gets numbers 20 percent off the calculation
system_should: Let a quantity change unit kind (mass to volume plus concentration) within the same lot. Keep the calculated concentration and later measured concentration as separate facts, the measured one winning. Make the solvent optional but allowed.
question_it_answers: What concentration is the DNA in this well, and is that calculated or measured?
cost_reason: Wrong concentration means the wrong amount goes into expression
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action reconstitute(vol_uL). Errors: wrong_volume_half_plate p≈0.02, missing_solvent_lot p≈0.6, yield_variation ±40 percent per well.

title: Making a diluted copy of a DNA plate
story:
Given a reconstituted DNA plate at about 25 ng/µL, 40 µL per well.
When a robot moves 4 µL from each well into 36 µL of water in a new plate (1:10).
Then the new plate has 40 µL per well at about 2.5 ng/µL, the source wells drop to 36 µL, and each new well keeps the DNA lot of its source.
real_life_noise: the water was pre-dispensed the day before and partly evaporated in the edge wells
the dilution factor is typed as 1:9 because "4 into 36"
the scientist dilutes only the columns that need it
system_should: Treat dilution as the same lot at a new concentration, plus a diluent as an ingredient. Store the factor or compute it from volumes, never both in a way that can disagree.
question_it_answers: What is in the diluted plate, and how does it relate to the original?
cost_reason: Concentration errors propagate into expression yield
sim_hook: Actor robot, action dilute(factor=5..20). Errors: factor_ambiguity p≈0.05, partial_plate p≈0.2 (not an error, just common).

title: Mixing a buffer from components creates a new lot
story:
Given 1 M HEPES (lot H-55), 5 M NaCl (lot N-12), Tween-20 (lot TW-3) and water.
When a scientist makes 500 mL of running buffer.
Then there is one new buffer lot with four parent lots, 500 mL in a bottle, expiring in 1 month, and each component's stock goes down.
real_life_noise: records the recipe amounts, not what was actually poured
forgets the Tween lot, since it's "always the same bottle"
makes 450 mL because the cylinder was wrong, labels it 500 mL
one component was already expired
system_should: Create a new lot with all components as parents and set expiry from the buffer type's rule. Warn when a component is expired or not QC'd. Let the recipe prefill the form, but store what was actually used.
question_it_answers: Which buffer lots used NaCl lot N-12?
cost_reason: A bad component must be traced to every buffer and experiment
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_buffer(recipe). Errors: missing_component_lot p≈0.10, recipe_not_actual p≈0.4, expired_component p≈0.02.

title: Loading buffer that lasts only a week
story:
Given loading buffer made on Monday with a 1 week life.
When it is used to fill a BLI sample plate the following Tuesday.
Then the transfer is recorded but flagged as using expired material, and every well filled from it carries that flag.
real_life_noise: the bottle label says Tuesday because the scientist wrote the date she expected to make it
two bottles of loading buffer exist and the old one gets used
system_should: Let the transfer happen (the bench already did it) but mark the destination wells. Expiry belongs to the lot, but the flag should show up on everything made from it.
question_it_answers: Did any experiment this week use expired loading buffer?
cost_reason: Bad buffer gives bad BLI curves that look like weak binders
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action fill_plate(buffer). Error use_older_bottle p≈0.05 when two bottles exist.

title: Normalising sample concentrations well by well
story:
Given an expression plate where Split GFP gives a different protein concentration per well (from 0.05 to 2 µM).
When a robot adds a different volume of buffer to each well so every BLI sample well lands at about 100 nM.
Then each well has its own transfer volume, its own new concentration, same protein lot, and wells too weak to reach 100 nM are recorded as "below target".
real_life_noise: the normalisation worklist is computed from a Split GFP file for a different plate
wells with very high concentration need more buffer than the well can hold, the robot caps it
the scientist reruns normalisation after adding a missing well, doubling buffer in some wells
system_should: Store per-well volume and concentration changes from one run. Link the worklist to the measurement it was computed from, so a mismatch in plate barcodes is caught. Keep "below target" as a state on the well, not just a note.
question_it_answers: What concentration did each sample go into BLI at, and what measurement was that based on?
cost_reason: Wrong concentrations give wrong binding constants
sim_hook: Actor robot, action normalise(per_well_vol from measurement). Errors: wrong_measurement_file p≈0.01, overflow_cap p≈0.02 per well, double_run p≈0.01.

title: Serial dilution of a target for a concentration series
story:
Given a Target X tube at 1 µM.
When a scientist makes a 2-fold series over 6 wells (1000, 500, 250, 125, 62.5, 31.25 nM), 100 µL final each.
Then six wells exist, each with its own concentration, all lot T-0412, and the chain is well 1 to well 2 to well 3, not all from the tube.
real_life_noise: records all six as coming from the tube directly
skips a step and the series goes 1000, 500, 125
system_should: Allow a well to be the source of another well on the same plate. Concentration should be traceable step by step.
question_it_answers: How much of the target tube did this series actually consume?
cost_reason: Small volumes, but consumption of the stock tube must still be right
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action serial_dilute(steps=4..8, factor=2..3). Error record_flat_from_stock p≈0.3.

title: Expression turns DNA into protein, so 96 new lots are born
story:
Given an expression plate with 96 wells, each holding DNA of one design plus cell-free expression mix.
When the expression run finishes (several hours at about 30 to 37 °C).
Then each well now contains a new protein lot, one per design, whose parents are the DNA lot in that well and the expression mix lot.
real_life_noise: the run is recorded as finished but the incubator crashed after 1 hour
the expression mix lot is the same for all 96 wells and nobody records it per well
the protein lot gets the DNA's lot number by copy-paste
system_should: Create new lots at the moment of the transformation, linked to every input lot. One shared input (the mix) may be linked once at the run level and apply to every well. The protein lot must be a different lot from the DNA, even if the container is the same plate.
question_it_answers: Which DNA and which expression mix made this protein?
cost_reason: This is where lineage from customer DNA to binding data is born
sim_hook: Actor robot (incubator), action express(plate). Errors: run_fail_unrecorded p≈0.01, mix_lot_missing p≈0.15.

title: Same plate, new contents
story:
Given an expression plate with barcode E-31 that held DNA plus mix this morning.
When expression finishes and the plate now holds protein.
Then the container is the same (same barcode, same freezer slot) but its content changed lot and material type, and the 2-week expiry clock starts.
real_life_noise: a query for "all DNA we have" still lists E-31
someone asks what was in E-31 yesterday
system_should: Content of a well is a history, not a field. Asking what was in a well at a time must work.
question_it_answers: What was in this plate on a given day?
cost_reason: Double counting DNA, and wrong expiry on proteins
sim_hook: Derived from XFER-020. Query checks after each express event.

title: Buying finished protein instead of expressing it
story:
Given a customer who sends 24 purified proteins in a 96-well plate instead of DNA.
When the plate is received and goes straight to BLI Sample Plate Prep.
Then the samples have supplier lots, no DNA parent, and the rest of the chain works the same.
real_life_noise: the customer's plate map uses their own well naming
concentrations are given in mg/mL, our plans use µM
system_should: Allow a sample lot with no parent lot. Convert mass concentration to molar only if molecular weight is known, otherwise keep both.
question_it_answers: Where did this sample come from, if not from our DNA?
cost_reason: Rare path, but must not need a separate model
sim_hook: Actor receiver, action receive_plate(material=sample, has_parent=false) p≈0.05 of experiments.

title: Evaporation from an open plate
story:
Given a 384-well plate with 20 µL per well left unsealed on the bench for 6 hours.
When it is measured before use.
Then wells hold 17 to 19 µL, edge wells less, and concentrations went up by the same factor.
real_life_noise: nobody measures; the system keeps showing 20 µL forever
the seal is put on crooked and the corner wells dry out over a weekend
system_should: Accept a recount fact per well or a plate-wide adjustment with a reason (evaporation). Don't try to predict evaporation in the database; let the simulation produce it and the recount correct it.
question_it_answers: Why does the system show more than the plate holds?
cost_reason: Small drift, but it adds up on source plates used many times
sim_hook: Environment process: per open plate, lose 0.2 to 0.6 µL per well per hour, edge wells ×2. Scientist recount p≈0.1 per use.

title: 96-well and 384-well formats in the same run
story:
Given four 96-well DNA plates.
When a robot compresses them into one 384-well plate (quadrant layout, plate 1 to A1, A3..., plate 2 to A2, A4...).
Then each 384 well maps to exactly one 96 well, and the mapping follows a known rule.
real_life_noise: the quadrant rule differs by robot software (interleaved vs block)
one of the four 96-well plates is only half full
system_should: Container types know their format (rows by columns). Well names must be validated against the format, so "P24" is fine on 384 and rejected on 96.
question_it_answers: Which 96-well plate and well did 384-well B2 come from?
cost_reason: A wrong quadrant rule scrambles four customers at once
sim_hook: Actor robot, action compress_96_to_384(rule=interleaved|block). Error wrong_rule_assumed p≈0.005 per run.

title: Tip and consumable use during a run
story:
Given a robot run of 96 transfers with fresh tips.
When the run finishes.
Then two boxes of 96 tips (one for aspirate steps, one spare for retries) and one destination plate are used up, counted as boxes, not tips.
real_life_noise: the robot reuses tips for buffer steps, so tip count isn't a fixed number
partial tip boxes are put back on the shelf
system_should: Track consumables as counts per box or per plate, not per tip. Decrement on run completion. Don't link every tip to a transfer.
question_it_answers: How many 384-well plates and tip boxes do we have left?
cost_reason: Running out stops the lab, but the fix is just ordering
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist consumes ceil(n_transfers/96) tip boxes; partial_box_return p≈0.4.

title: Liquid stuck in tips and walls (transfer loss)
story:
Given a protein sample of 50 µL pipetted into 5 wells of 10 µL.
When the transfers are done.
Then in practice the first four wells get 10 µL, the last gets about 7 µL, and 3 µL stays on tip walls and the tube. The source is empty.
real_life_noise: sticky protein or detergent buffers lose more
nobody records the loss, so the totals never balance
system_should: Accept that sum of outputs can be less than inputs. Record the gap as a loss on the run instead of forcing the numbers to balance. Never accept outputs larger than inputs without a flag.
question_it_answers: Why don't our volumes add up?
cost_reason: Small per transfer, but it hides real errors if not modelled
sim_hook: Physics: every transfer loses 1 to 5 percent; viscous material 5 to 15 percent.

title: Transfer between two plates of the same barcode (relabelled plate)
story:
Given a plate whose barcode label fell off in the freezer and was replaced with a new label.
When the next run scans the new barcode.
Then the system doesn't know the plate and creates a fresh empty one, so the run looks like it took from nothing.
real_life_noise: the scientist reuses the old barcode by printing it again
the old barcode is put on a different plate
system_should: Allow a barcode to be reassigned to an existing container with a recorded reason, and keep old barcodes as aliases. Refuse to auto-create a container from a scan inside a transfer.
question_it_answers: Is this the same plate as before?
cost_reason: Breaks lineage silently
sim_hook: Actor scientist, event label_lost p≈0.002 per plate-week in freezer; relabel_new_barcode p≈0.7, reprint_old p≈0.3.

title: Transfer with no destination container recorded
story:
Given a scientist takes 20 µL from a target tube for a quick test and doesn't use a tracked container.
When she records "used 20 µL".
Then the tube goes down by 20 µL and the run says "consumed, no destination".
real_life_noise: it's never recorded and the tube is 20 µL short at the next recount
system_should: Support consumption without a destination (goes into an untracked tube, an instrument, the sink). Keep the same transfer shape with an empty destination and a reason.
question_it_answers: What happened to the missing 20 µL?
cost_reason: Unrecorded uses are why counts drift
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action ad_hoc_use. Error unrecorded p≈0.25.

title: A transfer recorded twice
story:
Given a robot log uploaded by a script and then again by hand.
When both imports go through.
Then each well shows twice the consumption and the destination shows double the volume.
real_life_noise: the second import has a slightly different file name
the robot exports the same run in two formats
system_should: Use the instrument's run id plus timestamp as a key so the same run cannot be imported twice. If it is, keep the second as a rejected duplicate, visible.
question_it_answers: Did this run happen once or twice?
cost_reason: Doubles consumption of a whole plate in one click
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action import_log. Error duplicate_import p≈0.02 per run.

title: Undo a transfer that never happened
story:
Given a run recorded at 10:00 but the scientist cancelled before the robot started.
When she marks the run as cancelled at 10:30.
Then all its transfers are reversed by new entries, and the history shows both.
real_life_noise: she deletes the run instead (the system must not allow that)
system_should: Cancellation is a new event that reverses the run, not a delete.
question_it_answers: What did the record say before the cancellation?
cost_reason: Deletes lose the audit trail
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action cancel_run p≈0.02 per run; try_delete p≈0.1 of those.

title: Partial plate use across several days
story:
Given a reconstituted DNA plate of 96 designs.
When columns 1 to 4 are used on Monday, 5 to 8 on Wednesday, 9 to 12 next week.
Then the plate is one container with very different volumes per column, and freeze-thaw is counted for the whole plate each time it comes out.
real_life_noise: wells in column 1 get used again by mistake on Wednesday
plate stays on the bench between uses
system_should: Track volume per well, and storage events per plate. A well's history must show every draw.
question_it_answers: Which wells of this DNA plate still have enough to run again?
cost_reason: Re-runs need DNA; a used-up well means reordering
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action use_columns(subset). Error wrong_columns p≈0.01.

title: A tube that is both a source and a destination in one task
story:
Given a target tube with 30 µL at 2 mg/mL.
When a scientist adds 30 µL buffer to it to dilute in place.
Then the tube has 60 µL at 1 mg/mL of the same target lot, plus the buffer lot as an ingredient.
real_life_noise: records it as a new tube
doesn't update concentration, only volume
system_should: Allow in-place dilution: one container, volume up, concentration down, ingredient added.
question_it_answers: What concentration is this tube now?
cost_reason: Wrong concentration feeds into target plate prep
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action dilute_in_place. Error concentration_not_updated p≈0.15.

title: DNA arrival
story:
Given an order for 96 DNA designs from Twist.
When a 96-well plate arrives with dried DNA, a plate map file (well, design name, ng per well), and a supplier lot number.
Then one plate container exists, 96 wells each holding a mass of DNA (about 500 to 1000 ng), each well its own DNA lot linked to its design. Nothing is thrown away.
real_life_noise: two wells are marked "failed" in the plate map and hold no DNA
the plate map has 96 rows but the plate is 384 format
the plate is put in the freezer before being scanned
assumption, Twist ships some orders as dried DNA in plates; we assume this format for Adaptyv
system_should: Import the plate map as initial contents. Failed wells are empty from the start. In: nothing. Out: one plate, up to 96 new DNA lots. Lots are new (supplier lot per design).
question_it_answers: Which DNA did we receive, and which designs failed at the supplier?
cost_reason: Every later step depends on this mapping
sim_hook: Actor receiver, action receive_dna_plate(n=24..96). Errors: supplier_failed_well p≈0.01, plate_map_mismatch p≈0.01, late_scan p≈0.1.

title: DNA reconstitution
story:
Given the Twist plate from BIND-01.
When water is added to every well (for example 40 µL).
Then same plate, same DNA lots, now with volume and calculated concentration. Water lot is an ingredient. Nothing is thrown away.
real_life_noise: all the noise in XFER-014
reconstitutes the whole plate when only 24 designs are needed this week, so 72 wells sit wet in the freezer
plate sits on the bench 3 hours before going back, and the system has no record it was out
system_should: In: DNA plate (mass) plus water. Out: same plate (volume plus concentration). Lots carry over.
question_it_answers: What concentration is each DNA well now?
cost_reason: Concentration errors propagate into expression
sim_hook: Same as XFER-014.

title: DNA dilution (optional step)
story:
Given the reconstituted plate.
When a diluted copy is made because the DNA is too concentrated for expression.
Then a new diluted DNA plate exists with the same lots per well, lower concentration. The reconstituted plate stays as the master and goes back to the freezer.
real_life_noise: the step is skipped for some plates and not others, so later steps take from either plate
system_should: In: reconstituted plate plus water. Out: new plate, lots carry over. The next step must be able to take from either plate.
question_it_answers: Which plate did the expression plate take its DNA from?
cost_reason: Wrong source plate breaks lineage
sim_hook: Actor robot, action dilute p≈0.5 of experiments.

title: Expression plate prep
story:
Given DNA (reconstituted or diluted plate) and a cell-free expression mix (assumption, Adaptyv uses cell-free expression).
When a robot puts mix and a small volume of DNA (for example 2 µL) into each well of a new expression plate.
Then a new plate exists with each well holding DNA lot plus mix lot. DNA plate wells go down. Tips and the empty plate are used up.
real_life_noise: mix thawed and left at room temperature too long
plate map uses different well layout from the DNA plate (for example 96 to 384)
system_should: In: DNA plate, mix. Out: expression plate, still holding DNA (not protein yet). No new lots until expression runs.
question_it_answers: Which DNA went into each well of the expression plate?
cost_reason: Mapping errors here give wrong customer data
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist(DNA to expression plate). Errors as XFER-007 to XFER-010.

title: Expression run
story:
Given the expression plate from BIND-04.
When it incubates (assumption, several hours, about 30 °C).
Then each well contains a new protein lot, linked to its DNA lot and the mix lot. The plate gets a 2-week life from now.
real_life_noise: all the noise in XFER-020
expression plate goes into the fridge after the run with nobody recording the end time, so the 2-week clock starts from the plan
wells with no DNA (supplier failures) still get mix and are counted as "no expression"
system_should: In: expression plate with DNA. Out: same plate with protein. New lots per well.
question_it_answers: When was this protein made, and when does it expire?
cost_reason: Start of sample lineage
sim_hook: Same as XFER-020.

title: Antigen arrival
story:
Given an order for Target X from a supplier.
When a vial of lyophilised (freeze-dried) target arrives, for example 100 µg, with a certificate of analysis.
Then one vial exists with a new supplier lot, mass 100 µg, waiting for QC.
real_life_noise: two vials of the same lot arrive in one box and are registered as two lots
the certificate says 100 µg, the vial label says 0.1 mg
system_should: In: nothing. Out: one vial, new lot, not usable until QC. See RCV area for receiving detail.
question_it_answers: What target lots do we have waiting for QC?
cost_reason: Target is expensive and shared
sim_hook: Actor receiver, action receive_vial. Errors as RCV area.

title: Antigen reconstitution, buffer exchange and QC, ending in a target stock tube
story:
Given the 100 µg vial of Target X.
When it is dissolved in 100 µL water (1 mg/mL), moved into running buffer by buffer exchange (a spin column, losing about 10 to 20 percent), measured, and QC'd.
Then there is a target stock tube with about 90 µL at about 0.9 mg/mL in the new buffer, same supplier lot, QC passed. The vial and the spin column are thrown away.
real_life_noise: the yield after buffer exchange is 70 percent, recorded as 100
QC fails and the stock tube still gets aliquoted
the stock tube format is "ABE / ART format" in the diagram; we don't know what that means (assumption, it's a named tube format or supplier label)
