system_should: In: vial, water, buffer. Out: stock tube, same lot, new buffer as ingredient. Thrown away: vial, column. Losses recorded. QC result attached to the lot.
question_it_answers: How much usable Target X do we have after QC?
cost_reason: Shared target; wrong amount means wrong ordering decision
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action reconstitute_exchange_qc. Errors: loss_unrecorded p≈0.4, qc_fail p≈0.05, use_before_qc p≈0.02.

title: BLI or SPR target plate prep
story:
Given the target stock tube.
When a scientist dilutes target to, for example, 10 µg/mL in loading buffer and fills 8 wells of a 96-well black plate at 200 µL each (assumption, Octet uses about 200 µL per well in 96 format, 40 to 80 µL in 384 tilted plates).
Then a target plate exists, 8 wells of Target X lot, and the stock tube went down by about 16 µL.
real_life_noise: the target plate also has buffer-only wells for baseline, not recorded
target is taken from the oldest open tube, not the one recorded
system_should: In: target stock, loading buffer. Out: target plate. Lots carry over. Target plate is thrown away after use.
question_it_answers: How much target did this experiment use?
cost_reason: Target consumption drives reordering
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action prep_target_plate. Errors: wrong_tube p≈0.03, buffer_wells_unrecorded p≈0.3.

title: Split GFP plate prep
story:
Given the expression plate with protein.
When a robot moves a small amount (for example 5 µL) from each well into a split-GFP plate that holds the GFP1-10 detector (assumption, samples carry a short GFP11 tag; when they meet, the GFP turns on and glows in proportion to protein amount).
Then a split-GFP plate exists, each well holding protein lot plus detector lot. The expression plate wells go down.
real_life_noise: GFP detector stock has passed its 6-month frozen life
plate prepared in 384 from a 96 expression plate
system_should: In: expression plate, GFP stock buffer. Out: split-GFP plate. Lots carry over. Plate thrown away after measurement.
question_it_answers: Which protein is in each Split GFP well?
cost_reason: Bad mapping gives wrong concentrations downstream
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist(expression to GFP plate).

title: Split GFP measurement
story:
Given the split-GFP plate.
When a plate reader measures fluorescence.
Then each protein lot on the expression plate gets a measured concentration, and the split-GFP plate is thrown away with liquid still in it.
real_life_noise: reader file has its own well numbering
plate thrown away before the data was checked
system_should: In: split-GFP plate. Out: measurements linked to the protein lots, not just to the plate. Thrown away: split-GFP plate with contents.
question_it_answers: What concentration is each expressed protein?
cost_reason: Feeds normalisation
sim_hook: Actor plate reader, action measure. Error wrong_plate_file p≈0.01.

title: Sample concentration normalisation
story:
Given Split GFP concentrations for each protein lot.
When a worklist is computed and used during sample plate prep.
Then each sample well gets its own buffer volume to reach a target concentration.
real_life_noise: all the noise in XFER-018
the diagram marks this step as "implementation in progress", so today it may be a scientist's spreadsheet, not a worklist the system sees
the measurement used is from before a re-expression, so it describes different protein lots
system_should: In: measurement plus expression plate. Out: worklist. No material moves in this step itself.
question_it_answers: Which measurement did this normalisation use?
cost_reason: Wrong concentrations in BLI
sim_hook: Same as XFER-018.

title: BLI or SPR sample plate prep
story:
Given the expression plate with protein and loading buffer.
When a robot moves protein into one or more sample plates, diluting each to target concentration.
Then sample plates exist, wells hold protein lots plus buffer lot. The expression plate goes back to the fridge for 2 weeks in case of re-runs.
real_life_noise: more than one sample plate per expression plate
a re-run uses the expression plate after 2 weeks
system_should: In: expression plate, loading buffer. Out: sample plates. Lots carry over.
question_it_answers: Can we re-run from this expression plate?
cost_reason: Re-runs depend on expression plate life
sim_hook: Actor robot, action run_worklist(expression to sample plates).

title: BLI or SPR run
story:
Given a target plate and sample plates.
When the instrument runs.
Then data is produced for each sample well against the target wells, and both plates are thrown away with liquid still in them.
real_life_noise: run fails halfway and plates are thrown away anyway
data file has no plate barcodes
system_should: In: target plate, sample plates. Out: data linked to wells and lots. Thrown away: both plates.
question_it_answers: Which target lot and which protein lot made this binding curve?
cost_reason: This is the result the customer pays for
sim_hook: Actor instrument, action bli_run. Error run_fail p≈0.03.

title: Data processing and review
story:
Given the BLI data.
When it is processed and reviewed.
Then no material moves, but results that fail QC lead to a re-run request that needs to know what material is left.
real_life_noise: re-run asked after the expression plate has expired
expression plate still exists but the wells needed have under 5 µL left
target stock looks like 40 µL, but two aliquots were used without being recorded
system_should: No material moves. The inventory must answer "can we re-run this sample" from what's left and usable.
question_it_answers: Can we re-run these samples without new DNA or target?
cost_reason: Wrong answer means a delay or needless reorder
sim_hook: Actor reviewer, action request_rerun p≈0.1 per sample.

title: Scientist moves a tube from one freezer box to another and scans both ends
story:
Given tube T-1001 (Target X, lot L1) sits in freezer F1 (-80), rack R3, box B12, slot C4.
When a scientist takes it out, puts it in box B07 slot A1 in freezer F2 and scans the tube, then the new box and slot.
Then the system says T-1001 is in F2 / B07 / A1, slot C4 in B12 is free, and the history shows both places with who and when.
real_life_noise: scans the tube and the box but types the slot as "A01" instead of "A1"
scans the box first and the tube second, so the order of events is backwards
drops the tube in A1 but A1 is already taken in the system by a tube that was thrown away last month and never marked
scans at the freezer with gloves on and the scan registers twice
system_should: Record the move as a new event, never overwrite the old place. Accept slot names in a few common spellings and store one form. If the target slot is shown as taken, do not silently put two tubes in one slot. Ask, or record both and raise a conflict.
question_it_answers: Where is T-1001 right now, and where was it before?
cost_reason: A wrong slot means ten minutes of searching with the freezer door open
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action move_tube, error slot_typo p≈0.02, double_scan p≈0.01, target_slot_occupied_stale p≈0.01

title: A whole box moves, and everything in it moves with it
story:
Given box B12 holds 64 tubes in freezer F1, rack R3, shelf 2.
When a technician moves the box to freezer F2, rack R1, shelf 4 and scans only the box barcode.
Then all 64 tubes report freezer F2 as their place, without 64 separate move records being typed in, and their slots inside the box stay the same.
real_life_noise: two tubes were taken out of the box an hour earlier and are on the bench, but nobody scanned them out, so they "move" to F2 on paper
the box label is on the lid, and the lid was swapped with another box's lid
the box is put in the right freezer but on a different shelf than scanned
system_should: Store each tube's place as "inside box B12" and the box's place as "F2 / R1 / shelf 4", so one scan moves everything. Asking "where is tube X" walks up the nesting. Keep the box move as one event so the history is readable.
question_it_answers: Where is every tube that was in box B12?
cost_reason: If tubes are stored with flat freezer locations, one box move leaves 64 stale records
sim_hook: Actor technician, action move_box, error untracked_tube_removed_before_move p≈0.05 per box move, lid_swap p≈0.005

title: A plate goes freezer, bench, instrument, back to freezer in one day
story:
Given reconstituted DNA plate P-220 in freezer F3 (-20).
When at 09:10 it is taken to the bench to thaw, at 09:40 it goes onto the liquid handler deck, at 11:00 it comes off, and at 11:15 it goes back into F3 on a different shelf.
Then the system shows four moves in order, the plate's current place is F3 shelf 1, and the total time out of the freezer is about two hours.
real_life_noise: only the first and last moves get scanned; the bench and robot steps are missing
the "back to freezer" scan happens at 16:00 when the scientist remembers, though the plate went back at 11:15
the plate sits on the bench over lunch and nobody knows how long it was out
system_should: Accept moves with a "when it happened" time separate from "when it was recorded". Treat the robot run itself as evidence the plate was on the deck, even without a scan. Time out of the freezer is computed from moves, and is marked uncertain when steps are missing.
question_it_answers: Where is P-220, and how long has it spent outside the cold?
cost_reason: Wrong time-out-of-freezer hides thaw damage; wrong place costs search time
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action plate_round_trip, error skip_intermediate_scan p≈0.4 per intermediate step, late_return_scan delay 0-6 h with p≈0.15

title: Whole 96-tube rack read at once by a rack scanner
story:
Given a 96-position rack of 2D-barcoded tubes (Datamatrix code on the bottom of each tube) holding target aliquots.
When a scientist puts the rack on a flatbed rack scanner and it reads all 96 positions in one go.
Then the system gets 96 (tube barcode, position) pairs plus the rack barcode, and updates every tube's place in one event.
real_life_noise: 3 positions come back "no read" because of frost on the tube bottoms
the rack is put on the scanner rotated 180 degrees, so A1 reads as H12
one position reads "no tube" though there is a tube in it, because it sits too high
the scanner software exports a CSV that is saved and uploaded twice
system_should: Take the rack scan as one batch. Store no-reads as "unknown in position X", not as empty. Notice when the pattern of barcodes matches the known layout rotated 180 degrees and offer to flip it. Ignore an identical re-upload of the same scan file.
question_it_answers: What is in this rack, slot by slot?
cost_reason: A rotated rack swaps 96 tube places at once and nobody notices until the wrong target is used
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action rack_scan, error no_read p≈0.03 per position on frozen racks (0.005 when thawed), rotated_rack p≈0.01 per scan, duplicate_upload p≈0.02

title: Frosted -80 tube will not scan
story:
Given tube T-2044 has just come out of the -80 and its barcode label is covered in frost.
When a scientist tries the handheld scanner four times, gives up and types the barcode by hand from the printed digits.
Then the system accepts the typed barcode, records that it was typed and not scanned, and the rest of the task goes on.
real_life_noise: types one digit wrong and it matches a different, real tube
wipes the label with a glove and the printed digits smear
grabs the tube next to it, which scans fine, and uses that instead without recording it
system_should: Mark every record with how the barcode got in (scan, rack scan, typed, picked from list). Check typed barcodes with a check digit or against what is expected in that box. Typed entries that hit a tube in a different freezer should warn before going ahead.
question_it_answers: How sure are we that this event was about the right tube?
cost_reason: A typo that matches a real tube silently moves or consumes the wrong material
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action scan_frozen_tube, error scan_fail p≈0.15 for -80 tubes, then manual_entry with typo p≈0.02 per typed barcode

title: Two containers carry the same barcode
story:
Given tube T-3100 already exists, holding Buffer A.
When a new tube of Target Y is registered and its pre-printed label also reads T-3100 (a reprint from the same label roll).
Then the system refuses the second registration, or registers it on hold with a clear duplicate flag, and asks for a new label.
real_life_noise: the duplicate is only noticed weeks later, when a scan of T-3100 "moves" the buffer tube to a box that holds targets
label printer was reset and started counting from 3000 again
supplier pre-barcoded tubes from two different suppliers happen to share a number
system_should: Barcodes are unique among containers that are still in the lab. When a scan hits a barcode whose recorded place, material or size does not fit the context, warn. Keep a way to give a container a new barcode while keeping its history.
question_it_answers: Which container does this barcode really mean?
cost_reason: Every later event lands on the wrong container and mixes two histories
sim_hook: Actor label_printer, action print_label, error counter_reset_duplicate p≈0.001 per label; supplier_barcode_collision p≈0.0005 per received tube

title: Barcode from a thrown-away plate is used again
story:
Given plate P-500 was thrown away last month with its barcode label still on it, and its record says disposed.
When a scientist pulls a sheet of old printed labels and sticks P-500 on a new plate.
Then the scan of P-500 should not bring the old plate back to life; the system should say "this barcode belonged to a disposed plate" and offer to retire the old link and start a new container.
real_life_noise: some labs reuse plate barcodes on purpose for washable or reusable racks and boxes
the old plate was "disposed" in the system but is actually still in the back of a fridge
system_should: Keep container identity separate from the barcode string. A barcode can point to one live container at a time, and the history of which container held it when is kept. Reusable holders (racks, boxes) can be allowed to reuse barcodes; plates and tubes by default cannot.
question_it_answers: Is this plate new, or is it the old one we threw away?
cost_reason: A disposed plate can look usable again, exactly the failure the brief names
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action label_new_plate, error reuse_disposed_barcode p≈0.005 per new plate

title: Hand-written label with no barcode
story:
Given a scientist makes a quick dilution late in the evening and writes "TgtX 1:10 BA 21/10" on the tube with a marker.
When the next morning someone finds it on the bench.
Then the system either has a record without a barcode that can be matched by description and later given a printed label, or has nothing and the tube is registered as found.
real_life_noise: ethanol wipe has made the marker writing half unreadable
the scientist meant to register it but forgot
two hand-written tubes look identical
system_should: Allow a container to exist with no barcode for a while, with a short free-text label and owner. List "unlabelled containers older than 24 h" so they get labelled or thrown away. Never count them as usable stock while they have no barcode, unless someone confirms.
question_it_answers: What is this unlabelled tube and is it safe to use?
cost_reason: Unknown tubes either get thrown out (waste) or used blindly (bad data)
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_tube_without_label, p≈0.02 per manual dilution; forget_register p≈0.5 of those

title: Tube moved without anyone scanning it
story:
Given the system says tube T-1500 is in freezer F1, box B3, slot D2.
When a colleague borrows it, uses it, and puts it back in F2 box B9 slot E5 without scanning.
Then the system still says F1 / B3 / D2. The next person to look for it finds the slot empty.
real_life_noise: the tube is put back into B3 but in slot D3, so it looks like it is in place at a glance
it ends up in another person's box because the slot was free there
system_should: Not pretend to know. When someone records "slot empty" or a later scan finds the tube elsewhere, record the new place, mark the gap between the last known and found as unknown, and keep the fact that the record was wrong for a while. Report "last confirmed" next to "where".
question_it_answers: Where is T-1500 really, and when did we last know for sure?
cost_reason: Search time, and sometimes a needless reorder when the tube looks lost
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action borrow_and_return, error no_scan_on_return p≈0.10, wrong_slot_on_return p≈0.05

title: Item found in a slot the system says is empty
story:
Given the system says box B4 slot F7 is empty.
When a scientist opens the box and finds a tube there and scans it.
Then the system shows where it thought that tube was, moves it to B4 / F7 with a "found" reason, and the old place is freed.
real_life_noise: the tube's barcode is not in the system at all (never registered)
the tube's record says it was thrown away three weeks ago
the tube is a duplicate barcode (see LOC-006)
system_should: Have three paths: known tube found elsewhere (correct place, flag), unknown barcode (register as found, on hold until someone says what is in it), disposed tube found (do not quietly undo the disposal; ask whether the disposal record was wrong, and if so, correct it with a new entry).
question_it_answers: How often is our "where" wrong, and for which places?
cost_reason: Lost material reappearing as disposed hides real stock and inflates orders
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action open_box_scan_all, outcome found_unexpected p≈0.02 per slot checked; of those 60% misplaced known, 25% never registered, 15% marked disposed

title: Freezer breaks down and everything is moved in a hurry
story:
Given freezer F2 (-80) holds 40 boxes, about 2,500 tubes. The alarm goes off at 02:00 and the temperature is -45 and rising.
When the on-call person moves boxes into F1, F4 and a dry-ice cooler over the next hour, without scanning anything.
Then the next morning the system still says all 2,500 tubes are in F2, which is now off and empty.
real_life_noise: boxes are split across three places with no notes, or with notes on a paper towel
some boxes are put shelf-by-shelf, others piled loosely
the dry-ice cooler has no barcode and no location record at all
it takes a week before all boxes are rescanned
system_should: Let someone mark F2 as "emptied in emergency, contents being rehoused". All contents go to a "location uncertain, last seen F2" state, not to "missing". As boxes are scanned into new places they leave that state. Show a count of what is still unaccounted for. Record the temperature excursion against everything that was in F2 at the time, since that also matters for shelf life.
question_it_answers: After the F2 failure, where is everything, and what got warm?
cost_reason: Thousands of records wrong at once; expensive targets may be lost or warmed without anyone knowing
sim_hook: Actor on_call, action emergency_rehouse, event freezer_failure p≈0.5 per freezer per year; no_scan_during_rehouse p≈0.95 per box; rescan_delay 1-7 days

title: A new freezer is added
story:
Given the lab buys a new -80, F5, with 5 shelves and 4 rack slots per shelf.
When an admin adds F5 and its inner layout, and prints barcodes for each shelf and rack.
Then F5 can be chosen as a place, its racks and boxes can be scanned into it, and nothing about older freezers changes.
real_life_noise: the freezer is used for two days before anyone adds it, so moves are recorded as "bench" or "other"
the rack barcodes printed for F5 reuse numbers from F1 racks
the inner layout entered (5 shelves) does not match reality (shelf 3 was removed for tall racks)
system_should: Adding a place is adding rows, not changing the schema. Places nest: room, freezer, shelf, rack, box, slot. Layout can be changed later without breaking past history.
question_it_answers: What storage do we have and how full is it?
cost_reason: Mostly a setup chore, but late setup leaves vague "bench" records
sim_hook: Actor admin, action add_freezer, error late_setup delay 0-3 days p≈0.3

title: Room reorganisation renames and moves whole freezers
story:
Given freezers F1 to F4 stand in room 1.02.
When the lab moves F3 and F4 to room 1.05 and renames shelves so labels match a new scheme.
Then one move of F3 moves everything inside it, the room change is recorded once, and old reports still show the old names for the old dates.
real_life_noise: the rename is done by editing the name in place, so history now shows the new name for last year
the freezer is unplugged for 40 minutes during the move
while moving, some loose tubes in door shelves fall into a different shelf
system_should: Keep places as stable things with a name that can change over time. Moving a freezer is a move of one place inside another. Unplugged time is recorded as a possible temperature event for its contents.
question_it_answers: What did "F3 shelf 2" mean on a given date?
cost_reason: Mostly confusion in old reports, unless the unplugged time matters for stability
sim_hook: Actor admin, action move_storage_unit, error rename_in_place p≈0.3 per rename, unplugged 20-60 min

title: Last seen is not the same as where it is
story:
Given tube T-4400 was last scanned 94 days ago into F1 / B2 / A6, and nothing has happened to it since.
When a scientist asks where it is.
Then the system answers "last seen F1 / B2 / A6 on 2026-07-19 by Ana", not just "F1 / B2 / A6", and older records look less trusted than recent ones.
real_life_noise: the box it is in was moved since (this is fine, it moves with the box)
the box was "moved" via a box scan, but the tube had been taken out before
system_should: Every place answer comes with when it was last confirmed and how (direct tube scan, inferred via box, typed). A tube confirmed only by its box being moved is weaker than a tube scanned on its own.
question_it_answers: How much should I trust where the system says this is?
cost_reason: People stop trusting the system if they get burned by stale places with no warning
sim_hook: Derived from move logs; no extra actor. Sim tracks ground truth and reports drift between true place and recorded place per container.

title: Plates stacked in a plate hotel next to the robot
story:
Given a plate hotel (a vertical rack beside the liquid handler) with 20 numbered slots, used by the robot arm to fetch plates.
When 12 expression plates are loaded into slots 1 to 12 for an overnight run.
Then the system knows each plate's slot, and when the robot moves a plate to the deck and back, the slot changes are logged from the robot's own log.
real_life_noise: the scientist loads plates in a different order than the run file expects, so slot 3 holds what the run thinks is in slot 4
one slot is skipped because its shelf is bent
the robot log is imported hours later or the import fails silently
system_should: Treat the hotel as a place with numbered slots, same as a box. Accept moves from instrument logs as well as from people, and record which source said so. If a plate scanned at the hotel does not match what the run expects in that slot, stop and say so before the run, not after.
question_it_answers: Which plate is in which hotel slot right now?
cost_reason: Swapped plates in an automated run give wrong data for a whole plate of customer samples
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action load_plate_hotel, error slot_order_swap p≈0.02 per run, robot_log_import_fail p≈0.01

title: Plate is inside the instrument mid-run
story:
Given BLI target plate TP-77 and sample plate SP-78 are loaded into the BLI instrument at 14:00 for a 6-hour run.
When someone searches for TP-77 at 16:00.
Then the system says it is in the BLI instrument, in run R-512, started at 14:00, and that it cannot be used or moved until the run ends.
real_life_noise: run is aborted after 1 hour and the plates are taken out, but the run record still says "running"
a plate is kept in the instrument overnight after the run ended because nobody unloaded it
two plates swapped between the two instrument plate positions
system_should: A run puts its plates in the instrument for the run's time. When the run ends, the plates stay in the instrument until someone moves them out. A "running" run older than its expected length is flagged.
question_it_answers: Where is TP-77 and can I use it right now?
cost_reason: People may count in-use material as free, or waste time hunting for it
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action load_instrument, error abort_not_recorded p≈0.03 per run, left_in_instrument_overnight p≈0.1

title: Plate leaves the lab to a customer or a partner site
story:
Given an expression plate EP-14 with customer proteins.
When it is packed on dry ice and shipped by courier to the customer, with a tracking number.
Then it leaves the lab's stock (not usable here), its last place is "in transit, courier, tracking 1Z...", and later "delivered to customer Acme".
real_life_noise: the plate is scanned out but the shipment is delayed a day and it sits in the -20 by the door
the courier returns it because of an address problem
only a copy of the plate was shipped; the original stays, but someone scans the original out
system_should: Shipping is a move to a place outside the lab. The container keeps its identity and history. If it comes back, it is moved back in, not created again. Material that left the lab is not counted in usable stock.
question_it_answers: What left the lab, when, and to whom?
cost_reason: Shipped material counted as stock gives false numbers; scanning out the wrong plate loses track of the original
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action ship_out, error ship_scan_wrong_plate p≈0.01, returned_shipment p≈0.02

title: Material moved to another Adaptyv site
story:
Assumption: Adaptyv has, or will have, a second lab site, or a partner lab where some steps run.
Given 6 target tubes are sent from site A to site B on dry ice.
When site B receives them and scans them.
Then the tubes keep their barcodes and lot, show "in transit" for the days on the road, and then sit in site B's freezer.
real_life_noise: site B scans them in and the scan creates 6 new tubes, because their system did not find them
one tube is missing from the box on arrival
dry ice ran out on the way and the box arrived warm
system_should: Sites are just top-level places. A receive at site B matches existing containers by barcode first. Shortages on arrival are flagged. Transit time and temperature can be recorded against the tubes.
question_it_answers: How much Target X do we have at each site?
cost_reason: Duplicated containers at site B double count expensive target
sim_hook: Actor courier, action transfer_site, error missing_on_arrival p≈0.01 per tube, warm_on_arrival p≈0.02 per shipment

title: Wrong tube scanned, then corrected
story:
Given a scientist moves T-6000 to box B5 slot A2, but scans the tube next to it, T-6001.
When ten minutes later they see the mistake and fix it.
Then the system has: the wrong move of T-6001, a correction that cancels it, and the right move of T-6000. T-6001's place goes back to where it was.
real_life_noise: the fix is made by editing the old record directly
the mistake is only found two days later, after T-6001 was "moved" again
the person fixing it is not the person who made the mistake
system_should: Corrections are new events that point to the event they cancel. The current place is computed from events that were not cancelled. The history keeps both, with who did each.
question_it_answers: Who changed this tube's place, and what did the record say before?
cost_reason: Edited-in-place history makes audits impossible
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action move_tube, error wrong_adjacent_tube p≈0.01; correction delay 5 min to 3 days, p_corrected≈0.6

title: Physical count of a freezer disagrees with the system
story:
Given the system says freezer F1 holds 1,212 tubes across 22 boxes.
When the team does a stock-take and rack-scans every box.
Then the result is 1,190 tubes found where expected, 9 found in other slots or boxes, 13 not found, and 4 not in the system.
real_life_noise: the stock-take takes two days, and normal work continues in between
one box was not scanned because it was in use on the bench
the scanner had frost problems and 30 positions were no-reads
system_should: Treat a stock-take as one session that records what was seen, and compare it to what the records said at the time each box was scanned, not at the end. Produce a list of differences and turn accepted ones into corrections. Not-found tubes go to "missing", not "disposed".
question_it_answers: How accurate is our location data?
cost_reason: Without a reconcile step, location drift grows forever
sim_hook: Actor technician, action stock_take, uses ground truth from sim to produce differences; no_read p≈0.03 per position, box_in_use_skipped p≈0.05 per box

title: Box with grid positions, slot naming differs by box size
story:
Given the lab uses 9x9 boxes (81 slots, A1 to I9) for 2 mL tubes and 10x10 boxes (100 slots) for 1.5 mL tubes, plus 96-position racks (A1 to H12).
When a tube is placed in J10.
Then the system accepts J10 for a 10x10 box and rejects it for a 9x9 box.
real_life_noise: some boxes are numbered 1 to 81 instead of letter-number
people count from the wrong corner

real_life_noise.box types get mixed: a 10x10 insert put into a 9x9 box

system_should: Each holder type knows its grid. Positions are stored as row and column, and shown in whatever style the box uses. Invalid positions are rejected at entry.
question_it_answers: Which exact slot is this tube in?
cost_reason: Annoying but usually caught on the next look
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action place_tube, error invalid_position p≈0.005, numbering_style_mismatch p≈0.01

title: Two tubes put in the same slot in the system
story:
Given slot C4 in box B12 holds T-1001.
When T-1009 is scanned into B12 / C4 too.
Then the system does not let both sit in C4 silently. It either asks "move T-1001 out?" or records a conflict to be resolved.
real_life_noise: in real life T-1001 was taken out earlier without a scan, so the new scan is correct and the old record is the wrong one
the scientist really put two small tubes in one slot because the box was full
system_should: One container per slot by default. On conflict, assume the newest direct scan is the truth for the new tube and mark the old one as "location uncertain, was displaced from C4". Never delete the old one's history.
question_it_answers: What is in C4 right now?
cost_reason: Quiet double booking leads to picking the wrong tube
sim_hook: Arises naturally from LOC-009 no_scan removals; plus actor scientist, action double_up_slot p≈0.002

title: Rack scanned at the freezer finds a tube from another box
story:
Given rack RK-3 is recorded as holding 96 aliquots of Target X.
When it is rack-scanned and position B7 holds a tube of Target Z, which the system places in rack RK-9.
Then the system moves that tube to RK-3 / B7, flags it as "found in unexpected place", and RK-9 / B7 (its old slot) becomes unknown, not empty.
real_life_noise: the Target Z tube is a near-identical looking aliquot and someone will grab it thinking it is Target X
RK-9's B7 also holds a wrong tube, so the two were swapped
system_should: Detect swaps when two scans find each other's tubes. Show material-mismatch in a rack that is supposed to hold one material, because that is how the wrong target ends up in an experiment.
question_it_answers: Is every tube in this rack what we think it is?
cost_reason: A Target Z tube used as Target X ruins a binding run and the data looks real
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action return_tube_to_rack, error wrong_rack p≈0.005, swap_with_neighbour_rack p≈0.002

title: Tube kept in a pocket, cooler or ice bucket for the day
story:
Given a scientist takes 5 tubes from the -80 into an ice bucket on their bench.
When they scan them out to "bench, Ana" and use them over the day.
Then the tubes show as on the bench with Ana, time out of freezer keeps adding up, and at 18:00 a list shows tubes still out since morning.
real_life_noise: ice bucket is not a scannable place, so they pick "bench" from a list
one tube is left in the ice bucket overnight and the ice melted
Ana goes home and Ben picks up the bucket and puts tubes back in a different freezer
system_should: Allow temporary places like a person's bench or bucket. Show "out of storage" containers with how long. Being out overnight is worth a flag for proteins.
question_it_answers: What is out of the freezer right now, and since when?
cost_reason: Warm overnight targets go back into the freezer looking fine
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action take_to_bench, error left_out_overnight p≈0.02 per tube, returned_by_other_person p≈0.1

title: Handheld scanner is offline and syncs late
story:
Assumption: some scans are done on a battery handheld that stores scans and uploads when back in Wi-Fi range or docked.
Given a technician does 40 moves in the cold room where Wi-Fi is weak.
When the scanner uploads all 40 at 15:30, two hours after they happened.
Then the system records each move with its scan time, not the upload time, and orders them correctly against moves others made in between.
real_life_noise: meanwhile another scientist moved one of those tubes again at 14:00 from a desktop scan
the scanner clock is 7 minutes off
the scanner battery died and 10 scans were lost
system_should: Keep happened-at and recorded-at separate. When a late event lands before an already-recorded later event, compute the current place from event order by happened-at time and flag the overlap. Allow a device clock offset to be noted.
question_it_answers: In what order did things really happen?
cost_reason: Late syncs can move a tube "back" to an old place after it has moved on
sim_hook: Actor technician, action batch_scan_offline, sync delay 0-4 h, device clock_skew ±10 min p≈0.1 per device, lost_batch p≈0.005

title: Shelf label scanned instead of the box
story:
Given every shelf, rack and box carries a barcode.
When a scientist meaning to scan box B9 scans the shelf label beside it.
Then the system sees the tube is going "into a shelf", which is allowed for boxes but not for single tubes, and asks to scan a box.
real_life_noise: rules are too strict, people find a workaround (scanning any box) and it gets worse
a scanned barcode belongs to a tube, so the system thinks the user wants to put a tube into a tube
system_should: Know what kind of thing each barcode is, and what can hold what (a tube can go in a box slot or a rack slot, a box can go on a shelf). Reject impossible nesting with a short message.
question_it_answers: (data quality) Are places valid?
cost_reason: Caught at once if the rules exist; silent mess if not
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action scan_destination, error wrong_level_scanned p≈0.01

title: Supplier plate arrives with its own barcode
story:
Given a DNA plate arrives from the supplier (Twist, per the workflow diagram) with the supplier's barcode on the side.
When it is received and the lab adds its own label too.
Then both barcodes point to the same plate, and either one finds it.
real_life_noise: the supplier barcode is on the side that faces the wall in the freezer
the lab label is stuck over the supplier barcode
later scans use the supplier barcode only, and the system does not know it
system_should: Let a container have more than one identifier, each with a source (ours, supplier), all unique among live containers.
question_it_answers: Which plate is this, whichever label I scan?
cost_reason: Mostly friction, but unknown supplier barcodes create duplicate plates
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action receive_plate, error scan_supplier_code_later_unknown p≈0.05

title: Freezer slot map is full and items go to "overflow"
story:
Given F1 is full.
When a scientist puts a new box on top of the racks in F1, not in any rack, and scans it into "F1, loose".
Then the box is found under F1 but without a shelf or rack, and the box counts as "not properly stored" until moved.
real_life_noise: loose boxes slide to the back and freeze to the wall
people pick "F1" from a list without saying loose, and the box looks like it is in a rack
system_should: Allow a less exact place (just the freezer) and show how exact each place is. Report loose items per freezer.
question_it_answers: How full is each freezer, and what is stored loose?
cost_reason: Search time and slow freezer clutter
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action store_box, error store_loose p≈0.1 when freezer occupancy > 90%

title: Two people move the same box at nearly the same time
story:
Given box B20 is in F1.
When Ana scans it to the bench at 10:02:10 and Ben, who took it from Ana's bench, scans it to F3 at 10:02:40 on a different scanner.
Then the order is kept, and the current place is F3.
real_life_noise: Ben's scanner clock is a minute fast, so his scan looks earlier than Ana's
Ana's scan is sent twice because the app retried after a timeout
system_should: Each scan carries a unique id so retries are ignored. Close events from different devices are ordered by happened-at, with recorded-at used to break ties and to spot clock skew.
question_it_answers: Where is B20 now?
cost_reason: Rare, but shows whether event ordering is sound
sim_hook: Actor two scientists, action concurrent_move, p≈0.005 per box move; retry_duplicate p≈0.01 per scan

title: Plate taken off the robot deck but not scanned back to storage
story:
Given a 384-well sample plate is created on the liquid handler deck by a transfer task.
When the task ends and the plate is carried to the fridge, without a scan.
Then the system says it is still on the robot deck, position 4. The next run that needs deck position 4 finds a plate "there" on paper.
real_life_noise: the next run's load scan puts a different plate in deck position 4, displacing the old one
the plate is carried straight into the BLI instrument instead
system_should: Treat robot decks as places with positions. A new plate scanned into an occupied deck position pushes the old one to "location uncertain, last on deck 4". A daily report lists plates still "on the robot" after hours.
question_it_answers: What is really on the robot deck?
cost_reason: Lost plates of expressed protein have a two-week life; losing a day matters
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action unload_robot, error no_scan_after_run p≈0.2

title: Location tells the storage temperature, and that changes the expiry
story:
Given GFP stock buffer lasts 6 months frozen, but less in the fridge (from the brief).
When a tube of GFP stock moves from -20 freezer F3 to fridge K1.
Then its storage temperature comes from the place's set temperature, and the expiry rule switches from that moment.
real_life_noise: the fridge has no temperature set in the system
the move is recorded a day late (LOC-003), so the clock switch is a day late
the tube goes to a fridge shelf labelled "-20" because the shelf labels are old
system_should: Every storage place has a nominal temperature. Moves carry temperature changes into the expiry rules. Missing temperature on a place is shown, not assumed. (Details of the expiry rule belong to LIFE.)
question_it_answers: Is this still good, given where it has been?
cost_reason: Expired buffer used in a run looks fine on paper
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action move_between_temperatures, error late_record delay 0-24 h p≈0.1

title: Freezer drifts warm but nobody moves anything
story:
Given F4 was at -60 instead of -80 for 18 hours over a weekend (logged by the freezer monitor, assumption: a monitoring system exists).
When on Monday the lab records the excursion.
Then every container in F4 during that window gets the excursion attached, without anyone touching them one by one.
real_life_noise: two boxes were added to F4 during the window, and only those hours count for them
the monitor reading is noisy and the "real" excursion is disputed
system_should: Record the event on the place and work out which containers were there at the time from move history. Let a person decide whether it affects usability. (Usability rules are LIFE.)
question_it_answers: Which containers were in F4 when it was warm?
cost_reason: Damaged targets keep being used and cause failed experiments
sim_hook: Actor freezer_monitor, action excursion_event p≈0.1 per freezer per month, duration 1-24 h

title: Searching for a material, not a barcode
story:
Given Target X exists in 14 tubes across 3 freezers, plus 2 on the bench and 1 in the BLI instrument.
When a scientist asks "where is Target X I can use?".
Then the system lists the 14 usable tubes with place and slot, sorted so the oldest usable lot or the one already opened comes first, and the 3 out-of-storage tubes shown separately.
real_life_noise: 2 of the 14 are "last seen" over 6 months ago
one is in a box that is marked "in transit"
system_should: Answer "where" for a material by joining material, container and current place, and show the confidence for each (LOC-014).
question_it_answers: Where is the Target X I can actually use?
cost_reason: If the list is wrong people reorder target they already own
sim_hook: Query, not an event. Sim checks query result against ground truth.

title: Box barcode label falls off
story:
Given box B33's label was printed on paper and the glue failed in the -80.
When a scientist finds a box with no label.
Then they can identify it by rack-scanning or scanning a few tubes inside, and the system suggests "these tubes belong to B33", so a new label can be linked to B33.
real_life_noise: the tubes inside are from two different boxes
a new label is printed and given a new barcode, creating box B34 with the same tubes
system_should: Allow relabelling an existing container. When a box's contents are scanned, suggest the box whose recorded contents match best.
question_it_answers: Which box is this?
cost_reason: Friction plus a risk of a duplicate box record
sim_hook: Actor environment, action label_falls_off p≈0.002 per box per month; relabel_as_new p≈0.4

title: Plate stacker with plates in an unknown order
story:
Given a plate stacker on a plate reader holds 10 plates.
When a scientist loads them without scanning, and the reader scans each plate barcode as it pulls it in.
Then the reader's barcode log tells the order and puts each plate "in the reader stacker" for that run.
real_life_noise: the reader cannot read a barcode because the label is on the wrong side, and logs "NOREAD"
two plates go in upside down
system_should: Instrument barcode logs are another source of place events. A NOREAD is logged as an unknown plate at that stack position, to be matched by elimination.
question_it_answers: Which plates were on the reader in this run?
cost_reason: Wrong plate to data match ruins results for a whole plate
sim_hook: Actor instrument, action stacker_read, error noread p≈0.02 per plate

title: A container is disposed and its place must free up
story:
Given plate P-640 is in fridge K2, shelf 3.
When it is thrown away and scanned as disposed.
Then K2 shelf 3 no longer lists it, its last real place stays in history, and a later scan of P-640 warns that it was disposed.
real_life_noise: the plate is marked disposed but it is still in the fridge a week later
the plate is thrown away but nobody marks it, so the fridge "holds" it forever
system_should: Disposal is a move to "disposed", which is outside all storage. Scans of disposed containers raise a warning (see LOC-010 for the found-again case).
question_it_answers: Is this plate still in the lab?
cost_reason: The brief's own example, thrown-away plates that still look usable
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action dispose, error forget_dispose_scan p≈0.1, dispose_scan_but_kept p≈0.01

title: Scientist keeps a private box nobody else knows about
story:
Given Ana keeps a box of "her" target aliquots at the back of shelf 5, not registered.
When Ana leaves the company.
Then the system has no record of these tubes. A clean-up finds 30 unregistered tubes of an expensive target.
real_life_noise: some tubes were registered once, then moved to the private box without scans
labels are hand-written initials only
system_should: Make found-material registration fast, with an "owner unknown" option. Reports of containers whose owner has left help find these early.
question_it_answers: What do we hold that the system does not know about?
cost_reason: Unknown stock leads to needless reorders, and unknown-quality tubes used later
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action private_stash p≈0.01 per aliquot made, hidden from inventory until stock_take

title: Many tubes picked from one box for a task
story:
Given a target plate prep needs 8 different targets from boxes B1, B4 and B6.
When the scientist pulls all 8 tubes, uses them, and puts them back.
Then the system has a pick list with places, records each tube as out, and expects 8 scans back.
real_life_noise: 7 scanned back, 1 put back without a scan
two tubes put back in each other's slots
system_should: Offer a pick list sorted by freezer and box. After the task, show what is still out. Swaps in a box show up on the next rack scan.
question_it_answers: Did everything come back?
cost_reason: Lost or swapped target tubes are expensive
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action pick_and_return, error no_scan_return p≈0.05 per tube, swap_slots p≈0.01 per pair

title: Same physical tube, two records after a re-register
story:
Given tube T-7001 could not be found and was marked missing last month.
When it turns up, cannot be scanned (smudged label), and is registered again as new tube T-9050.
Then the lab holds one tube but the system has two records, one missing, one live.
real_life_noise: the "new" tube is given a new lot because nobody knew the old one
lineage from the original lot is lost
system_should: Allow two container records to be merged, with the merge as an event and the history kept on both. When registering found material, suggest matching missing containers (same material, volume, last place).
question_it_answers: Is this the same tube we lost?
cost_reason: Lineage breaks, so if the lot turns out bad this tube will not show up
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action register_found_unreadable, error re_register_as_new p≈0.5 of found-with-unreadable-label cases

title: Scan of a shelf to say "this is all there is"
story:
Given fridge K1 shelf 2 is recorded as holding 6 plates.
When a scientist scans all plates on that shelf and taps "this shelf is complete".
Then the 4 plates found stay, 2 plates not found go to "location uncertain", and 1 plate that was recorded elsewhere is moved to K1 shelf 2.
real_life_noise: one plate was hidden behind another and not scanned, so it is wrongly marked uncertain
the scientist taps "complete" by habit after scanning only some
system_should: Support "complete scan of a place" as a statement that nothing else is there. Missing ones become uncertain, not disposed. Keep the statement as evidence that can be wrong.
question_it_answers: What is on this shelf right now?
cost_reason: Fast cleanup of drift, but over-confident scans hide items
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action complete_place_scan, error missed_item p≈0.03 per item, false_complete p≈0.05 per scan

title: Loading buffer made on Monday expires the next Monday
story:
Given a scientist makes 50 mL of loading buffer on Monday 2026-10-19 at 10:00 from PBS lot P7 and a detergent lot D2, and puts it in the 4 °C fridge.
When the system is asked on Monday 2026-10-26 at 10:30 what loading buffer is usable.
Then this bottle shows as expired since 10:00 that morning (made plus 7 days), with the reason "expired", and it no longer counts in usable stock even though 30 mL is still in it.
real_life_noise: the bottle is registered on Tuesday because the scientist forgot, so the record says "made" a day late and the expiry is a day too generous
two bottles made on different days sit side by side with the same handwritten label "LB"
someone tops up an old bottle with freshly made buffer, so the bottle now holds a mix of two ages
the label on the bottle says "exp 27/10" in a European date format and a visiting student reads it as month 27
system_should: Start the clock from the time the buffer was made, not the time it was typed in, and keep both. Count the 7 days from the making event. When fresh buffer is poured into an old bottle, treat the result as the older age (the mix expires when its oldest part does). Show the date unambiguously, as text like "26 Oct 2026".
question_it_answers: Which loading buffer can I use today?
cost_reason: Old loading buffer can shift BLI baselines, so a whole run's data may need re-running
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_buffer(type=loading, volume=50 mL). Error late_registration with p≈0.15, delay drawn 2–30 h, recorded_at moves but happened_at should not. Error top_up_old_bottle with p≈0.05.

title: GFP stock buffer lasts 6 months frozen but only a month once kept in the fridge
story:
Given 10 tubes of GFP stock buffer made on 2026-06-01, stored at -20 °C, so each expires 2026-12-01.
When on 2026-10-21 a scientist takes one tube out and moves it to the 4 °C fridge to use over the next weeks.
Then that tube's expiry becomes the earlier of 2026-12-01 and 2026-11-20 (one month in the fridge, Assumption), so 2026-11-20. The 9 tubes still in the freezer keep 2026-12-01.
real_life_noise: the tube is moved but not scanned, so the system thinks it is still frozen and keeps the 6-month date
the tube goes back into the freezer after a week; nobody is sure if the clock should reset
all 10 tubes share one barcode on the rack instead of one each
system_should: Work out expiry from the storage history, not from one fixed field. Each storage condition has its own lifetime, and moving to a warmer condition can only bring the date closer, never push it further away. Putting the tube back in the freezer does not give the lost time back. If a container has no scan for a long time, show its expiry as uncertain rather than trusting the last known place.
question_it_answers: Is this GFP buffer still good, given where it has been?
cost_reason: A degraded GFP buffer gives wrong concentration numbers, which feed sample normalisation
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action move(container, freezer_-20 -> fridge_4). Error unscanned_move with p≈0.10. Follow-up action move(fridge -> freezer) with p≈0.3 within 3–14 days.

title: Expression plate expires 2 weeks after expression
story:
Given an expression plate whose expression run finished on 2026-10-07 at 16:00, stored at 4 °C.
When on 2026-10-21 at 17:00 someone plans a re-run of BLI sample plate prep from it.
Then the plate and all 96 protein wells show expired since 16:00 that day, and the planner sees "expired" as the reason they are not usable.
real_life_noise: the expression run was recorded as started, not finished, so the clock begins 18 h early
the plate was frozen at -80 °C on day 3 by a scientist who wanted to keep it longer (Assumption, labs do this)
4 wells were already pulled for a split-GFP plate and are near empty
system_should: Start the 2-week clock when the protein exists, which is the end of the expression run. Expire every well with the plate since each well is its own material but they share one making event. If the plate was frozen, keep the 2-week rule unless the lab has said frozen expression plates have a different lifetime. The system should not invent a longer one.
question_it_answers: Can this re-run still use the original expression plate, or do we need to express again?
cost_reason: Re-expressing takes days and DNA; using old protein gives bad binding data delivered to a customer
sim_hook: Actor robot, action expression_run(end_time). Error record_start_not_end with p≈0.05. Actor scientist, action rerun_request on plate with age drawn 5–20 days.

title: GFP and BLI plates are thrown away right after the run
story:
Given a split-GFP plate and two BLI sample plates and one BLI target plate are used in runs that end on 2026-10-21 at 14:00.
When the runs are recorded as finished.
Then the plates are marked as used up and disposed of, the material left inside them stops counting as usable, and the target protein left in the target plate wells is recorded as lost, not as still in stock.
real_life_noise: the run finishes but nobody scans the plates into the waste, so they stay "in instrument" for days
a scientist keeps one BLI target plate in the fridge "in case we need to re-read it" and it is reused the next day
the instrument aborts at well 60; plates are reused for a second attempt
system_should: Make "disposed after use" a rule of the plate type, so ending the run is enough to retire them even if nobody scans the bin. Still allow a recorded exception, like an aborted run, where the plate is kept on purpose and gets a short life (Assumption: 24 h at 4 °C). Count the lost target volume, because the target is expensive and that loss is part of how much each experiment costs.
question_it_answers: How much target did that run actually consume, including what was left in the plate?
cost_reason: Used plates that look usable get picked for re-runs; target loss is invisible otherwise
sim_hook: Actor robot, action finish_bli_run. Auto-dispose event follows. Error plate_kept_for_reuse with p≈0.03, abort_mid_run with p≈0.02.

title: Target stock in the freezer lasts years, but only within the supplier's own expiry
story:
Given Target X lot L1 arrives on 2026-03-01 with a certificate of analysis (the supplier's quality sheet) saying "use by 2027-03-01 when stored at -80 °C".
When it is reconstituted, QC'd, split into tubes and stored at -80 °C.
Then the tubes show expiry 2027-03-01, the earlier of the supplier date and our own "many years" rule.
real_life_noise: the certificate is a PDF in an email and the use-by date is never typed in
the certificate gives "stable 12 months from date of receipt" instead of a date
the supplier sends an updated certificate months later with a longer date
system_should: Keep the supplier's date as a separate limit on the lot, alongside our own rule, and use the earliest. Accept relative rules (12 months from receipt) and turn them into a date using the receiving event. If no supplier date was entered, show that as missing data, not as "never expires".
question_it_answers: When does this target lot expire, and why that date?
cost_reason: Using a target past the supplier date risks customer data; throwing away good target costs money
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action receive_lot with coa. Error coa_expiry_missing with p≈0.25. Coa format drawn: absolute date 60%, relative 30%, none 10%.

title: Expiry starts from manufacture, from opening, or from making, depending on the material
story:
Given three things arrive or are made the same week: a bottle of PBS powder (expires 3 years from the manufacture date on the label), a bottle of detergent stock (good for 6 months once opened, Assumption), and a buffer made in-house (1 month from making).
When each is checked on 2026-10-21.
Then each one's expiry uses its own start event: the label date, the first-opening event, and the making event.
real_life_noise: nobody records when the detergent was opened; the bottle has "opened 3/9" scribbled on it
a sealed bottle is opened, then a second sealed bottle of the same lot is opened by someone else a month later
the supplier label has only a lot number and the manufacture date must be looked up on their site
system_should: Let each material type say which event starts its clock (manufacture, receipt, opening, making, thawing). Store opening as an event on the container. If the start event is missing, use the earliest safe guess (receipt date) and mark the expiry as estimated.
question_it_answers: Why does this bottle expire on that date?
cost_reason: Mostly cheap reagents, but a bad component spoils every buffer made from it
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action open_container. Error forget_open_event with p≈0.4 for consumable reagents, which is the common real case.

title: A made buffer cannot outlive its components
story:
Given PBS lot P7 expires 2026-10-30 and a buffer is made from it on 2026-10-20 with a 1-month rule (would be 2026-11-20).
When the buffer's expiry is worked out.
Then it shows 2026-10-30 plus a warning, or 2026-11-20 with a note, depending on the lab's rule for that buffer type. Our default: the earliest component expiry caps it (Assumption).
real_life_noise: the PBS was already expired on the day of making and the scientist used it anyway
the component lot was not scanned, so the system does not know which PBS went in
system_should: Carry each component's expiry into the made material, and make the cap rule a setting of the material type. If a component was already expired when used, record that and flag the new buffer, but do not block the making event, since it already happened at the bench.
question_it_answers: Was anything made from an expired component?
cost_reason: Buffer is cheap but silently bad buffer is hard to trace later
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_buffer with components. Error use_expired_component with p≈0.04, skip_component_scan with p≈0.1.

title: Target aliquot is thawed, used, and refrozen; freeze-thaw count goes up
story:
Given a 24 µL tube of Target X lot L1 at -80 °C with 0 freeze-thaw cycles, and a limit of 3 cycles for this target (Assumption, many protein suppliers say "avoid repeated freeze-thaw" and some state 3).
When a scientist takes it out at 09:00, thaws it on ice, uses 10 µL for a BLI target plate, and puts it back at -80 °C at 11:30.
Then the tube has 14 µL left and 1 freeze-thaw cycle, still usable.
real_life_noise: the tube is put back without a scan, so the system never sees the cycle
the scientist takes 3 tubes out, uses one, and puts all 3 back; the 2 unused ones also had a cycle
the tube is placed on the bench, not on ice, for 2.5 h
system_should: Count a cycle from the pair of events "left the freezer" and "came back", not from a number someone types. Unused tubes taken out and returned also get a cycle. If the return was not scanned but the tube is later seen in the freezer, infer a cycle and mark it as inferred.
question_it_answers: How many times has this target tube been thawed?
cost_reason: Damaged target gives weak or no binding signal, so customer results look negative when they are not
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action thaw(container) then refreeze(container). Error no_scan_on_return with p≈0.12. Error take_extra_tubes with p≈0.08, extra count 1–3.

title: Fourth thaw goes past the limit
story:
Given a target tube with 3 freeze-thaw cycles already, limit 3.
When a scientist thaws it again at 10:00 for a re-run.
Then the system shows the tube as "over freeze-thaw limit". It does not stop the scientist (the thaw already happened), but the tube leaves usable stock and any plate made from it is flagged.
real_life_noise: there is no other tube of the lot, so the scientist uses it anyway with a note
a lead scientist decides this target is fine up to 5 cycles and changes the limit for the lot
system_should: Keep the limit on the material type with a possible override on the lot, and record who changed it and why. Flag downstream plates instead of blocking. A plate made from an over-limit tube should be traceable later, so if binding looks odd someone can find the cause.
question_it_answers: Did any of our results use a tube past its freeze-thaw limit?
cost_reason: Bad data delivered to a customer with no way to explain it later
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action thaw on tube with cycles>=limit. Choice use_anyway with p≈0.6 when no other tube exists, else p≈0.1. Actor lead, action override_limit with p≈0.05.

title: Thawed target kept in the fridge has a short life of its own
story:
Given a target tube thawed on 2026-10-20 at 09:00 and kept at 4 °C for use over the week instead of being refrozen.
When on 2026-10-27 at 10:00 someone wants to use it.
Then it shows expired since 2026-10-27 09:00, because thawed target at 4 °C lasts 7 days (Assumption, a common supplier statement for reconstituted proteins), even though the lot itself is good until 2027.
real_life_noise: it is unclear whether the tube was refrozen on day 2 and thawed again
the fridge holds three thawed tubes of the same lot; people use whichever is at the front
system_should: Let thawing start a new, shorter clock on the container while the lot's long expiry stays the same. The container's expiry is the earliest of its clocks. The same lot can be usable in one tube and expired in another.
question_it_answers: Which tube of this target lot should I use first?
cost_reason: Using an old thawed tube wastes a BLI run; throwing out a fresh one wastes expensive target
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action thaw then move(fridge_4) without refreeze, p≈0.3 of thaws. Later actor picks a random tube from fridge rather than oldest, p≈0.5.

title: Target tube left on the bench overnight
story:
Given a target tube thawed at 16:00 on Tuesday for a BLI target plate.
When a scientist finds it on the bench at 08:30 Wednesday, 16.5 hours at room temperature (about 22 °C).
Then the scientist records "left out overnight", and the tube is put on hold (not usable) until someone decides: throw it away or keep it with a note.
real_life_noise: the finder does not know when it was left; last scan was the thaw at 16:00
nobody records anything and the tube goes back to the freezer looking normal
the tube is unlabelled, so the finder guesses from the cap colour
system_should: Support an "on hold" status with a reason, separate from expired. A hold is set by a person and lifted by a person, and both are recorded. Use the last scan to say how long it might have been out (at most 16.5 h here). If the tube was never put back, its state should eventually show up as "out of storage for a long time".
question_it_answers: Which containers are on hold, and why?
cost_reason: Degraded target silently used in a run, or a whole tube thrown out by mistake
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action thaw then forget_return with p≈0.02 per thaw. Finder actor records left_out with p≈0.6, otherwise silent refreeze.

title: Freezer warms up over the weekend
story:
Given freezer F2 (-80 °C) holds 240 target tubes and 12 DNA plates.
When the freezer's monitor shows it rose to -40 °C from Saturday 02:00 to Saturday 09:00, then to -15 °C by Sunday 07:00, before someone moved everything to F3 on Sunday at 08:00.
Then every container whose last known place was F2 at that time gets an "excursion" record with the peak temperature and duration, and target tubes go on hold. DNA plates stay usable (DNA tolerates this much better, Assumption).
real_life_noise: some containers were moved to F3 without being scanned during the rescue
two boxes were in F2 according to the system but were actually in F1
the monitor log has a 3-hour gap
a scientist puts everything back into F2 on Monday after the repair, again without scanning
system_should: Record the excursion once, on the storage place, with start, end and peak. Work out which containers were affected from where they were during that time window, not where they are now. Let each material type say how much excursion it tolerates. Hold the affected ones until someone reviews, and keep a list that can be worked through.
question_it_answers: What was in the freezer when it failed, and what can we still use?
cost_reason: Hundreds of expensive target tubes; either using damaged ones or reordering everything
sim_hook: Actor environment, action temperature_excursion(place, start, end, peak), p≈1 per freezer per year. Rescue actor moves containers, error unscanned_move with p≈0.3 under time pressure.

title: Fridge door left open for 40 minutes
story:
Given the buffer fridge reaches 12 °C for 40 minutes on a Thursday afternoon.
When the excursion is logged.
Then nothing changes status, because buffers tolerate short warm-ups (Assumption), but the excursion is stored and visible on each container's history.
real_life_noise: the door alarm is muted and nobody logs it; only the monitor CSV shows it
someone logs it twice, once from the alarm and once by hand
system_should: Store small excursions too, but let the material rules decide they change nothing. Merge duplicate reports that cover the same place and time. A record with no action taken is still useful later if a buffer behaves oddly.
question_it_answers: Has this buffer ever been out of its storage range?
cost_reason: Usually nothing happens; noise if every small event put things on hold
sim_hook: Actor environment, action temperature_excursion small, p≈0.1 per fridge per week. Error duplicate_report with p≈0.2.

title: Lead scientist re-checks an expired target lot and extends it
story:
Given Target Y lot L4 expired by our rule on 2026-10-01, with 600 µL left across 25 tubes.
When a scientist runs a QC check (a test binding with a known reference) on one tube on 2026-10-15, it passes, and the lead extends the lot's expiry to 2027-04-15.
Then all 25 tubes are usable again, the old expiry stays in the history, and the extension is linked to the QC result and the person who approved it.
real_life_noise: the extension is entered on only the tube that was tested, not the lot
three of the tubes have had 4 thaws and should not be extended even though the lot is
the re-QC tube was taken from a different lot by mistake
system_should: Extend at the lot level, with a link to the QC event, but keep container-level limits (thaws, holds, excursions) in force. Never edit the old expiry; add a new one that takes over from a date. Check that the QC'd tube belongs to the lot being extended.
question_it_answers: Why is this target usable when its date passed?
cost_reason: Target is expensive, so extending saves money, but extending the wrong lot puts bad data out
sim_hook: Actor lead, action extend_expiry(lot, qc_event). Error extend_container_not_lot with p≈0.2. Error qc_on_wrong_lot with p≈0.02.

title: Re-QC fails, lot is retired with material still inside
story:
Given the same expired lot as LIFE-014, but the re-check shows weak binding.
When the lead marks the lot as failed on 2026-10-15.
Then all 25 tubes stop being usable with reason "QC failed", but they still exist in the freezer until someone throws them away, and the 600 µL is shown as held but not usable.
real_life_noise: tubes are thrown away weeks later in one go, and only some are scanned into the bin
one tube was already lent to another team and is not in the freezer
system_should: Separate "failed" (a state of the lot) from "disposed" (something that happened to each container). Let the bulk disposal be recorded and show which tubes are still physically somewhere.
question_it_answers: What do we hold that is failed but not thrown away yet?
cost_reason: Failed tubes picked by mistake; freezer space wasted
sim_hook: Actor lead, action fail_lot. Later actor scientist, action dispose_batch with p_scan_each≈0.7.

title: Material expires in the middle of a run
story:
Given a BLI run starts at 22:00 on Sunday 2026-10-25 and runs 6 hours. The loading buffer in the instrument was made 2026-10-18 at 23:00, so it expires at 23:00 on 2026-10-25.
When the run finishes at 04:00.
Then the run record says the buffer was usable when the run started and expired during it. The system marks the run with a warning, not an error, and the lab decides whether the data stands.
real_life_noise: the run is queued on Friday and nobody checks expiry at queue time
the robot has a 2-hour delay before start, which pushes the start past expiry
system_should: Check usability at the time the material was actually used (the transfer time), not at the time of planning or of typing in. Have a clear rule for "expired during the run" and store which rule was applied. Our default is: usable at the moment of transfer is fine; flag if expiry falls inside the run window.
question_it_answers: Were all materials in date when this run used them?
cost_reason: Questioning valid data or keeping invalid data; both annoy customers
sim_hook: Actor robot, action bli_run with queue_delay drawn 0–4 h. Expiry check at transfer time. Rate of mid-run expiry arises naturally from buffer ages.

title: Plate thrown away with protein still in the wells, on purpose
story:
Given an expression plate with about 80 µL left per well after sample plates were made, 10 days old.
When the scientist decides the project is done and throws it away, scanning the plate into the bin.
Then the plate and all its wells are disposed, and the 96 × 80 µL is recorded as discarded, not consumed by any run.
real_life_noise: the scientist does not know how much was left and records 0
the customer asks for a re-run three days later
system_should: Record disposal with the remaining amount, even an estimated one, and a reason (project done, expired, contaminated, broken). Keep discarded separate from consumed so cost and usage reports stay honest. When a re-run is requested later, say clearly that the plate is gone.
question_it_answers: How much did we throw away rather than use?
cost_reason: Waste is invisible; re-run planning trusts a plate that no longer exists
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action dispose(container, reason, remaining). Error remaining_recorded_zero with p≈0.3.

title: Wrong plate thrown away by accident
story:
Given two expression plates of similar age sit on the same fridge shelf, one finished (EP-0412) and one still needed (EP-0415).
When a scientist throws away EP-0415 and scans EP-0412 into the bin.
Then the system says EP-0412 is gone and EP-0415 is still in the fridge, which is the opposite of the truth, until someone finds EP-0412 still on the shelf.
real_life_noise: the mistake is found only when a robot fails to find EP-0415 two days later
the disposal is corrected but the bin was emptied already
system_should: Let a disposal be reversed by a new correction event, keeping both in the history. When a container marked disposed is scanned again in a real place, flag it loudly. Support "lost" as a separate state for EP-0415 once it can't be found.
question_it_answers: What did the record say before the correction, and who changed it?
cost_reason: A needed plate is gone and re-expression costs days; the record points people to the wrong thing
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action dispose, error scan_neighbour with p≈0.01 when two similar containers share a shelf. Discovery after 1–3 days via robot not_found.

title: Tube thrown away by accident with lots of target in it
story:
Given a 200 µL tube of an expensive target sits on the bench with a "done" pile of empty tubes.
When a cleaner or colleague clears the bench at 18:00 and it goes to the biohazard bin unscanned.
Then the system still shows the tube as on the bench. Days later a scientist searches for it, cannot find it, and marks it lost, then later "disposed (likely)".
real_life_noise: nobody knows for sure it was thrown away; it might be in another fridge
planning already counted the 200 µL as available for a re-run next week
system_should: Keep "lost" separate from "disposed" and from "usable". A lost container should stop counting as usable right away but stay findable if it turns up. Flag containers on the bench that haven't been scanned in more than a day.
question_it_answers: Is this target really available, or is it just in the record?
cost_reason: Expensive target; a planned run fails on the day
sim_hook: Actor other_person, action clear_bench, error dispose_unscanned with p≈0.005 per bench container per day. Finder marks lost after search with p≈0.8.

title: Empty-looking tube thrown away still has 6 µL
story:
Given a target tube whose record says 6 µL left, below the 10 µL a pipette can get out reliably (Assumption).
When a scientist throws it away as empty.
Then the 6 µL is recorded as dead volume discarded, and the tube's record closes at zero.
real_life_noise: the scientist records it as "empty" and the 6 µL disappears from the books
the record actually said 30 µL because earlier draws were not recorded
system_should: On disposal, close the container's balance with an explicit "discarded" entry equal to what the record said was left. If that is large, ask for a reason, since it often means earlier use was never recorded.
question_it_answers: Where did the missing target go?
cost_reason: Small amounts each, but a pattern hints at missing records
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action dispose(remaining=record). Error unrecorded_draw earlier with p≈0.05 per use, showing up here as a large discarded amount.

title: Target tubes sent to a partner lab
story:
Given Target X lot L1 with 20 tubes in our freezer.
When on 2026-10-21 we ship 5 tubes on dry ice to a partner lab for a joint study, with a courier tracking number.
Then those 5 tubes leave our usable stock and our lab, but they stay in the history with the destination and date, and the lot still links to them.
real_life_noise: the shipment is delayed and the tubes sit in the dispatch fridge at 4 °C for a day
the partner returns 2 unused tubes a month later
only the box is scanned, not the tubes inside
system_should: Record "left the lab" as an event with destination, rather than deleting the containers. If tubes come back, treat them as returning with an unknown storage history (on hold until checked), not as if they never left. Scanning a box should move its contents with it.
question_it_answers: Where did this lot go, including outside the lab?
cost_reason: If the lot turns out bad, the partner must be told
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action ship(containers, destination). Error scan_box_only with p≈0.5. Return event p≈0.1 within 60 days.

title: Leftover protein sent back to the customer
story:
Given a customer asked to get back the leftover expressed proteins after their binding results.
When the scientist copies 40 µL per well from the expression plate into a new shipping plate and sends it on 2026-10-21.
Then the shipping plate is recorded as a new container that left the lab to "Customer C", with each well linked to its source well, and the expression plate keeps whatever is left.
real_life_noise: the whole expression plate is shipped instead of a copy, so the original is gone
the customer's well layout differs, so a mapping file is needed
system_should: Treat it like any transfer followed by a shipment. Keep the well-to-well link so the customer's question "which well is my design 34" can be answered later.
question_it_answers: What exactly did we send to this customer?
cost_reason: Customer confusion, wrong proteins tested on their side
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action transfer_plate then ship(customer). Error ship_original_not_copy with p≈0.1.

title: DNA plate moved to a second site
story:
Given Adaptyv opens a second site (Assumption, as the lab grows) and a reconstituted DNA plate must move there.
When it is shipped frozen and scanned in at the other site 30 hours later.
Then the plate is still ours, its location changes to the second site's freezer, and the transit time is recorded. Nothing in its lifetime changes for DNA.
real_life_noise: the receiving site scans it in, but the sending site never scanned it out
the dry ice ran out in transit and it arrived at about 0 °C
system_should: Treat a site as just another top-level place, so a move between sites is a move, not leaving and re-entering. Record transit as a place with no temperature guarantee. If arrival temperature is noted as off, it is an excursion like any other.
question_it_answers: Where is this DNA plate, across all our sites?
cost_reason: DNA is slow and costly to reorder
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action ship_internal(site_b). Error no_scan_out with p≈0.3. Error transit_excursion with p≈0.05.

title: DNA stored for years is still fine, but this freezer has had two failures
story:
Given a DNA plate from 2022, stored at -20 °C, with two recorded freezer excursions since then.
When someone wants to re-express a design from it in 2026.
Then it is usable by date ("many years"), and the history shows the two excursions so the scientist can decide whether to check it first.
real_life_noise: the plate moved freezers three times and one move was never recorded
the DNA has been thawed 9 times for different re-expressions
system_should: For long-lived material, the date alone says little, so show the history summary: number of thaws, excursions, places. Do not invent an expiry; "no expiry set" should be clear and not mistaken for "unknown".
question_it_answers: Can we trust this old DNA plate?
cost_reason: Bad DNA means failed expression and a wasted week
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action reuse_old_dna with plate age 1–5 years. Thaw count grows by 1 per reuse.

title: Tip boxes have no expiry but run out
story:
Given a rack of 96-tip boxes is used by the liquid handling robot.
When the robot uses 3 boxes per expression plate prep and 30 boxes are left on the shelf.
Then the system shows 30 boxes, no expiry, and how many plate preps that covers (10).
real_life_noise: a half-used box is put back on the shelf and counted as full
a box is dropped and its tips are unusable
a delivery of 20 boxes is registered as 20 cases of 10
system_should: Count consumables by unit, with a pack size so "cases" and "boxes" don't get mixed up. Allow a partial box. No expiry is a normal state for these, not missing data.
question_it_answers: How many tip boxes do we have, and when do we run out?
cost_reason: Running out stops the robot for a day; cheap otherwise
sim_hook: Actor robot, action consume_tip_box per plate prep. Error partial_box_counted_full with p≈0.05. Receive error pack_size_confusion with p≈0.03.

title: BLI sensor tray regenerated a few times, then retired
story:
Given a tray of 96 Protein A biosensors (the dip-in tips used to measure binding on a BLI instrument) is used in a run.
When after the run the sensors are regenerated (stripped with a low-pH glycine solution so they can be reused), and this happens 4 times.
Then the tray shows 4 regenerations. With a limit of 5 for this sensor type (Assumption, suppliers say several cycles depending on the target), one more use is allowed, then it is retired.
real_life_noise: regeneration is done inside the run program, so nobody records it separately
a tray is reused without regeneration because the next run is the same target
two half-used trays are combined into one
system_should: Track uses and regenerations as a count on the consumable container, with a limit on the type. Because regeneration is part of the run method, let the run record it automatically. When trays are combined, keep the highest count, to stay on the safe side.
question_it_answers: Can we use this sensor tray again?
cost_reason: Worn sensors give lower signal; sensors are costly to throw away early
sim_hook: Actor robot, action bli_run with regenerate step. Error manual_reuse_unrecorded with p≈0.1. Retirement when count>limit.

title: A sensor that held a bad target lot must not be reused
story:
Given a BLI sensor tray loaded with Target Y lot L4, which later fails QC.
When the team looks back at what lot L4 touched.
Then the sensor tray appears in the list, and if it was regenerated and reused, the runs that followed are flagged too, because some target may remain on the sensor.
real_life_noise: sensor trays have no barcode, only a label on the box
system_should: Treat reusable consumables as containers that held material, so they show up in "what did this lot touch". Mark carry-over risk on later runs that reused them.
question_it_answers: What did this bad target lot touch?
cost_reason: Hidden carry-over spoils data that otherwise looks clean
sim_hook: Actor lead, action fail_lot after use. Query trace includes sensor trays, error tray_without_barcode with p≈0.3.
