title: First small molecule arrives, dissolved in DMSO, light-sensitive
story:
Given the lab starts testing a small molecule (a drug-like compound, not a protein) as a binding partner.
When 5 mg of powder arrives, is dissolved to 10 mM in DMSO (a common solvent for these), split into 20 × 20 µL tubes in amber (light-blocking) tubes, and stored at -20 °C.
Then the system has a new material type "small molecule" with its own rules: powder 2 years at room temperature dry, DMSO stock 6 months at -20 °C (Assumption, a common rule of thumb), max 5 freeze-thaw cycles, must be kept dark.
real_life_noise: the powder's amount is by mass (mg) and the stock is by volume and concentration; someone records µL as mg
a tube is put in a clear rack under the bench light for a day
DMSO freezes at about 18.5 °C, so tubes in a cold room look frozen and people think they are thawed when they are not
system_should: Add the new type with rows and settings, not new tables. Handle units properly: mass for powder, volume plus concentration for the stock. Let a type carry conditions like "keep dark" that can be broken and recorded like a temperature excursion.
question_it_answers: Can the model take a new kind of material without a schema change?
cost_reason: Shows whether the model scales; compounds are cheap but data from bad ones is not
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action register_material_type(small_molecule, rules). Error unit_mismatch with p≈0.05. Action light_exposure event with p≈0.02 per day on bench.

title: DMSO stock left open absorbs water
story:
Given a 10 mM DMSO stock tube of compound C1.
When it sits uncapped on the bench for 3 hours in humid weather while a plate is set up.
Then the scientist records "left open", the tube's concentration is now uncertain (DMSO pulls water from the air, which dilutes the stock and can make the compound fall out of solution), and it goes on hold.
real_life_noise: nobody records it; it shows up later as a weaker dose response
system_should: Let material-type rules list conditions that put a container on hold (open time for DMSO stocks, light for light-sensitive). Mark concentration as "uncertain" rather than changing the number.
question_it_answers: Is this stock's concentration still what the label says?
cost_reason: Wrong concentration gives wrong binding numbers
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action leave_open(duration). Recorded with p≈0.3. Hidden effect on simulated measurement.

title: The lab changes a lifetime rule; what happens to what's already on the shelf
story:
Given loading buffer's lifetime is 1 week, and 6 bottles exist.
When on 2026-10-21 the lead shortens it to 5 days after seeing drift in BLI baselines.
Then the 6 bottles' expiry is worked out again under the new rule from today, and the history shows both the old and the new date with the rule change as the reason. Runs done before today stay judged under the old rule.
real_life_noise: someone edits the rule to "5" without units, meaning 5 days, but the field was in weeks
a rule is changed for one bottle by mistake instead of the type
system_should: Version the lifetime rules with a start date, so any past question ("was this usable on 10 Oct?") uses the rule in force then. Store units with numbers.
question_it_answers: Was this buffer usable on the day of that run, by the rules of that day?
cost_reason: Changing past answers silently breaks audits
sim_hook: Actor lead, action update_lifetime_rule. Error unit_mistake with p≈0.05.

title: What expires in the next 14 days, by the right clock
story:
Given a mix: 3 loading buffer bottles (1 week rule), 2 expression plates (2 weeks), 1 GFP buffer tube moved to the fridge (1 month cap), 4 thawed target tubes at 4 °C (7 days), and target lots with supplier dates in 10 days.
When someone asks on 2026-10-21 what expires by 2026-11-04.
Then each shows with its expiry date and which rule set it (made plus 7 days, thawed plus 7 days, supplier date, and so on), sorted by date.
real_life_noise: some items have no expiry because a start event is missing
some are on hold already and should be listed separately
system_should: Answer with the date and the reason for each. Show "unknown expiry" items in their own group, not hidden. Leave out items already disposed.
question_it_answers: What expires soon, and why?
cost_reason: Missed expiry wastes material or spoils runs
sim_hook: Daily query by scientist actor; checks against the sim's own true expiry to measure how often the system disagrees.

title: Supplier recalls a lot after we've used it
story:
Given supplier lot S9 of a buffer component was used in 4 buffers over 3 weeks, and those buffers in 30 runs.
When the supplier emails a recall on 2026-10-21 saying S9 may be contaminated.
Then the lot is marked "recalled", every container still holding S9 or anything made from it goes on hold, and the 30 runs are listed for review.
real_life_noise: the recall names a lot number with a typo, matching no lot exactly
one buffer was made from a mix of S9 and S10 and nobody recorded the split
system_should: Follow the made-from links down to all descendants. Holding is automatic; disposal is a separate decision. If the lot number doesn't match, show close matches instead of silently doing nothing.
question_it_answers: What did this recalled lot end up in?
cost_reason: Contaminated reagent in customer data
sim_hook: Actor supplier, action recall(lot) with p≈0.01 per lot. Error lot_number_typo with p≈0.1.

title: Plate in the instrument longer than planned
story:
Given BLI sample plates are loaded in the instrument at 25 °C (Assumption, BLI instruments usually hold plates at a set temperature) for a run planned for 4 hours.
When the instrument errors and the plates stay inside overnight, 14 hours in total.
Then the plates are thrown away by rule, but if someone wants to use them for a retry, the system shows they've been at 25 °C for 14 hours and warns.
real_life_noise: instrument does not report the error; plate is only found next morning
scientist retries with the same plates to save expression time
system_should: Count time in the instrument as time at the instrument's temperature. Allow the retry, with a warning that is stored on the new run.
question_it_answers: How long has this plate been sitting at room temperature?
cost_reason: Evaporation and protein loss lead to poor data
sim_hook: Actor robot, action instrument_hang with p≈0.01 per run, duration 6–16 h. Retry choice p≈0.5.

title: Evaporation in a plate over days in the fridge
story:
Given an expression plate sealed with foil, stored at 4 °C, record says 100 µL per well.
When after 9 days the seal is found partly peeled at one corner and edge wells have about 70 µL.
Then the scientist records a volume correction for the affected wells, with reason "evaporation", and the history keeps the old numbers.
real_life_noise: correction done for the whole plate with an average instead of per well
nobody checks and the robot aspirates air at the edges
system_should: Support a correction that applies to some wells, with a reason. Corrections are new entries, not edits of the old amount.
question_it_answers: Why does the robot not find the volume the system promised?
cost_reason: A few wells give bad data; robot errors
sim_hook: Actor environment, action evaporate(plate, edge_wells, rate) with p≈0.1 per plate per week when seal_quality is poor.

title: Container expired but people want to use it for a test run
story:
Given an expired loading buffer bottle and an expired expression plate.
When a scientist uses them for an instrument check run that produces no customer data.
Then the system lets this through, recording "used while expired, purpose: test", and the run is marked as not for customer data.
real_life_noise: the test run's data ends up in the customer report by accident
system_should: Allow use of expired material with a reason, rather than blocking. Keep that flag on everything made in the run so it shows up if someone later tries to use that data or material for real.
question_it_answers: Which runs used expired material, and why?
cost_reason: Blocking frustrates people into not recording; not flagging lets expired material leak into results
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action use_expired_with_reason, p≈0.02 of runs.

title: Daylight saving switch shifts an expiry by an hour
story:
Given a loading buffer made on Saturday 2026-10-24 at 02:30 Swiss time (Assumption, Adaptyv is in Lausanne), with a 7-day rule.
When clocks go back on Sunday 2026-10-25.
Then expiry is 2026-10-31 at 02:30 local time, with times stored in UTC underneath so the 7 days are exact.
real_life_noise: the robot's clock was not changed and logs times one hour off for a week
system_should: Store times in UTC and show local time. Keep the device clock offset in mind when a robot's times disagree with scans.
question_it_answers: Exactly when does this buffer expire?
cost_reason: An hour rarely matters, but wrong clocks confuse audit trails
sim_hook: Actor robot, error clock_offset +1 h for 7 days after DST switch with p≈0.3.

title: Expired material keeps taking up freezer space
story:
Given 120 containers that expired more than 90 days ago are still in freezers.
When a lab manager asks for a clean-out list.
Then the system lists them by place (freezer, shelf, box), with a total count per freezer, so someone can clear them in one pass and scan each into the bin.
real_life_noise: a third of them are not where the record says
someone throws away a whole box without scanning each tube
system_should: Support disposing a box and everything recorded inside it in one action, and list what the record said was inside so leftovers can be found.
question_it_answers: What can we throw away to free freezer space?
cost_reason: Clutter makes finding the right tube harder
sim_hook: Actor lab_manager, action cleanout(place) monthly. Error dispose_box_unscanned_contents with p≈0.4.

title: Target bought as a finished frozen protein vs. made in-house have different rules
story:
Given Target Z is usually bought from a supplier (QC'd, many years at -80 °C) but this time is expressed in-house as lot IH-3.
When IH-3 is made on 2026-10-10.
Then it gets the in-house rules: QC needed before use, and a lifetime the lab sets for in-house target (Assumption: 1 year at -80 °C until we know more).
real_life_noise: IH-3 is recorded under the supplier lot's name, so it inherits a supplier expiry
system_should: Rules depend on the material type and the source (bought or made), not only the material name. Keep the lot's source explicit.
question_it_answers: Where did this target lot come from, and which rules apply to it?
cost_reason: Wrong expiry on an in-house target that has less stability data
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action express_target_in_house with p≈0.1 of target lots. Error register_under_supplier_lot with p≈0.05.

title: Buffer made with the wrong date on the label
story:
Given a scientist makes GFP buffer on 2026-10-21 but writes 2026-01-21 on the tubes and in the record.
When the system works out expiry.
Then it shows these tubes as expiring 2026-07-21, so already expired. Someone notices, corrects the made date, and the expiry moves to 2027-04-21.
real_life_noise: the error is caught only when someone tries to throw the "expired" tubes away
system_should: Warn when a made date is far from the time it was typed in. Allow correcting the made date with a reason, recalculating expiry, and keeping the history.
question_it_answers: Why did this buffer's expiry change?
cost_reason: Good buffer thrown out or bad buffer kept
sim_hook: Actor scientist, action make_buffer, error wrong_date (month typo) with p≈0.01.

title: SPR chip reused across runs, with a cycle count
story:
Given the lab also runs SPR (another binding method that uses a sensor chip with the target fixed on its surface), and one chip holds Target X lot L1.
When the chip is used for 6 runs over 3 days, stored at 4 °C in between.
Then the chip shows its uses, the target lot on it, and its age, and after a set number of uses or days (Assumption, 7 days at 4 °C) it is retired.
real_life_noise: chip is moved between two instruments and the count resets in someone's head
system_should: Treat the chip as a container that holds target with its own clock and use count, like a sensor tray. Link it to the target lot for tracing.
question_it_answers: Is this chip still good, and what target is on it?
cost_reason: Chips are costly; a worn chip gives poor data
sim_hook: Actor robot, action spr_run(chip). Use count grows; error count_not_recorded with p≈0.1.

title: How much Target X do we hold, and how much of it can we actually use?
story:
Given Target X sits in 14 tubes across two lots. Lot L1 passed QC; lot L2 arrived yesterday and has not been QC'd. Two L1 tubes are past their expiry and one is marked discarded but still has volume on record.
When a scientist asks "how much Target X do we have?"
Then the answer comes in two numbers, held and usable, plus a breakdown of the gap: so many µL waiting for QC, so many µL expired, so many µL in discarded containers. The usable number counts only QC-passed, unexpired, not-discarded, not-quarantined material, minus dead volume that can't be pipetted out.
real_life_noise: one tube has a negative balance because a transfer was recorded twice
a tube with 2 µL left is technically held but nobody can get it out
L2's QC result was entered on paper and not yet typed in
system_should: Never show one number alone. Show held, usable, and the reason for each µL that isn't usable. A tube with a negative balance is shown as a problem, not added as a negative to the total.
question_it_answers: How much do we have, and how much of it is usable?
cost_reason: Overcount means a run fails mid-plate; undercount means an expensive reorder
sim_hook: The question is hard after a sim day with mixed lots, a pending QC, one expiry passing midnight and one double-recorded transfer (p≈0.01 per transfer).

title: Why isn't this tube usable?
story:
Given tube T-0412 of Target X shows 40 µL held and 0 µL usable.
When a scientist scans it at the bench and asks why.
Then the system lists every reason that applies, not just the first one: lot L2 is on QC hold, and the tube was moved to the fridge four days ago so its shorter fridge shelf life ran out yesterday.
real_life_noise: the QC hold was lifted for L2 but the fridge expiry still blocks it
reasons conflict, e.g. lot released but this one tube quarantined after a spill
system_should: Return all blocking reasons with the date each started and who set it. If a reason is lifted, the remaining ones still show.
question_it_answers: Why can't I use this material?
cost_reason: People either use bad material or throw away good material because they can't see why
sim_hook: Generate tubes that hit two or three blocking rules at once (QC hold, storage-based expiry, quarantine).

title: What's left of a shared target from earlier experiments before we order more?
story:
Given Target X was bought for customer A's experiment in August and customer B's in September. After both, 9 aliquots remain in freezer F2 and a half-used stock tube sits in F4.
When the lab manager plans a new binding experiment that needs 600 µL of Target X.
Then the system shows 410 µL usable left from earlier experiments, split by lot and location, with each lot's QC status and freeze-thaw count, so the manager orders the 190 µL shortfall rather than a whole new lot.
real_life_noise: the half-used stock tube was thawed for experiment B and never logged back to the freezer
one aliquot is labelled for customer A and people treat it as reserved even though nothing in the system says so
two lots of Target X come from different suppliers and may not be interchangeable
system_should: Treat leftover target as shared stock, not as belonging to the experiment that used it last. Group by lot so the planner can decide whether mixing lots is acceptable. Flag tubes with an uncertain last location. Assumption: Adaptyv does not want to mix two target lots inside one experiment without a decision, so the answer is per lot, not one sum.
question_it_answers: What target is left from previous experiments?
cost_reason: Targets cost thousands per lot and take 5-10 days to arrive
sim_hook: Run two simulated binding experiments on the same target lot, then ask the question with one tube's location stale.

title: Experiment planning asks whether it can run next week's plates
story:
Given the planning system (a separate program) needs, for next Tuesday, 600 µL of Target X, 2 L of loading buffer and 6 BLI plates.
When it asks the inventory, through an API, for usable amounts as they will be on Tuesday.
Then the inventory answers with usable amounts that already exclude anything that expires before Tuesday (loading buffer lasts one week, so today's batch counts and last Friday's batch does not), and says how fresh the data is.
real_life_noise: the planner asks twice in a minute and gets different numbers because a split was recorded in between
loading buffer made today has not been entered yet
system_should: Answer "usable on date D", not just "usable now". Include the time of the latest recorded event so the planner knows what the number is based on. The inventory does not reserve anything; that stays in the planning system.
question_it_answers: Can the planned experiment run with what we have?
cost_reason: Planner books robot time and customer deadlines on these numbers
sim_hook: A planning agent queries for future dates while the scientist agent is mid-way through recording a buffer batch.

title: Numbers for a re-run after BLI data fails QC
story:
Given BLI run R-88 measured 96 customer proteins against Target X. Data review fails 12 wells (noisy curves).
When the person planning the re-run asks what is still available for exactly those 12 samples and that target.
Then the system shows, for each of the 12 samples, the leftover volume on the expression plate (if it is still within its 2-week life) or the DNA it came from, and how much usable Target X is left from the same lot used in R-88.
real_life_noise: the expression plate is 13 days old, so it's usable today but not on Thursday when the re-run is scheduled
the sample plate for R-88 was thrown away with protein in it, so the leftover there doesn't count
the robot log reports 10 µL drawn per well but the plate was actually overdrawn on three wells
system_should: Work per well, not per plate. For each failed sample give the closest usable source and how far back you'd have to go (sample plate, expression plate, DNA). Say when a source will expire relative to the planned re-run date. Prefer the same target lot as the original run and say so if it's gone.
question_it_answers: What do we have for re-running the wells that failed QC?
cost_reason: A re-run planned on a dead expression plate means re-expressing from DNA, which adds days
sim_hook: Data-review agent fails a random subset of wells (p≈0.1); plates age through the sim clock so some sources expire between the question and the re-run.

title: The same well fails QC twice
story:
Given sample S-17 failed data QC in run R-88 and again in its re-run R-93.
When the re-run planner asks for a third attempt.
Then the system shows S-17's full material history (both runs, both sample plate wells, the same expression well, the same DNA) so someone can see whether the problem is the material, not the measurement.
real_life_noise: re-run used a different target lot without anyone noting it
system_should: Make repeated failures on the same source visible. Show which inputs both failed attempts had in common.
question_it_answers: Is a repeated failure caused by the same material?
cost_reason: Re-running bad material wastes target and robot time
sim_hook: Seed a "bad expression well" that fails every time it is measured.

title: What expires in the next 14 days?
story:
Given loading buffer (1 week), other buffers (1 month), GFP stock (6 months frozen) and expression plates (2 weeks) are all in stock.
When the lab manager asks Monday morning what expires in the next 14 days.
Then the list is sorted by date, grouped by material, shows location and amount left, and leaves out containers that are already empty or discarded.
real_life_noise: a GFP stock was taken out of the freezer and left in the fridge, so its real expiry is much sooner than its label
a buffer has no expiry recorded because the maker forgot to enter the make date
system_should: Calculate expiry from how it was actually stored, not from the label. List items with unknown expiry in a separate "we can't tell" section rather than hiding them.
question_it_answers: What expires soon?
cost_reason: Expired buffer used in a run ruins the data; good buffer thrown out early wastes time
sim_hook: Storage-move agent leaves frozen items out (p≈0.02); buffer-maker agent skips the make date (p≈0.05).

title: What has already expired but is still on the shelf?
story:
Given 7 containers expired in the last month and nobody threw them out.
When a technician asks for a clean-up list.
Then the system lists them by location so one walk round the lab clears them, with amount left and whether the material was ever used in a run after it expired.
real_life_noise: one expired buffer was used in a run two days after expiry
system_should: Show expired-but-present separately from discarded. Flag any use after expiry and link to the run it went into.
question_it_answers: What expired material is still around, and was any of it used?
cost_reason: Expired material used silently undermines results sent to customers
sim_hook: Scientist agent picks the nearest tube without checking expiry (p≈0.03).

title: Where is this plate right now, and how sure are we?
story:
Given expression plate EP-221 was scanned into fridge R1 at 09:10, onto the bench at 11:30, and the robot read its barcode at 11:45. No scan since.
When a scientist asks where EP-221 is at 15:00.
Then the system says "last seen in the liquid handler at 11:45, by robot scan", and that nothing has confirmed it since. It does not claim it is in fridge R1.
real_life_noise: the plate was put back in R1 without a scan
a person scanned the shelf barcode but not the plate
system_should: Answer with the last known place, when, and how it was seen (person scan, robot read, or just assumed from the task). Note that "where is it" is always "where was it last seen".
question_it_answers: Where is it?
cost_reason: Time lost searching; a plate left at room temperature spoils
sim_hook: Mover agent skips the return scan (p≈0.15); question asked several hours later.

title: Find every tube of Target X across the lab, ordered by how easy it is to grab
story:
Given Target X is in 3 freezers, one box, and one tube is listed as being on the bench.
When a scientist needs one aliquot now.
Then the system lists usable tubes with freezer, shelf, box and box position, oldest usable first (or fewest freeze-thaws first, depending on the lab's rule), and puts the bench tube last with a warning that it may be thawed.
real_life_noise: two tubes claim the same box position A3
system_should: Show the full nested location. When two containers claim one slot, show both and flag it. Assumption: Adaptyv picks aliquots oldest-first; the order should be a setting.
question_it_answers: Which tube should I take, and where exactly is it?
cost_reason: Mostly lost minutes, sometimes an extra thaw
sim_hook: Box-filling agent puts two tubes in one slot (p≈0.01).

title: What hasn't been seen in 30 days?
story:
Given 23 containers have no scan, move or use for 30 days.
When the lab manager runs a monthly check.
Then the list shows them with last place, last action and who did it, so someone can go and check whether they still exist.
real_life_noise: long-term DNA freezer stock is untouched for months on purpose
system_should: Let material types set what "too long" means; untouched DNA in the freezer is normal, an untouched bench plate is not.
question_it_answers: What might be lost?
cost_reason: Ghost stock slowly inflates every count
sim_hook: Sim runs 60 days; some containers drop out of the agents' attention.

title: Bad target lot, find every plate, run and experiment it touched
story:
Given target lot L7 of Target X is found to be degraded three weeks after QC passed.
When QC asks what was made from L7.
Then the system walks forward: stock tube → 18 aliquots → 6 BLI target plates → 6 BLI runs → 4 experiments → 3 customers. It also lists which aliquots are still in the freezer so they can be quarantined.
real_life_noise: one aliquot was diluted into a working tube that was never registered, so the trail breaks there
a BLI target plate was prepared from two lots mixed in one well
a run was recorded against the wrong plate barcode and corrected the next day
system_should: Follow corrected records, not the original wrong ones, but mention the correction. Where the trail breaks, say so and name the last known point and who handled it, instead of reporting a clean list. Mixed-lot wells count as touched.
question_it_answers: If a batch of target is bad, what did it touch?
cost_reason: Wrong results go to customers, or good results get thrown out
sim_hook: Hard when the sim includes unregistered intermediate tubes (p≈0.02 per dilution) and one wrong-barcode correction on a run.

title: Which customers need to hear about the bad lot?
story:
Given the forward trace from ASK-012 lists 4 experiments.
When the customer-facing person asks who to contact and what to say.
Then the system gives customer, experiment, delivery date of results and which of their samples were measured against L7, so the message can be specific ("samples 3-40 of your August batch").
real_life_noise: one experiment's results haven't been delivered yet, so it's a re-run, not a notice
system_should: Separate results already delivered from results still in review. Assumption: the inventory knows which experiment and customer a run belongs to, from the planning system's IDs.
question_it_answers: Which customers were affected by a bad material?
cost_reason: Customer trust; telling the wrong customer is as bad as not telling the right one
sim_hook: Same as ASK-012, with some experiments still mid-workflow when the lot is flagged.

title: Trace a result back to the exact material
story:
Given a customer questions the binding result for their protein P-55.
When a scientist asks what exactly went into that measurement.
Then the system walks backward from the BLI run well: sample plate well → expression plate well → DNA plate well → DNA supplier lot and certificate; and on the other side, target plate well → aliquot → stock tube → target lot and its QC; plus the buffer lots used at each step.
real_life_noise: the robot transfer file had well B7 and C7 swapped and was corrected a day later
the buffer used was made from two component lots
system_should: Give the full tree with each step's time, operator or robot, and amount. Show where a step was corrected and what it said before.
question_it_answers: Where did this result's material come from?
cost_reason: Without it a disputed result can't be defended or explained
sim_hook: Robot agent swaps two wells in a transfer file (p≈0.005), corrected later by a scientist agent.

title: Which customer's protein is in well B7?
story:
Given a sample plate on the bench with a smudged label.
When a scientist scans it and asks what is in B7.
Then the system says the protein, its customer and experiment, how much was put there and when, and the DNA it came from.
real_life_noise: B7 was left empty on purpose (control) or holds buffer only
plate was rotated 180° on the robot deck, so B7 really holds G6's protein
system_should: Answer per well, and say clearly when a well is empty, a control or a blank. If a rotation or swap was recorded, apply it. Assumption: plate orientation errors are caught by people, not by the robot, so they show up as later corrections.
question_it_answers: What is in this well?
cost_reason: Results attached to the wrong customer protein
sim_hook: Robot agent places a plate rotated (p≈0.002); detected later by a review agent.

title: Who changed this tube's volume, and what did it say before?
story:
Given tube T-0099 shows 120 µL today. It was 200 µL on Monday.
When the lab manager asks what happened.
Then the history lists each entry: -50 µL by robot run R-90 on Tuesday, -40 µL by Ana on Wednesday, +10 µL correction by Ana on Thursday ("recorded 40, was 30"), each with when it happened at the bench and when it was typed in.
real_life_noise: two people recorded the same pipetting step
system_should: Never overwrite; show the old value next to the new one for every change. Corrections point to the entry they fix.
question_it_answers: Who changed what, when, and what did it say before?
cost_reason: Without history, mistakes can't be found or fixed fairly
sim_hook: Volume-entry agent mistypes (p≈0.02) and corrects a day later (p≈0.7 of mistakes).

title: What did we believe last Tuesday?
story:
Given on Tuesday at 17:00 the inventory said 300 µL usable Target X. On Thursday someone back-dated a Tuesday 14:00 split they had forgotten to enter, and on Friday a QC failure for one lot was entered.
When the lab manager asks "what did the system say on Tuesday at 17:00?" (to explain why an order wasn't placed).
Then the system can answer two different questions: what we believed at the time (300 µL), and what we now know was true at that time (180 µL). Both are kept.
real_life_noise: people say "as of Tuesday" meaning either one
system_should: Keep both the bench time and the typed-in time on every entry so both questions can be answered. Make the two answers clearly named so nobody confuses them.
question_it_answers: What did the record say on a past date?
cost_reason: Without it, blame and process fixes land in the wrong place
sim_hook: Agents delay entry by hours to days (log-normal delay); one QC result arrives after the fact.

title: Correction made five days later
story:
Given on the 1st a scientist recorded taking 50 µL from tube T-07. On the 6th they realise it was 15 µL.
When they correct it.
Then a new entry adds 35 µL back with a reason and a link to the original. Usable today goes up by 35 µL. Every report since the 1st shows the corrected amount from now on, and the old reports can still be reproduced.
real_life_noise: in between, someone used the "missing" 35 µL figure to justify ordering a new lot
the person deletes and re-enters instead of correcting
system_should: Corrections are new entries, never edits. Show which decisions or exports were made on the wrong number, where we can tell.
question_it_answers: What changed because of a late correction?
cost_reason: Silent rewrites make past decisions impossible to explain
sim_hook: Correction delay drawn from 0-10 days; some agents try a delete-and-redo instead of a correction.

title: Back-dated entry that would have made a balance negative
story:
Given tube T-12 had 100 µL. On Monday 80 µL was taken and recorded. On Wednesday someone back-dates a Sunday use of 40 µL.
When the Sunday entry is added.
Then, replayed in bench-time order, the tube went to 60 µL on Sunday and to -20 µL on Monday. The system accepts the fact but flags the tube: one of the two entries must be wrong, or the starting volume was.
real_life_noise: the back-dated entry has the date wrong by one day, not the volume
system_should: Re-check balances whenever a back-dated entry arrives. Flag impossible histories instead of refusing the entry or quietly clamping to zero. Answer "how much is left" with a warning until resolved.
question_it_answers: Is this tube's history even possible?
cost_reason: Impossible histories hide real losses or double-counting
sim_hook: Late-entry agent with date-picker error (p≈0.1 of late entries off by a day).

title: A record deleted by mistake
story:
Given a technician "deleted" the receipt record for target lot L9, thinking it was a duplicate. It wasn't; the other one was.
When the lab manager notices L9's tubes have no source.
Then the deleted record can be found, with who deleted it, when and why, and restored; nothing that pointed to it was lost.
real_life_noise: the real duplicate is still active, so restoring L9 without voiding the duplicate double-counts
system_should: Deleting means marking void with a reason, never removing rows. Restoring is another entry. Show the pair (restored L9, still-active duplicate) so someone voids the right one.
question_it_answers: What was deleted, by whom, and can we get it back?
cost_reason: A missing receipt breaks lineage for every tube of that lot
sim_hook: Receiving agent registers duplicates (p≈0.02); clean-up agent voids the wrong one of the pair (p≈0.3).

title: Physical count doesn't match the system
story:
Given the system says freezer F2 holds 40 tubes of Target X totalling 960 µL.
When a technician counts and finds 37 tubes, and estimates volume by eye on five of them.
Then the count is recorded as its own event: 3 tubes not found, 5 volume estimates. The system shows the gap tube by tube and does not change any quantity until someone decides.
real_life_noise: two "missing" tubes are actually in F3
eye estimates are rough (±5 µL) and shouldn't overwrite precise records
system_should: Keep counted values next to recorded values. Adjustments made after a count are their own entries, labelled as count adjustments, so loss from counts can be measured separately from loss in runs. Missing is a status, not a deletion.
question_it_answers: Where does our record disagree with the shelf?
cost_reason: Blindly trusting the count or the record both hide real problems
sim_hook: A count agent with its own error rate walks one freezer; earlier sim noise (moves without scans) creates real gaps.

title: How much did we lose in the last quarter, and on what?
story:
Given finance asks for the cost of material wasted in Q3.
When the lab manager asks the system.
Then it reports, by material and by cause: expired before use, discarded with material inside, failed QC lots, count adjustments (unexplained loss), and dead volume. Each line uses the purchase price per µL of that lot, or the made-in-house cost where we have one.
real_life_noise: some lots have no price recorded
in-house DNA and buffer cost is a rough estimate
system_should: Show amounts even where price is missing, and say how much of the total is unpriced. Keep cause categories distinct. Assumption: Adaptyv records purchase price per lot somewhere; if not, the inventory should at least hold a price field.
question_it_answers: What did waste cost us, and why?
cost_reason: Without causes, the lab can't decide what to fix
sim_hook: Run a 90-day sim with expiries, discards-with-volume and count losses; strip prices from 10% of lots.

title: Which operator or robot has the most discrepancies?
story:
Given the last two months of corrections, count adjustments and flagged impossible balances.
When the lab manager asks where mistakes come from.
Then the system groups them by who or what recorded the original entry (each person, each robot, each manual step), normalised by how many entries each made.
real_life_noise: one person works all the night shifts and does far more entries
a robot's errors are actually caused by a bad transfer file written by a person
system_should: Report rates, not raw counts. Attribute to the recorder and also to the task type, so a bad procedure isn't blamed on a person. This is for fixing process, not for blame; say that in the report.
question_it_answers: Where do our recording errors come from?
cost_reason: Wrong conclusions about people hurt the team more than help
sim_hook: Give sim agents different error rates and see if the report finds the noisy one.

title: How many times has this target lot been frozen and thawed?
story:
Given aliquot A-33 of Target X lot L1 was taken out three times for target plate prep.
When a scientist asks before using it a fourth time.
Then the system says 3 thaws for A-33, and also shows the stock tube's thaws before A-33 was split off (2), because those count too.
real_life_noise: a tube was taken out, not used, and put back without a scan
a freezer door left open; nobody knows if anything thawed
system_should: Count thaws from moves out of and back into cold storage, carried from parent to child. When a move wasn't scanned, say the count is a minimum ("at least 3"). Assumption: Adaptyv has a maximum thaw count per target, set per material.
question_it_answers: How many freeze-thaw cycles has this material had?
cost_reason: Over-thawed targets give weak binding signal that looks like a sample problem
sim_hook: Mover agent skips out/back scans (p≈0.1) so the count is uncertain.

title: Is this a reliable answer, or are there open problems underneath?
story:
Given usable Target X is 410 µL, but two tubes in it are flagged (one impossible balance, one unscanned move).
When any question returns a number.
Then it comes with "based on N containers, M of them have open flags", and the flagged amount separately.
real_life_noise: flags pile up and nobody closes them
system_should: Make uncertainty part of every answer instead of a separate report. Count how old open flags are.
question_it_answers: How much can I trust this number?
cost_reason: Hidden doubt is worse than stated doubt
sim_hook: Any long sim run; flags accumulate from every noise source.

title: Audit, show the full record of one lot from receipt to last use
story:
Given an auditor (or a customer's quality team) picks target lot L4.
When they ask for its full story.
Then the system shows receipt (supplier, certificate, date, who received), QC (method, result, who), every split and transfer, every location, every correction with old and new values, and disposal, in time order with typed-in times next to bench times.
real_life_noise: certificate of analysis was attached a week after receipt
one entry was made by a shared lab account
system_should: Produce this from the same entries as everything else, no separate audit table to keep in sync. Flag entries made by shared accounts as weaker.
question_it_answers: Can we prove what happened to this lot?
cost_reason: Failed audit or lost customer trust
sim_hook: Pick a random lot after a 60-day sim and render its history; add shared-account entries (p≈0.05).

title: Which results depend on a record that was later corrected?
story:
Given 9 corrections in the past month touched containers that later fed into runs.
When data review asks which delivered results are built on corrected records.
Then the system lists each run, the correction, and whether the correction changes what material went in (a swapped well) or only an amount.
real_life_noise: correction arrives after results were delivered
system_should: Distinguish corrections that change identity (which protein, which lot) from those that change only volume. Identity changes after delivery are urgent.
question_it_answers: Did a correction affect a result we already delivered?
cost_reason: A swapped-well correction means a wrong result is out with a customer
sim_hook: Well-swap errors corrected after the data-review step finishes.

title: How much buffer do we need to make this week?
story:
Given loading buffer lasts 1 week, and next week's planned runs need 3 L.
When the person making buffers asks how much usable loading buffer will still be good on each day of the week.
Then the system shows usable volume per day, falling as batches expire, and the component stock needed to make more (lot, amount, expiry of each component).
real_life_noise: one component lot expires before the buffer made from it would
system_should: A made buffer can't outlive its shortest-lived component; show the effective expiry. Assumption: buffer recipes are fixed per buffer type.
question_it_answers: Do we have enough fresh buffer and components?
cost_reason: Running out of loading buffer stops BLI runs that day
sim_hook: Component lots with mixed expiries; buffer maker sometimes uses the newest component lot instead of oldest.

title: Do we have enough consumables for next week?
story:
Given BLI plates, tips and chips have no expiry and are counted in units.
When the lab manager asks how many BLI chips are left.
Then the system gives units on the shelf, minus any boxes opened and known to be partly used, and when it was last counted.
real_life_noise: people take a handful of tips and never record it
system_should: Track consumables by box, not by tip. Say when the count is only as good as the last physical count. Per-tip tracking is cut (see journal).
question_it_answers: How many consumables do we have?
cost_reason: Running out of chips delays runs, but reordering is quick
sim_hook: Consumable use is only recorded at box level; boxes run out earlier than recorded (p≈0.2).

title: Which expression plates must be used before they spoil?
story:
Given expression plates last 2 weeks and 5 are in the fridge, each with leftover protein in some wells.
When the re-run planner asks which plates still hold protein that could be needed.
Then the system lists each plate with days left, how many wells still hold usable volume, and which of those wells belong to samples that failed data QC.
real_life_noise: an expression plate's start date is the end of the expression run, not the plate prep date, and people disagree which
system_should: Use one clear rule for when the 2-week clock starts and show it. Assumption: the clock starts when the expression run ends.
question_it_answers: What expiring material might we still need for re-runs?
cost_reason: Throwing away a plate a day too early forces re-expression from DNA
sim_hook: Data review runs late, so failed wells are only known a few days before the plate expires.

title: Can we re-express from DNA, and which DNA plate?
story:
Given protein P-55 needs re-running and its expression plate is gone.
When the planner asks for the DNA.
Then the system points to the reconstituted Twist plate well (and any diluted copy), with volume left and location, and says whether the original supplier plate still exists.
real_life_noise: the diluted DNA plate is the only one with that well left, and it's at a different concentration
system_should: Show every container holding that DNA, with concentration, not just volume.
question_it_answers: Where can we restart this sample from?
cost_reason: Reordering DNA costs 5-10 days and money if we miss a usable copy
sim_hook: Dilution step is optional in the sim (p≈0.5), so sometimes only diluted copies remain.

title: Two tubes scanned with the same barcode
story:
Given a reprinted label means two tubes in the lab carry barcode T-0555.
When someone scans T-0555 and asks what it is.
Then the system says this barcode currently points to more than one physical tube, shows both histories, and refuses to guess.
real_life_noise: the second tube was registered as "the same tube, moved"
system_should: Detect a container that is in two places at once, or moves faster than people walk, and flag it.
question_it_answers: Is this barcode trustworthy?
cost_reason: Two materials merged under one identity corrupts both lineages
sim_hook: Label printer agent reprints an existing barcode (p≈0.001); two agents scan it in different rooms within minutes.

title: What is sitting inside this instrument right now?
story:
Given the BLI instrument holds a target plate and two sample plates for a run that stopped halfway.
When a scientist asks what's inside before opening it.
Then the system lists the plates loaded, the run they belong to, and how far the run got according to the last recorded step.
real_life_noise: a plate from yesterday's run was never unloaded in the record
system_should: Treat an instrument as a place. Show anything "in" it for longer than a run takes as suspicious.
question_it_answers: What's in the robot?
cost_reason: Mostly confusion and lost time
sim_hook: Runs that abort mid-way (p≈0.02) and unload steps that aren't recorded.

title: How much of this run's inputs came from material that was later flagged?
story:
Given run R-101 used buffer lot B-12, which was later found contaminated, and target lot L1, which is fine.
When data review asks whether R-101 can be trusted.
Then the system lists every input lot of R-101 with its status now and its status at the time of the run.
real_life_noise: the buffer was flagged before the run but the flag was typed in after
system_should: Show both "status when used" and "status now", so a lot that was already bad at the time (but not yet recorded) is visible.
question_it_answers: Were any inputs to this run bad?
cost_reason: Results built on contaminated buffer go out to customers
sim_hook: Contamination event with delayed reporting.

title: Discarded container still counted as stock
story:
Given a BLI plate was thrown in the bin after the run, but the discard scan never happened.
When planning asks for usable sample plates.
Then the system should not offer a single-use BLI plate that has already been run, even without the discard scan, because the material type says those plates are thrown away after use.
real_life_noise: sometimes a plate is reused for a quick re-read
system_should: Use material rules (single use after a run) to mark things probably gone, and say "probably discarded, not confirmed".
question_it_answers: Is this plate really still around?
cost_reason: Plates already thrown away looking usable is exactly what the brief warns about
sim_hook: Discard scan skipped (p≈0.2) after BLI and GFP runs.

title: How much did one experiment consume, and what did it cost?
story:
Given customer B's experiment is finished.
When finance asks what material it used.
Then the system adds up every amount taken by runs tagged to that experiment, by lot and material, including its share of dead volume and failed re-runs, priced per lot.
real_life_noise: target aliquots used for two experiments on the same plate
a re-run was not tagged to the experiment
system_should: Split shared plates by well. Show untagged consumption that probably belongs to this experiment separately.
question_it_answers: What did this experiment cost in material?
cost_reason: Wrong pricing to customers
sim_hook: Plates shared between two experiments; experiment tag missing on re-runs (p≈0.1).

title: Which supplier's target lots fail QC most often?
story:
Given a year of target receipts from three suppliers.
When the lab manager reviews suppliers.
Then the system shows lots received, QC failures and lots later flagged bad, per supplier and per target.
real_life_noise: one supplier changed name after an acquisition
system_should: Keep QC outcomes on lots linked to supplier so this falls out for free.
question_it_answers: Which suppliers can we rely on?
cost_reason: Informs buying, not daily work
sim_hook: Suppliers with different QC failure rates.

title: The question we can't answer, and saying so
story:
Given an aliquot's parent was never registered (it was split from an unknown tube in a rush).
When someone asks which lot it is from.
Then the system says "lot unknown", lists what we do know (material, date first seen, who registered it) and does not guess the most likely lot. Its usable status is "blocked, unknown lot" until someone decides.
real_life_noise: only one lot of that target was ever in the lab, so the guess would probably be right
system_should: Allow an explicit "unknown" instead of forcing a guess at entry. Let someone link it later with a reason, which is a correction like any other.
question_it_answers: What happens when the record simply doesn't know?
cost_reason: A confident wrong lot is worse than an honest unknown during a bad-lot trace
sim_hook: Rushed-split agent skips parent scan (p≈0.01).

title: Results for one plate when the robot log and the person disagree
story:
Given the liquid handler log says it moved 10 µL into each of 96 wells; the scientist recorded a plate-level transfer of 1 mL total from a tube that had only 800 µL.
When someone asks how much protein is in each well.
Then the system keeps both records, prefers the robot log per well, and flags the 200 µL gap on the source tube.
real_life_noise: robot log is uploaded a day late
system_should: Say which source each number came from. Don't average them.
question_it_answers: Which record do we believe when two disagree?
cost_reason: Hidden disagreement turns into wrong usable numbers later
sim_hook: Robot log and manual entries generated independently with separate error rates.

title: Material that left the lab, where did it go?
story:
Given some leftover customer protein was shipped back to the customer and a target aliquot was sent to a partner lab.
When someone asks for the history.
Then the record ends with "left the lab" with where to, date and who sent it, and those amounts no longer count as held.
real_life_noise: the shipment was recorded as a discard
system_should: Keep "left the lab" distinct from "discarded", so cost and lineage reports stay honest.
question_it_answers: Where did material go when it left us?
cost_reason: Mostly a record-keeping issue, matters for customer questions
sim_hook: Shipping action, mis-recorded as discard (p≈0.1).

title: A late lineage edit makes a batch its own ancestor
story:
Given DNA lot D1 was used to make protein lot P1, which was used to make labelled lot P2.
When someone corrects D1's source to P2 after all three runs have been saved.
Then the proposed origin forms a circle, even though each individual link looks valid.
real_life_noise: The source picker shows short names and both lots are called stock.
The correction is dated before the first run to make the timeline look tidy.
A second person adds another source link while the first person saves.
Ordinary aliquot transfers within D1 already exist and must stay valid.
system_should: Reject a circle in ancestry between distinct lots, including one introduced by a correction or concurrent writes. Keep the rejected proposal available for review without making it active. Transfers that keep the same lot are movements, not new ancestry edges.
question_it_answers: Can a result trace back to a real starting material without looping forever?
cost_reason: A circular history makes source tracing unreliable
sim_hook: Create D1 -> P1 -> P2, then propose P2 -> D1 with an earlier bench time. Repeat with two simultaneous edits whose combined links form a circle. Assert no accepted ancestry cycle and no rejection of same-lot aliquoting.

title: A purchased batch is topped up with material made in-house
story:
Given a tube holds 200 µL of bought target lot B1 with a supplier certificate.
When a scientist adds 100 µL of the same target made in-house as lot H1 and calls it B1.
Then the 300 µL stock has two sources and cannot inherit B1's certificate as proof of the whole stock.
real_life_noise: The scientist sees the same protein name and thinks the lots are interchangeable.
The label still carries only the supplier's lot number.
H1 has not passed QC yet, while B1 has.
The top-up is entered as a second receipt to avoid creating a process run.
system_should: Keep each source lot's origin. Record the blend as a new derived lot with both contributions and pending review, or block mixing if the model does not support it. Do not let a bought-or-made flag erase one source or extend its certificate to the blend.
question_it_answers: Which part of this stock was bought and which part was made here?
cost_reason: Mixed stock can borrow QC and source claims it has not earned
sim_hook: Receive B1, make H1, then attempt a top-up under B1's identity. Assert both source contributions remain traceable and the blend is not released by B1's QC alone.

title: A tube moves inside a box inside a rack
story:
Given tube T1 sits in slot C4 of box B1, which sits in rack R1 in freezer F1.
When R1 moves to a trolley and then freezer F2 without individual tube scans.
Then T1's current location follows the rack while its slot and box stay the same.
real_life_noise: Someone removes T1 to the bench halfway through the rack move.
The rack destination scan reaches the server before the departure scan.
A cached tube screen still shows F1 and offers to save that location.
The trolley sits at room temperature for 40 minutes before anyone notices.
system_should: Derive location through containment at the requested time. Apply the rack move only to contents actually inside it then. Preserve the trolley interval for storage history and refuse a stale screen's silent location overwrite.
question_it_answers: Where is T1 now and how long was it outside the freezer?
cost_reason: Nested moves can hide both missing stock and warm exposure
sim_hook: Nest T1 in B1 in R1, remove T1 during the move, and deliver rack scans backwards. Assert location and exposure for T1 differ from those of tubes that stayed in R1.

title: One well contains two lots of the same target
story:
Given well A1 receives 20 µL from target lot L1 and 30 µL from target lot L2.
When 10 µL of the mixed well is used in a binding run and L2 later fails QC.
Then that run is exposed to L2 even though L1 supplied part of the well.
real_life_noise: Both source lots share a material name and look identical in a dropdown.
The second addition is uploaded as an edit of A1's lot field.
The robot reports only the total withdrawal, not the amount from each source.
The well was not mixed properly, so equal composition cannot be assumed without a stated rule.
system_should: Preserve both inputs through a blend lot or explicit contents model. Trace the withdrawal to both sources. State any mixing assumption before estimating proportions; retain exposure links even when exact fractions are unknown. Do not force a single source lot onto the well.
question_it_answers: Which runs may contain material from L2?
cost_reason: A single lot field can hide a contaminated contribution
sim_hook: Add L1 and L2 to A1, withdraw 10 µL, then fail L2. Assert the destination run appears in the exposure query with both sources retained.

title: QC fails three wells of a plate
story:
Given a 96-well plate contains separately tracked samples and all wells await QC.
When QC passes 93 wells and fails B3, C7 and H12.
Then the failed wells remain present but unusable while the other 93 can be released.
real_life_noise: The QC file names wells as B03 while the plate screen uses B3.
An empty row for D4 means no result, not a pass.
The operator also clicks a plate-wide pass button.
B3 was copied to another plate before the result arrived.
system_should: Attach results to the tested contents and wells, normalize well addresses, and distinguish missing results from passes. Detect the conflicting plate-wide release. Trace B3's descendants and show reasons for each blocked well without blocking unrelated wells by accident.
question_it_answers: Which wells can run and which copied samples need review?
cost_reason: Plate-wide status can release failed samples or waste good ones
sim_hook: Load 96 wells, copy B3, import 92 passes, three failures and one blank, then submit a plate-wide pass. Assert per-well states and a review flag on B3's copy.

title: Powder becomes solution and concentration is measured later
story:
Given 2 mg of a target powder is received and reconstituted to a final volume of 1 mL.
When QC later measures 1.7 mg/mL and 100 µL has already been consumed.
Then the system must separate the measured concentration from the recorded volume and original powder mass.
real_life_noise: The scientist enters 1 mL of added solvent, not final solution volume.
A dilution factor of ten is applied twice in the instrument export.
The concentration result arrives after the withdrawal and has an uncertainty range.
Another screen tries to add the powder's mg to the solution's µL.
system_should: Record reconstitution as a process with mass input and solution output. Keep concentration as a scoped measurement with units, method and time. Convert only with valid supporting measurements and expose assumptions. Do not rewrite past volume withdrawals or add incompatible dimensions.
question_it_answers: How much solution remains and what mass estimate can we support?
cost_reason: Unsupported conversions can overstate available target
sim_hook: Reconstitute powder, withdraw 100 µL, then import a late concentration result and a duplicate dilution factor. Assert volume remains 900 µL and invalid or ambiguous conversions are flagged.

title: A correction is corrected and the first correction is retried
story:
Given a withdrawal was recorded as 50 µL but should have been 5 µL.
When a correction changes it to 5, a second correction changes it to 8, and the first correction is resent.
Then the effective withdrawal is 8 µL, with all three accepted versions visible in history.
real_life_noise: A scientist types a replacement amount while an import job sends a signed adjustment.
The second correction points to the first correction, not the original event.
The first screen retries after a timeout with the same request identifier.
Someone attempts another correction from the now stale 5 µL version.
system_should: Define whether corrections replace a fact or add a delta and validate that meaning. Link the correction chain, apply each request once, and detect edits based on superseded versions. Keep both current balance and what was believed after each accepted correction queryable.
question_it_answers: What is the true withdrawal and how did our account of it change?
cost_reason: Reversing a correction twice creates stock that never existed
sim_hook: Save 50, replace with 5, replace with 8, retry the 5 request, then submit a stale edit. Assert one effective 8 µL withdrawal and distinct historical answers at each recording time.

title: Yesterday's source transfer arrives after today's withdrawal
story:
Given tube T1 appears empty in the server's record this morning.
When a 20 µL withdrawal is reported before yesterday's offline 100 µL fill arrives.
Then the current account can settle at 80 µL without pretending the server knew about the fill earlier.
real_life_noise: Both events carry the same second because the scanner has low clock precision.
The fill references a source that has not synced yet either.
A back-dated second withdrawal would make yesterday's balance negative.
The dashboard already alerted someone that T1 was empty.
system_should: Hold unresolved dependencies for reconciliation. Keep bench time and recording time distinct, with explicit ordering or ambiguity when times tie. Recheck affected historical balances when late events arrive; do not silently publish an impossible history or erase the earlier dashboard state.
question_it_answers: What was available yesterday and what did we know this morning?
cost_reason: Late events can repair today's total while breaking past balances
sim_hook: Deliver withdrawal, fill and source receipt in reverse order, then add a conflicting back-dated debit. Assert dependency resolution, historical balance checks and recording-time queries.

title: Two people withdraw from the last 50 microlitres
story:
Given T1 has 50 µL and two scientists each read that balance.
When each records a 30 µL withdrawal at the same time.
Then both writes cannot be accepted as ordinary valid withdrawals against that balance.
real_life_noise: Both people have already pipetted before pressing save.
One request times out and is retried.
A volume correction lands between the two writes.
Each person blames the other and enters the old balance again.
system_should: Check the balance and save the debit as one protected operation. Reject or hold the conflicting write for reconciliation without losing the report of what physically happened. Never turn a stale balance edit into a stock credit. Keep both people and request identities in the audit trail.
question_it_answers: Can two accepted writes spend the same material twice?
cost_reason: Concurrent writes can show usable stock after it is exhausted
sim_hook: Start two 30 µL debits against one 50 µL version behind a barrier. Retry one request. Assert no duplicate debit, no unflagged negative balance and a retained conflict report.

title: An offline scanner brings back an old location
story:
Given a scanner goes offline with T1 listed in freezer F1.
When it records T1 on the bench at 10:00, an online user records T1 in F2 at 11:00, and the scanner syncs at 16:00.
Then the late sync adds the bench interval without moving T1 back from F2.
real_life_noise: The scanner clock is 12 minutes slow.
The user presses upload twice after the progress bar freezes.
Another offline move has no destination scan.
A barcode was scanned from a printed worksheet rather than the physical tube.
system_should: Keep device event identities, device time and server receipt time. Apply known causal order rather than last upload wins. Flag uncertain clock order or incomplete moves and retain the last supported location with its uncertainty. Do not count retries as extra movements.
question_it_answers: Where is T1 and how certain is that location after offline work?
cost_reason: A late upload can hide a tube or erase a warm interval
sim_hook: Queue a 10:00 offline move, save an 11:00 online move, then upload the queue twice with clock skew. Assert deduplication and either F2 or an explicit ordering conflict, never a silent return to the bench.

title: Two physical tubes carry the same barcode
story:
Given an old printer reuses barcode 004271 for a new tube while the original tube still exists.
When a scientist scans that code to consume 10 µL.
Then the system cannot safely choose a tube from the barcode alone.
real_life_noise: The tubes hold different targets and are stored in different buildings.
One import strips leading zeroes and another keeps them.
A supplier label happens to match the lab's internal code.
The old tube was marked missing, not destroyed.
system_should: Give containers stable internal identities separate from labels. Define barcode namespaces and normalization rules. Flag collisions and require disambiguation or relabelling before accepting a scan-driven change; do not merge histories or assume missing means the old code is free.
question_it_answers: Which physical object did this scan identify?
cost_reason: Barcode collisions attach consumption and QC to the wrong material
sim_hook: Register colliding internal and supplier labels plus a leading-zero variant. Scan the ambiguous label and assert no quantity change occurs until a specific container is resolved.

title: A split creates more liquid than the parent held
story:
Given a parent tube holds 500 µL.
When a split claims twenty children of 26 µL and 10 µL left in the parent, with no diluent input.
Then the proposed 530 µL account is impossible as a simple split.
real_life_noise: The robot log reports commanded volume rather than delivered volume.
The first ten children were already saved before the second upload failed.
Someone marks the parent empty to hide the mismatch.
Another operator records 20 µL of dead-volume loss against the same run.
system_should: Check the whole run, including all children, leftover and losses, in compatible units. Keep partial evidence but do not publish unsupported output as usable. Distinguish a split from a dilution with real additional inputs and use explicit measurement tolerances rather than an arbitrary allowance.
question_it_answers: Did this run create unsupported stock?
cost_reason: Per-transfer checks alone can miss an overdrawn parent
sim_hook: Submit the split in two batches with leftover and loss entries. Assert the completed run cannot release 520 µL of children from a 500 µL input without a valid additional source.

title: A customer returns a previously shipped tube
story:
Given 100 µL left the lab for a customer and was removed from available stock.
When the customer returns 60 µL in the same tube after a week.
Then the lab holds returned material whose custody and storage are uncertain.
real_life_noise: The customer says it stayed frozen but supplies no temperature record.
The original barcode is covered by the customer's label.
The returned tube looks unopened despite the lower reported volume.
Receiving enters it as a new purchase with the old supplier certificate.
system_should: Record the return as a new custody event linked to the shipment and original contents when supported. Reconcile the amount independently and place the return on hold pending the stated release checks. Do not undo the shipment, double-count the old stock or inherit usable status automatically.
question_it_answers: What came back and is any of it safe to offer for use?
cost_reason: Returned material can carry unknown exposure or contamination
sim_hook: Ship 100 µL, return 60 µL under a changed label, then retry receiving. Assert one held return linked to the outbound history and no automatic QC pass.

title: A failed lot passes a later QC test
story:
Given target lot L1 failed QC and its remaining tubes were put on hold.
When a second test passes after the first test is found to have used a faulty control.
Then release needs an explicit decision about which result is invalid and which contents the new test covers.
real_life_noise: The new test uses a different assay and acceptance threshold.
Only one of five tubes is sampled after a thaw.
The first failure already triggered a review of downstream experiments.
A person enters the pass with a bench time earlier than the failure.
system_should: Keep both results and a reasoned release decision with scope and authority. Do not make latest recorded pass win by default. Re-evaluate remaining stock separately from old experiment reviews; releasing stock must not erase the failure or silently close those reviews.
question_it_answers: Why is L1 usable now despite its earlier failure?
cost_reason: A new pass can conceal a real failure or clear unrelated tubes
sim_hook: Fail L1, open downstream reviews, then import a scoped pass with an earlier bench time. Assert release requires a recorded decision and old reviews remain visible.

title: A freezer excursion shortens expiry after aliquots have moved
story:
Given lot L1 normally lasts years frozen and some tubes spend six hours in a warming freezer.
When the excursion is discovered two days later and a rule gives affected stock only 24 hours after exposure.
Then affected remaining stock is already expired and withdrawals since that deadline need review.
real_life_noise: One box left the freezer before the warming began.
Two aliquots were made during the excursion and moved to another freezer.
The sensor has a missing hour and reports in a different time zone.
A later return to cold storage is mistaken for a fresh shelf-life start.
system_should: Determine exposure from historical containment and location, carry relevant exposure into aliquots, and retain uncertainty where readings are missing. Shorten expiry without resetting age on cooling. Keep when the lab learned this separate from when the revised deadline applies and flag affected past uses.
question_it_answers: Which tubes expired early and which runs used them after that point?
cost_reason: A freezer incident can invalidate stock that already moved elsewhere
sim_hook: Generate a nested freezer stay, an early departure and a mid-excursion split. Report the excursion two days late. Assert scoped expiry and review links for later uses.

title: A disposed tube is found alive in the wrong bin
story:
Given T1 was recorded as discarded with 40 µL still inside.
When it is found sealed in a reusable-tube bin the next morning.
Then the disposal record was wrong, but the tube's contents and storage still need checking.
real_life_noise: The disposal entry was made by scanning a whole box.
Someone already reordered the target because T1 disappeared from usable stock.
A scientist adds a new receipt to bring the 40 µL back.
The bin sat on a warm bench overnight and the label is partly torn.
system_should: Correct the specific disposal without manufacturing a second receipt or deleting its audit history. Restore physical presence only after identifying the tube, reconcile quantity, and hold it for storage and contamination review. Undoing disposal alone must not restore usable status.
question_it_answers: Is the found tube the same stock and what prevents its reuse?
cost_reason: A disposal reversal can double-count stock or release damaged material
sim_hook: Dispose T1, submit both a found-tube correction and a fresh receipt, then add overnight warm exposure. Assert one physical holding with a linked correction and explicit hold reasons.

title: A new enzyme is sold in activity units
story:
Given a new enzyme type arrives as 5,000 activity units and a small molecule arrives labelled only as 10 mM.
When a user asks to consume 2 µL of each.
Then neither request can be converted to the recorded stock quantity without more information.
real_life_noise: The enzyme's activity depends on the assay conditions printed in its certificate.
A vendor uses U while another uses mU.
The small molecule has a concentration but no recorded solution volume.
The type editor offers volume as a default and silently fills in 1 mL.
system_should: Allow new type rules and units with explicit dimensions. Store activity with its assay definition and concentration separately from amount. Require missing conversion evidence or keep quantity unknown and blocked for that request. Never treat molarity as total stock or infer activity from volume alone.
question_it_answers: Can we support this requested amount in a unit we actually know?
cost_reason: A flexible type table still fails if every amount assumes volume
sim_hook: Add activity-based and concentration-only types without changing schema. Attempt µL debits before and after supplying valid conversion measurements. Assert unsupported conversions are refused and missing amount stays unknown.

title: The clock shows the same local time twice
story:
Given a London scanner records a tube leaving at 01:50 BST on 25 October 2026.
When it records the return at 01:10 GMT after the clocks go back.
Then the tube spent 20 minutes outside, although the local return time looks earlier.
real_life_noise: The scanner export omits the UTC offset from both rows.
A server in another time zone supplies the receipt timestamp.
An imported spring event uses 01:30 on a London date when that local time did not exist.
A user fixes the apparent negative interval by swapping the events.
system_should: Store unambiguous instants and retain the supplied zone or offset. Flag ambiguous or nonexistent local times for resolution instead of guessing. Use elapsed instants for exposure calculations and recording instants for audit order; do not repair times by sorting their display strings.
question_it_answers: How long was the tube warm across a daylight-saving change?
cost_reason: Time ambiguity can turn a real exposure into zero or a negative interval
sim_hook: Submit the two offset-bearing events and assert a 20-minute interval. Repeat with bare local times and a nonexistent spring time; assert explicit time-resolution errors.

title: The instrument consumes target but sends no result
story:
Given an instrument starts a run with a 200 µL target tube.
When its computer crashes after pipetting and no completion file is produced.
Then the absence of a result does not prove that no target was used.
real_life_noise: The operator restarts the same run with the same tube.
Pump priming consumed liquid before the first recorded transfer.
A late log contains commanded moves but no delivery confirmation.
The tube cannot be weighed accurately enough to settle the exact loss.
system_should: Track run progress and confirmed versus uncertain consumption. Put affected quantity on hold or show a conservative supported bound until reconciliation; do not advertise the full starting amount as usable. A retry is a separate physical attempt even when it shares the experiment name.
question_it_answers: What can we safely claim remains after an unreported run?
cost_reason: Missing files can make consumed target appear available again
sim_hook: Start a run, confirm some withdrawals, crash before completion and launch a second attempt. Assert missing reports never refund confirmed consumption and unresolved loss appears in availability reasons.

title: A user account is deleted after making corrections
story:
Given a scientist received lots, corrected volumes and approved QC over several months.
When their login account is deleted after they leave.
Then inventory facts and their attribution must remain interpretable.
real_life_noise: The identity provider removes the profile rather than merely disabling login.
A new scientist later receives the same email address.
One change was made by a robot acting on the departing scientist's request.
An old import used a display name with no account identifier.
system_should: Separate the audit actor from the live login account and keep a stable historical reference. Preserve human and service attribution where known, mark unresolved legacy actors honestly, and never cascade-delete inventory events. Email reuse must not transfer authorship to the new person.
question_it_answers: Who made this change after their login no longer exists?
cost_reason: Account cleanup can erase or misattribute the audit trail
sim_hook: Save changes under a stable actor, delete the linked login and create another login with the same email. Assert event counts and original actor references survive unchanged.

title: Two valid-looking moves make boxes contain each other
story:
Given boxes B1 and B2 are separate and can each hold smaller containers.
When one user puts B1 inside B2 while another puts B2 inside B1.
Then the combined containment history has no physical meaning.
real_life_noise: Each user checked the old location before either move was saved.
A spreadsheet import also tries to put a box inside itself.
A late move creates a circle only for an interval last Tuesday.
Two tubes are assigned to the same exclusive slot in B1 during the repair.
system_should: Enforce one parent per container at any instant, no containment circles, and exclusive slot occupancy where slots hold one object. Check concurrent moves together and recheck intervals touched by late edits. Location queries must stop with a clear data error if legacy data contains a loop.
question_it_answers: Does every container have a physically possible location at this time?
cost_reason: Broken containment corrupts every location and exposure query below it
sim_hook: Race the two inverse moves, attempt self-containment, then insert an overlapping historical move and slot collision. Assert no accepted containment cycle or double occupancy.

title: A robot stops halfway through a plate transfer
story:
Given a robot plans 96 transfers of 10 µL into a new plate.
When it stops after 40 completed transfers, with the forty-first delivery uncertain.
Then the source and destination records must reflect partial physical work.
real_life_noise: The application saved all 96 planned outputs before starting.
The robot picked up the forty-first volume but may have dropped it into waste.
The operator resumes from well 40 instead of well 42.
The final file says failed without listing which movements completed.
system_should: Separate planned movements from executed facts and track completion per transfer. Keep confirmed debits and credits even when the run fails. Hold uncertain source and destination amounts for reconciliation, and identify each resume attempt so overlapping transfers cannot silently duplicate outputs.
question_it_answers: Which wells actually contain material after a failed run?
cost_reason: All-or-nothing run status can invent wells or refund real consumption
sim_hook: Plan 96 transfers, confirm 40, leave one pickup unresolved and resume with an overlapping well. Assert only confirmed contents are released and the overlap requires reconciliation.

title: An import retry looks like another physical transfer
story:
Given a robot's transfer file has already debited 10 µL from T1 and credited well A1.
When the same file is uploaded again after a network timeout.
Then it must not move another 10 µL in the inventory.
real_life_noise: The second upload has a different filename and upload identifier.
The robot restarts its local event counter at one each day.
A real repeat run uses the same plate layout and transfer amounts.
A revised file reuses the original movement identifier but changes 10 to 12 µL.
system_should: Identify physical actions using a stable source, run attempt and action identifier. Deduplicate identical retries, flag conflicting payloads under one identity, and retain import history. Do not deduplicate genuine repeat work merely because its values match; changed amounts need an explicit correction.
question_it_answers: Was this material moved twice or was the same report received twice?
cost_reason: Retry handling can double consumption or erase a real repeat run
sim_hook: Upload identical actions under renamed files, repeat them under a new physical attempt, then reuse one identity with changed volume. Assert one posting per action and a conflict for the changed payload.

title: A source lot is corrected after its children have been used
story:
Given a run says child C1 came from lot L1 and C1 has already fed two experiments.
When a bench photo proves the source was actually L2.
Then current ancestry and affected-experiment queries must change without erasing the old account.
real_life_noise: L1 and L2 have the same material name and different QC states.
Correcting the source would overdraw L2's recorded balance.
A scientist already exported a recall list based on L1.
Someone proposes moving the child balance instead of correcting the original transfer.
system_should: Correct source attribution and its quantity effects together, checking the newly affected source. Recompute descendant exposure and usability, retain the earlier recording-time answer, and flag changed review lists. If quantities cannot reconcile, keep the physical-source evidence and an explicit unresolved balance rather than silently accepting or losing it.
question_it_answers: Which experiments are affected after we discover the wrong source was recorded?
cost_reason: Correcting a label alone can leave balances and recall paths wrong
sim_hook: Use C1 downstream, replace its L1 source with insufficient-balance L2, and query before and after the correction's recording time. Assert updated exposure, retained history and a visible balance conflict.

title: Different suppliers reuse the same lot number
story:
Given two suppliers both send a target labelled lot 2026-10.
When receiving imports their certificates and later receives another shipment of the first supplier's lot.
Then equal printed lot numbers must not merge the suppliers or create stock twice.
real_life_noise: The suppliers sell the same target under different catalogue numbers.
The second shipment is a real additional quantity, not a duplicate delivery.
One supplier's certificate is revised without changing its lot number.
A distributor's lot number differs from the original manufacturer's number.
system_should: Separate internal lot identity, external lot references, delivery identity and certificate versions. Use enough supplier and product context to resolve an external reference, and preserve manufacturer and distributor links when known. Additional receipts can add quantity to an existing lot; retrying one receipt cannot.
question_it_answers: Which supplier batch and certificate apply to this exact stock?
cost_reason: Lot-name collisions can spread the wrong QC or certificate across stock
