sim_hook: Receive equal lot strings from two suppliers, add a second delivery from one and retry the first delivery. Assert two lot identities, three physical receipts and retained certificate versions.

title: A material type rule changes after stock has been used
story:
Given loading buffer has a seven-day shelf life and a batch made ten days ago was used on day six.
When a new rule shortens shelf life to three days.
Then the model must say whether the rule applies only to new batches or also to old stock.
real_life_noise: The editor changes a single row that all batches reference.
The new rule is entered today but applies from last Monday.
A label printed under the old rule still says seven days.
The change is later narrowed to one formulation of loading buffer.
system_should: Version rules and record their scope, effective time and recording time. Require an explicit choice about existing stock, then recompute affected availability and past-use reviews accordingly. Keep the original rule and old query results explainable; a type-row edit must not silently rewrite history.
question_it_answers: Under which shelf-life rule was this batch released and used?
cost_reason: Mutable rules make historical usability impossible to reproduce
sim_hook: Create and consume a buffer under rule v1, add prospective and retrospective v2 changes, then narrow their scope. Assert the two application choices produce distinct, reproducible availability histories.

title: A QC pass and contamination hold arrive together
story:
Given lot L1 is awaiting release after a purity test.
When one person approves purity while another reports suspected contamination in tube T3.
Then the purity pass must not clear the independent contamination hold.
real_life_noise: Both screens offer a single status dropdown with passed as an option.
The contamination report applies only to T3, not every tube of L1.
The pass reaches the server last despite happening first.
A supervisor resolves the purity review but has not seen the contamination report.
system_should: Keep independent checks and holds with their own scope and resolution. Derive usability from all applicable reasons. Detect concurrent attempts to resolve the same hold, and never let a general pass or later upload clear an unrelated unresolved restriction.
question_it_answers: Which exact reason still blocks T3 after the purity pass?
cost_reason: One status field can lose an independent safety restriction
sim_hook: Race a lot purity pass against a tube contamination hold, then resolve only purity. Assert T3 stays blocked for contamination while unaffected released tubes remain usable.

title: A found tube has unknown quantity rather than zero quantity
story:
Given a labelled tube is found in a freezer with visible liquid but no amount in the old spreadsheet.
When it is imported and someone asks for the total target available.
Then its unknown quantity must not be presented as either zero stock or a usable estimated amount.
real_life_noise: The spreadsheet has a blank, a dash and the text enough in different quantity cells.
Tube capacity is 1.5 mL and is mistaken for fill volume.
An operator guesses 100 µL without measuring it.
A later weighing provides a range rather than an exact volume.
system_should: Track physical presence separately from quantified contents. Distinguish unknown, estimated, measured and zero amounts. Show the known usable total with a separate count of unquantified holdings and their reasons; do not let an empty numeric cell become zero or capacity become stock.
question_it_answers: How much do we know we have and what stock still needs measuring?
cost_reason: False precision leads to needless orders or unsupported experiments
sim_hook: Import blank and text quantities for found tubes, then add an estimate and a measured range. Assert presence survives and exact totals never silently include capacity or guessed quantities.

title: Evaporation changes volume without removing the same fraction of protein
story:
Given a well contains 100 µL of target solution at 1 mg/mL.
When it sits uncovered and a later check finds 80 µL with the target retained.
Then a 20 µL loss does not necessarily mean a 20 percent loss of target mass.
real_life_noise: The scientist chooses a generic consumption action for the missing liquid.
The well is also near the pipette's minimum recoverable volume.
A concentration reading suggests evaporation but adsorption to plastic remains possible.
The cover-off interval is reported only after the plate has been diluted again.
system_should: Distinguish evaporation, consumption and unexplained measurement differences. Track relevant measurements and uncertainty by dimension. Do not scale mass or concentration automatically from a volume adjustment without a supported assumption, and carry uncertainty into later dilution calculations and usability reasons.
question_it_answers: What amount and concentration can we support after liquid loss?
cost_reason: A correct liquid balance can still give a wrong assay concentration
sim_hook: Record an uncovered interval and an 80 µL measurement, then dilute the well. Compare known-solvent-loss and unexplained-loss cases; assert no unsupported proportional mass debit or exact concentration claim.

title: A single-use chip returns with unused capacity
story:
Given a pack of ten chips is counted as consumable stock.
When one chip is opened, used for one sample and put back with unused channels.
Then the nine sealed chips are usable but the used chip is not a fresh tenth chip.
real_life_noise: The instrument reports one used channel rather than one used chip.
An operator credits the chip back because the run failed QC.
The barcode identifies the pack, not the individual chip.
The pack's material type has no expiry, so the screen assumes everything is usable.
system_should: Separate count-based consumption from reusable capacity and enforce the chip's single-use rule. A failed experiment does not undo opening or use. Keep the used item present if it is still in the lab, but exclude it from sealed stock; avoid claiming per-chip identity where none was recorded.
question_it_answers: How many fresh chips remain after a failed run?
cost_reason: Unused channels and no expiry can make a spent consumable look fresh
sim_hook: Open one of ten chips, consume one channel, fail the run and attempt a return credit. Assert nine fresh chips and a spent item or count with no automatic refund.

title: Passing one assay does not qualify material for every use
story:
Given target L1 passes identity QC and is suitable for one binding method.
When another method requires an activity test that L1 has never passed.
Then the same physical stock has different supported uses.
real_life_noise: The certificate says passed without naming the method in its summary.
A lot-wide usable flag is copied onto every child tube.
The activity threshold changes with the requested assay.
A caller asks only for usable quantity without supplying a purpose.
system_should: Retain what each QC test established and which release rule it satisfies. State the default meaning of usable and expose missing qualifications separately. Allow inventory callers to inspect supported use conditions without taking on experiment planning; a general pass must not imply untested capabilities.
question_it_answers: For which uses is this quantity actually qualified?
cost_reason: One usable flag can promise material for an unsupported assay
sim_hook: Pass identity and method-A checks but leave method-B activity untested. Query release evidence for both methods and without a purpose. Assert the missing qualification remains explicit.

title: A whole box is discarded after one tube was removed
story:
Given box B1 originally contains ten tubes, and T1 leaves for the bench at 09:00.
When B1 is discarded at 10:00 and T1's move is synced at noon.
Then the disposal applies to nine tubes rather than the stale list of ten.
real_life_noise: The disposal screen saved a snapshot of yesterday's contents.
Someone tries to return the disposed empty box to a freezer slot.
A tenth tube was added at 09:30 without appearing in that snapshot.
The disposal correction arrives before the late movement it depends on.
system_should: Resolve disposal scope against the best supported containment at the disposal time. Keep the originally recorded scope and explicit revisions, including unresolved conflicts. Re-evaluate late departures and arrivals without silently restoring discarded descendants or making a disposed parent usable through a location move.
question_it_answers: Exactly which contents were destroyed with the box?
cost_reason: Stale containment can erase surviving tubes and retain discarded ones
sim_hook: Queue T1's departure, add another tube, discard B1 from a stale snapshot and deliver the queued events out of order. Assert corrected disposal membership and an auditable original scope.

title: A bad batch reaches a result through a shared buffer
story:
Given suspect component lot C1 is used in buffer B1, which is used in diluting DNA, expressing protein and preparing target wells.
When C1 is recalled after several results are delivered.
Then the affected-results query must follow every relevant input path, not only the main protein lineage.
real_life_noise: The buffer appears in robot logs as a reagent rather than a sample source.
The same buffer touches several branches that meet again in one experiment.
One plate is washed, but there is no validated claim that this removes the risk.
Some stock and results have already left the lab.
system_should: Link material inputs and physical contacts at the level the model supports, distinguishing ancestry from exposure where useful. Traverse all recorded paths, deduplicate affected outputs and retain external endpoints. Do not drop an input because it contributed little mass or assume washing clears an untested risk.
question_it_answers: Which stock and delivered results may have been exposed to C1?
cost_reason: Main-source-only lineage misses shared reagent failures
sim_hook: Fan C1 through buffer into three workflow branches that reconverge, then recall it. Assert every recorded descendant or exposed result appears once, including shipped outputs.

title: An empty tube is refilled with a different lot
story:
Given barcoded tube T1 once held lot L1 and was recorded empty.
When a scientist refills it with L2 and a late L1 QC result arrives.
Then the old result must not attach to the new contents merely because the barcode matches.
real_life_noise: The tube was never washed and a small residue may remain.
The old label still names L1.
A delayed instrument file identifies only T1, not the contents at sampling time.
The tube was empty on paper but still had an unknown dead volume.
system_should: Either forbid reuse for this container type or track separate periods of contents with preparation and contamination checks. Bind measurements and transfers to the contents sampled at the relevant time. Treat leftover residue as a mixing or uncertainty problem; a new fill must not inherit old QC by container identity.
question_it_answers: Which contents did this late result actually test?
cost_reason: A stable barcode can wrongly carry QC across unrelated contents
sim_hook: Empty T1, attempt an L2 refill, then import an L1 result with the old sampling time. Assert reuse policy and contents history prevent L2 from receiving L1's pass.

title: Two different proteins share a name and stock unit
story:
Given two target variants are both displayed as Target X and held in µL.
When a dashboard totals stock by name.
Then it must not offer the combined quantity as interchangeable material.
real_life_noise: One variant has a sequence mutation and the other has a different purification tag.
An import drops the suffix that distinguished the variants.
Their concentrations differ by a factor of ten.
A scientist renames one material to correct a spelling error after months of use.
system_should: Use stable material identities and define which properties distinguish variants. Keep aliases and display-name changes separate from identity changes. Aggregate only quantities with compatible meaning and show concentration or variant differences that prevent substitution; correcting a name must not merge materials.
question_it_answers: How much of the exact requested target do we have?
cost_reason: Name-based totals can send the wrong protein into a run
sim_hook: Create same-name variants with different concentrations, import a truncated name and rename one identity. Assert separate stock totals and no automatic material merge.

title: Repeated tiny transfers gain or lose stock through rounding
story:
Given a source contains 100 µL and a robot makes one thousand transfers of 0.1 µL.
When reports alternate between 0.1 µL and 100 nL.
Then the supported total is 100 µL, without rounding each transfer to zero or inventing a small leftover.

title: Stock expires while nobody writes a new event
story:
Given a released tube expires at 12:00 UTC and a dashboard last refreshed at 11:59.

system_should: Define deadline boundaries and how date-only expiry is interpreted. Evaluate usability at an explicit requested instant and expire cached answers at time boundaries. title: A location correction changes yesterday's storage exposure
story:
